description:

2027 Clinical Pharmacology Internship Overview
Envision spending your summer working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie Interns.
AbbVie’s Clinical Pharmacology (ClinPharm) organization provides critical scientific support for all phases of pharmaceutical research and development in all divisions of the business. ClinPharm leads the design, execution, and interpretation of all clinical pharmacology Phase 1 studies, and exposure-clinical response modeling and simulation to optimize dose selection and trial design. The team also integrates data from multiple sources including preclinical and clinical pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, dosing compliance/adherence, effective and toxic exposures, financial metrics, and overall cost/benefit. Another key responsibility of the team is to present the data to regulatory authorities world-wide and authors more than half of the clinical summary documents for global regulatory submissions.
Internship projects could vary and are dependent on therapeutic area needs. Current therapeutic areas supported include Immunology, Oncology, Neurology, and Specialty assets.
Key project responsibilities include:
Analysis of literature and in-house proprietary data
Dose- and Exposure- Safety & Efficacy Endpoint Analysis
Database analyses
Development of mathematical models (e.g. PK/PD, Population PK, etc.)
Conducting simulations using mathematical models
Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD)
Clinical study design
Presentation to the broader team at the conclusion of the assignment
Publication of authorized analyses
Minimum Qualifications
Currently enrolled in university, pursuing a PharmD or PhD in Pharmacokinetics, Pharmaceutics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Clinical Pharmacology, or other related field
Must be returning to university for at least one semester following the internship
Preferred Qualifications
Expected graduation date between December 2027 – June 2028
Experience analyzing scientific literature and data, including database and dose- or exposure-response (safety and efficacy) analyses
Familiarity with developing and running mathematical models and simulations (e.g., PK/PD, Population PK), ideally in a Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD) context
Understanding of clinical study design

Independently plan and perform routine tasks competently within a timely fashion and generate precise, reliable and consistent results.

Analyze and critique results, noting significant deviations from the expected results.
Troubleshoot experiments and instrumentation.
Learn and understand new experimental techniques with a curiosity to apply them for unique project / assignment requirements.
Demonstrate skill in multiple techniques and appropriately modify protocols, as required, to suit the changing needs of research or development sciences.
Place data in proper scientific context by consulting and citing relevant literature.
Demonstrate technical proficiency in their field, preferentially in the analytical areas of quantitative and instrumental analysis.
Raises the bar and is never satisfied with the status quo.
Impact projects predominantly through lab and/or pilot plant based activities.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, and GxP compliance, where applicable.
Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, or equivalent education, with typically 3 or more years’ experience or Master’s Degree or equivalent education (no additional experience).
Theoretical and practical knowledge (in chromatography and / or spectroscopy is highly preferred) to carry out job function.
Builds strong relationships with peers and cross functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.

Knowledgeable on multiple technologies and systems that support CSOC and CSIRT services (e.g., SOAR, SIEM, IPS/IDS, EDR, etc.)

title: Business Solutions Engineer
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Works as a business-facing, hands-on technical lead who partners directly with internal customers to understand business outcomes, workflows, pain points, data needs, and solution requirements and rapidly translate them into secure, scalable, and supportable technology solutions. Combines senior business systems analysis with software and solution engineering to independently shape, prototype, configure, integrate, test, and, when appropriate, build AI-enabled and conventional applications or partner with other teams for medium to larger scale builds. Partners closely with BTS colleagues, including Business Solutions Consultants (BSCs), Business Relationship Managers (BRMs), and BTS Compliance, as well as technical vendor partners, and owns the transition of new application builds to BTS support, including operational readiness and success metrics. Uses forward-deployed and iterative development practices to remain close to users, validate requirements through working software, and continuously refine solutions in partnership with business stakeholders and technical teams. Applies practical knowledge of generative AI, agentic AI, automation, data, APIs, cloud services, and enterprise platforms while adhering to architecture, security, privacy, quality, compliance, and software lifecycle standards.
Responsibilities:
Partner directly with business stakeholders and Business Technology Solutions (BTS) colleagues to understand business objectives, end-to-end workflows, pain points, decision points, data needs, user experience expectations, and measurable outcomes.
Lead structured discovery and requirements activities; translate ambiguous needs into process models, epics, features, detailed user stories, acceptance criteria, functional requirements, non-functional requirements, data requirements, integration requirements, and traceability documentation.
Use rapid prototyping, AI-assisted analysis, agentic AI, workflow automation, and other fit-for-purpose tools to validate assumptions, clarify requirements, demonstrate solution concepts, and shorten feedback cycles with users.
Develop solution options and technical designs covering application components, AI or agent workflows, data flows, APIs and integrations, identity and access, security, privacy, observability, deployment, support, and lifecycle considerations. Evaluate build, buy, configure, and reuse options.
Personally configure, prototype, code, integrate, test, and troubleshoot applications or solution components when hands-on development is the most effective delivery approach. Produce maintainable, documented work products that can advance to production.
Coordinate across software engineering, data, AI/ML, architecture, platform, infrastructure, cybersecurity, privacy, quality, compliance, testing, and support teams to resolve dependencies and move solutions from concept through implementation and adoption.
Maintain a prioritized backlog and iterate continuously with business partners through demonstrations, usability feedback, testing, and release learning. Balance speed with technical quality, risk, scalability, and user value.
Define and execute testing approaches, including functional, integration, regression, user acceptance, AI evaluation, and production-readiness testing. Verify that delivered capabilities satisfy requirements and intended business outcomes.
Collaborate routinely with BTS Business Solutions Consultants (BSCs), Business Relationship Managers (BRMs), and BTS Compliance to align demand, priorities, solution direction, and compliance obligations, and engage technical vendor partners to scope, guide, and review their contributions.
Plan and lead the transition of new application builds to BTS support, including support handoff, runbooks, knowledge transfer, training, service-level expectations, monitoring and alerting, incident, and problem management, and hypercare.
Define how each launched application will be operationalized, including ownership, release and change management, access management, enhancement intake, lifecycle and retirement planning, and ongoing support and cost considerations.
Define success metrics and KPIs with business partners (e.g., adoption, usage, performance, reliability, quality, AI output accuracy, user satisfaction, and business value); instrument solutions to measure them, monitor results after launch, and drive improvements when targets are not met.
Create and maintain required business, functional, technical, and operational documentation, including architecture and design artifacts, interface specifications, decision records, test evidence, support procedures, and training materials.
Provide technical leadership within assigned initiatives, guide less-experienced contributors, communicate risks and trade-offs clearly, and independently escalate material architecture, responsible AI, security, privacy, compliance, quality, or delivery concerns.
Required:
Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Data Science, or a related discipline plus 5 years of relevant experience; or a Master's Degree plus 4 years of relevant experience.
Demonstrated experience in a hybrid role spanning business systems analysis, solution engineering, software development, technical consulting, product delivery, or similar disciplines.
Proven ability to lead business discovery sessions and convert complex or ambiguous needs into user stories, acceptance criteria, functional and non-functional requirements, process and data models, and implementable technical designs.
Hands-on experience building or configuring applications, integrations, automations, or data-enabled solutions using modern development languages, APIs, cloud services, low-code platforms, or enterprise application platforms.
Practical knowledge of generative AI and agentic AI concepts, including large language models, prompt and context engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, tool use, agent orchestration, evaluation, guardrails, human-in-the-loop controls, and limitations of AI-generated outputs.
Understanding of software engineering and delivery practices, including Agile product development, source control, testing, CI/CD, observability, production support, secure development, documentation, and software lifecycle controls.
Experience working with cross-functional technical teams and translating effectively between business stakeholders, engineers, architects, data specialists, security, privacy, quality, and compliance partners.
Experience transitioning applications or solutions to a support organization and operationalizing them after launch, including ITSM practices, support models, monitoring, and operational readiness.
Ability to define, instrument, and track KPIs and performance metrics, and to use them to evaluate whether a system meets business needs and to guide continuous improvement.
Experience working with technical vendors and partners, including shaping requirements, reviewing deliverables, and holding them accountable to quality and compliance standards.
Strong analytical, facilitation, communication, and relationship-management skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts, solution options, risks, and trade-offs to non-technical audiences.
Ability to work with a high degree of independence, manage multiple priorities, make sound technical recommendations, and deliver results through influence in a matrixed environment.
Preferred:
Experience with GxP, validation, responsible AI, data privacy, or regulated software delivery.
Life sciences and pharmaceutical industry experience, including familiarity with regulated environments and how technology supports drug discovery and development.
R&D operations experience, including supporting scientific and clinical research workflows, systems, and business processes.
R&D contracting lifecycle processes, procurement, and vendor management experience.
Finance experience, including budgeting, forecasting, invoicing, and financial systems and controls relevant to R&D and technology initiatives.

This is a technical role responsible for executing the design, building, testing, and implementation of security systems across our environment, with a specific emphasis on endpoint security and mobility. You will work closely with other members of the Information Security team to identify potential threats and vulnerabilities and develop strategies and solutions to mitigate these risks, securing the end-user device estate and the mobile platforms through which the enterprise increasingly operates, and contributing to our overall information security strategy.
You will join the Business Technology Solutions (BTS) Information Security and Risk Management (ISRM) Architecture organization. Our team translates business objectives and cyber risk strategy into concrete security measures — processes, technologies, and services — across a diverse and complex infrastructure landscape, including on-premises, cloud, and X-as-a-Service models.
Responsibilities:
Define and evaluate security architecture for the end-user device estate — workstation and laptop hardening, EDR/endpoint protection (e.g., CrowdStrike, Defender), data protection, and configuration baselines.
Advise on mobility security: MDM/UEM (e.g., Microsoft Intune), mobile application management, conditional access, and BYOD posture across iOS and Android.
Perform Security Architecture Reviews — adjudicate submissions, align the risk and controls with the system owner, and ensure review quality.

Identify and communicate current and emerging security threats and risks; design security architecture elements and propose new or revised measures to mitigate them as they emerge.
Help develop solutions that balance information security needs with the needs of the business, in collaboration with team members and business and IT stakeholders.
Be fluent with AI concepts and incorporate AI into your daily workflows — using AI to accelerate design reviews, threat modeling, documentation, and analysis — targeting improved efficiency, quality, and speed.

Support training and mentorship of more junior employees as well as employees outside the Information Security Team, as needed.

Advanced knowledge of operating systems, networking protocols, systems administration, and security technologies.
Advanced knowledge and application of cybersecurity terminology and concepts, and foundational understanding of the cyber threat landscape and attack vectors.

The Clinical Data Strategy and Operations (CDSO) DMO Lead or Clinical Data Scientist (CDS) serves as the data management domain expert and key strategic partner to the clinical study team. This role owns the data collection strategy, drives implementation, oversees data quality delivery, and supports on-time achievement of key study milestones. As the Data Operations single point of contact for cross-functional stakeholders, the DMO Lead or CDS applies strong project management, risk oversight, and continuous process optimization to enable data quality, inspection readiness, and successful trial delivery.
Responsibilities:
Serves as the CDSO data management subject matter expert and single point of contact for assigned studies, owning data collection, data cleaning, and database lock strategies to enable high-quality, inspection-ready study delivery.
Leads risk-based and continuous data review strategies from study start-up through database lock, leveraging centralized monitoring, statistical review, and clinical data science methodologies to proactively identify and mitigate study risks.
Triages data quality standards across studies to identify trends, drive site-level actions through effective cross-functional communication, and maintain data currency in support of timely, reliable study decisions.
Interprets clinical and operational data, quality metrics, predictive signals, and dashboard outputs to develop data-driven recommendations that strengthen study execution, risk management, patient safety oversight, and quality across the clinical development lifecycle.
Contributes to defining, managing, and monitoring data-driven protocol deviations.
Defines and manages study data flow and triages issues from raw EDC data through mapped SDTM data, partnering with internal technology teams, service providers, and vendors to drive timely mitigation and support end-to-end data integrity.
Performs data mining and custom analytics, gathers business requirements for study dashboards, and generates operational metrics that support study decisions.

The Franchise Lead is the single accountable Business Technology Solutions (BTS) partner for a dedicated commercial franchise, a senior technology executive who sits at the intersection of commercial strategy and technology enablement, ensuring every technology and data investment directly accelerates brand performance, patient access, and commercial growth.
Serving as a trusted advisor to franchise VPs, Senior Directors, and IBT leads across Market Access & Patient Services (MAPS) and Sales & Marketing, this individual is the connective tissue between business ambition and technology execution, translating commercial priorities into a cohesive, forward-looking technology roadmap. This role owns the full BTS investment portfolio end-to-end: from strategic prioritization and business case development through delivery oversight and ROI validation, coordinating execution across shared services platforms and data teams’ enterprise wide.
As a strategic anchor for the META Business Unit, this leader navigates complex external environments to drive priorities that position the organization toward industry leadership. Most critically, this role eliminates technical friction across the patient journey, from Awareness to Adherence, ensuring that platforms spanning Consumer Marketing, MAPS, and HCP Sales & Marketing operate as one integrated ecosystem. In an era defined by omnichannel execution, connected data, and intelligent automation, this role is where brand strategy becomes technology reality.
Responsibilities:
Business-BTS Strategic Alignment: Act as the primary BTS point of contact for Therapeutic Brand Leads and commercial support function leaders, building trusted, advisory-level relationships with VPs and Senior Directors across MAPS, and Sales & Marketing to ensure the franchise BTS strategy is fully aligned to and enabling commercial brand objectives.
Strategic Commercial Pillar Support: Own and drive the franchise BTS roadmap across the three core commercial pillars, MAPS, and Sales & Marketing, with a clear mandate to eliminate technical friction across the E2E Patient journey.

Strategic Outcome & Value Management: Define Business Requirements (BRDs) and high-level success criteria for all franchise technology initiatives, establishing the strategic foundation for functional scoping, solution design, and delivery. Mentorship. Act as an M&A subject matter expert and mentor for other team members.
Due Diligence. Act as the primary point of contact for due diligence efforts, and the representative of Commercial BTS within the broader BTS community of M&A practitioners.
Bachelor’s Degree with 10 years of relevant experience; Master’s Degree with 9 years of experience; PhD with 5 years of experience.
Respective years of progressive experience in solution or enterprise architecture, with at least 3–5 years in a senior leadership or people management role.
Proven track record of architecting and delivering complex, cross-platform technology solutions in a large, matrixed organization, preferably within pharmaceutical, biotech, or life sciences.
Demonstrated experience with feasibility assessment, solution trade-off analysis, and architecture decision-making at scale.
Prior experience managing a cross-platform solution portfolio and leading teams of 4 or more direct reports, including coordination with Technical Product Owners.
Skills & Experience
Strategic Business Partnership & Executive Influence: Proven ability to build trusted advisory relationships with VPs and Senior Directors, translating complex technology concepts into clear business language and aligning diverse stakeholders around a shared technology vision with commercial rigor.
Commercial Domain Expertise: Deep understanding of pharmaceutical commercial operations across Patient Services, Market Access, and Sales & Marketing, with the ability to connect technology strategy directly to brand performance and patient access outcomes.

At AbbVie, partnership accelerates innovation and helps deliver transformative medicines to patients faster. As Director, Global Alliances, Neuroscience , you will shape and manage strategic external collaborations from discovery through commercialization, with primary responsibility for AbbVie’s Neuroscience partnerships. AbbVie is the industry leader in neuroscience by sales, with a broad and growing portfolio spanning neurodegeneration, psychiatry, neuroinflammation, migraine, and other strategic priorities.
You will lead complex, high-value alliances that advance AbbVie’s neuroscience pipeline and marketed portfolio. As the bridge between AbbVie and its partners, you will foster transparency, strategic alignment, and a shared vision for success across therapeutic areas including neurodegeneration, psychiatry, neuroinflammation, migraine, movement disorders, and other AbbVie neuroscience priorities. You will anticipate challenges, resolve issues, and create the conditions for collaboration that drive scientific and business impact.
You will lead strategic business reviews at key contractual decision points and deliver clear, data-driven recommendations to senior leadership. When needed, you will help negotiate amendments or restructure existing alliances to improve performance and long-term value. You will also support due diligence and business development by assessing, structuring, and negotiating partnership opportunities that strengthen AbbVie’s global pipeline and enterprise strategy.
This role is ideal for a strategic, proactive, and forward-looking relationship builder who thrives at the intersection of science, business, and collaboration and is motivated to make a meaningful impact on patients worldwide.
Major Responsibilities:
Lead Neuroscience Alliances: Advance AbbVie’s neuroscience strategy by aligning AbbVie and its partners around a shared vision, effective governance, and seamless execution across discovery, development, and commercialization. Support alliances across neurodegeneration, psychiatry, neuroinflammation, migraine, movement disorders, and other AbbVie neuroscience priorities. Build trusted relationships and foster joint problem-solving.
Lead Strategic Reviews and Governance: Manage governance forums, including Joint Steering Committees, guide data-informed decisions, assess alliance performance, and recommend actions at key contractual inflection points. Advocate for AbbVie’s alliances, resolve conflicts, and strengthen partner relationships through cross-functional collaboration.
Serve as a Strategic Advisor: Provide forward-looking insights on alliance health, opportunities, and risks to help leadership make data-driven, value-maximizing portfolio decisions.
Support Business Development and Due Diligence: Collaborate with Search and Evaluation and Business Development to evaluate, structure, and negotiate new collaborations. Support due diligence and alliance launch planning to ensure strategic fit, governance readiness, and effective transition to Global Alliances. Represent AbbVie at corporate partnering events to strengthen relationships with current and prospective partners.
Optimize Partnerships: Implement and refine processes, tools, and communication frameworks that improve transparency, consistency, and operational excellence.
Promote Excellence and a Partnering Culture: Establish best-in-class alliance practices and represent AbbVie as a partner of choice in the global biopharma community.
This is a hybrid role requiring at least three (3) days onsite in the AbbVie North Chicago, IL headquarters office. This role requires up to 25% travel, both domestically and internationally.
Experience: At least five years of experience in pharmaceutical development, commercialization, alliance management, corporate ventures, or business development. Requires a strong understanding of drug research, development, and commercialization; experience with scientific, regulatory, development, and commercial concepts across early- and late-stage programs; and familiarity with legal agreements and contractual governance.
Education: Advanced scientific, legal, or business degree (PharmD, PhD, MD, JD, MBA, or equivalent) strongly preferred.
Strategic and Business Acumen: Demonstrated analytical thinking in conflict resolution, risk management, and organizational alignment, with the ability to develop and present strategic proposals that improve business outcomes. Experience in strategic analysis, business development, or consulting, with the ability to translate enterprise strategy into execution.
Communication and Influence: Exceptional communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills, with a proven ability to align and influence vice president- and executive-level stakeholders in complex, cross-functional environments.
Proactive Leadership: Self-starter who anticipates challenges, drives progress independently, and navigates ambiguity with sound judgment and creativity.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Demonstrated success in matrixed, global organizations, influencing without authority and delivering results across diverse teams.

This is a rare opportunity to help shape the future of neuroscience at AbbVie, the industry leader in neuroscience by sales. You will work with visionary leaders, leading-edge science, and trusted partners worldwide to deliver meaningful impact for patients living with serious neurological and psychiatric conditions. Join a high-profile team that thrives on collaboration, strategy, and results, and help define the future of Global Alliances across neurodegeneration, psychiatry, neuroinflammation, migraine, movement disorders, and other AbbVie neuroscience priorities.

Establish, maintain and deploy global engineering standards, technical practices and governance expectations for biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy process engineering strategy, process platform deployment, process package design, technical assurance, manufacturing technology interfaces and project delivery.
Drive consistent application of technical standards, design principles, lessons learned and engineering playbooks across regions, sites and capital projects.
Define enterprise standards, engineering requirements and technical guardrails for new biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy technologies, including requirements for consistent design, deployment, qualification, operation and scale-up across Strategic Investments.
Ensure discipline strategies support AbbVie’s long-range Strategic Investment objectives, strategic investment programs and adoption of new technologies across future manufacturing platforms.
Provide governance and escalation for technical decisions with material safety, quality, compliance, cost, schedule, operability or lifecycle impact.

Partner with Strategic Investments and project leadership to ensure technical assumptions, deliverables, risks and resource needs are integrated into capital program plans.
Apply Strategic Investment lessons learned and standards to improve project quality, speed, reliability and readiness across the portfolio.

Drive timely resolution of technical issues and ensure suitable escalation when decisions have broader project, network or business impact.

Build technical capability through coaching, mentoring, standards governance, knowledge management and cross-functional collaboration.

Network needs, site readiness, operability, maintainability, startup, handover and operational performance support.

Compliance expectations, validation strategy, qualification readiness, safety, risk review and inspection readiness interfaces.

Cross-discipline technical integration, standards, design reviews, technical issue resolution and lessons learned.

Strong communication, risk management, technical judgment, stakeholder engagement and structured problem-solving skills.

Project execution support
Stakeholder management
Vendor / partner technical coordination
GMP and regulated manufacturing awareness
Operational readiness and handover support

Matrix leadership and influence without direct authority

title: Non-Human Identity and Cloud IAM – Platform Lead
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. This position is part of AbbVie's Information Security & Risk Management (ISRM) team within Business Technology Solutions. The Identity & Access Management (IAM) team is responsible for the development, implementation, and oversight of the organization's IAM strategy, ensuring secure, efficient, and compliant access to systems and data. The NHI and Cloud IAM function addresses one of the fastest-growing attack surfaces in enterprise security—machine identities now outnumber human ones, and the rapid expansion of AI agents is accelerating that trend. This role does not own the AI agent or cloud platforms themselves—those are owned by partner teams across BTS—but it is the IAM team's authoritative voice on how those platforms must integrate with identity governance, and it is accountable for ensuring that no non-human identity operates outside of AbbVie's visibility or control.
Take the next step in your career with an organization that strategically invests in the long-term health of the company, its technology and its people. The AbbVie Business Technology Solutions (BTS) team shapes the digital transformation necessary for our treatments to positively impact patients' lives. In the role of Non-Human Identity and Cloud IAM – Platform Lead, you'll tackle one of the most complex and rapidly evolving challenges in enterprise security: establishing a unified strategy for non-human identities, AI agent governance, and cloud IAM—bridging today's fragmented landscape into a coherent, observable, and future-ready program. This is a senior, highly technical role that requires both architectural depth and the organizational influence to drive accountability across the teams that own AI, agentic, and cloud platforms—ensuring that every non-human identity is visible, governed, and secured from AbbVie's IAM systems.
In this role, you'll be responsible for:
Define and drive the enterprise Non-Human Identity (NHI) strategy—rapidly assessing all in-flight initiatives across the organization, rationalizing overlapping efforts, and establishing a centralized, authoritative governance program covering all machine identities across on-premises, cloud, and agentic environments
Build and maintain a comprehensive NHI registry encompassing service accounts, APIs, bots, application identities, robotic process automation (RPA), and AI agents—ensuring every non-human identity is discovered, inventoried, classified, and continuously governed within IAM systems
Own AbbVie's identity governance posture for AI agents: while the creation and operation of AI agent platforms is owned by other teams, this role is accountable for ensuring those platforms integrate with IAM—so that every AI agent is inventoried in the NHI registry, mapped to its owning human or system identity, governed through appropriate access controls, and visible for security monitoring
Proactively discover and identify new AI agents and agentic workloads as they are introduced across the enterprise; partner with AI platform, cloud, and business teams to ensure timely onboarding into the NHI governance framework, and drive remediations or mappings where gaps exist
Serve as the IAM point of accountability for all agent-related identity questions: defining standards for how agents authenticate, what credentials they use, how those credentials are secured, and how agent activity is observable from an identity and access perspective
Establish centralized NHI observability by driving integration between IAM platforms and external systems—including AWS, Azure, GCP, and agentic platforms (e.g., Microsoft Copilot ecosystem, AWS Bedrock, or similar)—so that IAM maintains a living, authoritative view of all non-human identities regardless of where they originate
Design and implement modern NHI credential security controls including just-in-time (JIT) access, dynamic secrets, short-lived certificates, automated credential rotation, and runtime authentication—reducing standing privilege for machine identities to near zero where possible
Assess the current tooling landscape for NHI and cloud IAM; determine whether existing platforms can be extended or reconfigured, or whether new capabilities are needed; and build a pragmatic, phased modernization roadmap
Own and evolve the Cloud IAM and IGA strategy, closing the integration gap between cloud-native identity platforms (AWS IAM, Azure Entra ID, GCP IAM) and AbbVie's central IAM/IGA tools—ensuring cloud identities, entitlements, and access certifications are governed consistently and automatically
Design cloud identity governance frameworks including role-based access models, entitlement management, access certifications, and least-privilege enforcement across cloud environments
Drive cross-functional alignment across IAM, AI Platform, Cloud, Security Architecture, Compliance, Audit, and business teams—translating complex, fast-moving requirements into executable roadmap priorities and holding partner teams accountable for IAM integration commitments
Establish KPIs and maturity metrics for the NHI and Cloud IAM program, providing executive-level visibility into inventory completeness, risk posture, program progress, and open gaps
Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements (SOX, GDPR, PCI-DSS) for machine identities and cloud access controls; respond to and remediate audit findings
Manage budget, resources, and vendor relationships for all NHI and Cloud IAM technologies and solutions
Lead and mentor a team of technical specialists, cultivating a culture of proactive governance, automation, and continuous improvement
Bachelor's degree with 8 years experience OR 7 years of experience OR PhD with 3 years experience
Hands-on experience with non-human identity management, cloud IAM, or machine identity governance in large enterprise environments
Demonstrated experience establishing or maturing NHI programs—including service accounts, API credentials, application identities, and/or automated/agentic workloads
Strong hands-on expertise with cloud IAM frameworks: AWS IAM, Azure Entra ID, and/or GCP IAM, including integration with central IGA platforms
Experience designing and implementing cloud IGA processes: entitlement management, access certifications, role-based access models, and least-privilege enforcement in cloud environments
Proven experience with secrets management platforms and modern credential security patterns (JIT access, short-lived certificates, dynamic secrets, automated rotation)
Architecture-level understanding of identity federation, service-to-service authentication, and cloud-native identity patterns (OAuth, OIDC, SAML, workload identity)
Strong track record of driving complex, cross-functional programs in matrixed organizations—including influencing and holding accountable teams that are not direct reports
Demonstrated ability to proactively identify governance gaps, drive partner teams to remediate, and establish scalable, automated processes to prevent recurrence
Excellent communication and executive presentation skills, with the ability to translate deeply technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders and build alignment across organizational boundaries
Beneficial:
Familiarity with AI agent platforms and their identity/credential patterns (e.g., Microsoft Copilot ecosystem, AWS Bedrock agents, or similar agentic frameworks)
Experience building NHI discovery and inventory capabilities, including integration with platforms not originally designed for identity governance
Familiarity with containerization and Kubernetes service account management
Hands-on experience with IGA platforms and their cloud connectors (Saviynt, SailPoint, or equivalent)
Scripting and automation experience (PowerShell, Python, Terraform, or other IaC tools)
Knowledge of certificate management, PKI infrastructure, and API security platforms
Understanding of CIS, NIST, and other cloud security compliance frameworks
Industry certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, AWS/Azure/GCP security certifications, or equivalent
Experience in the pharmaceutical or life sciences industry
Tools and skills you will use in this role:
Cloud IAM platforms: AWS IAM, Azure Entra ID, GCP IAM — and their integration with enterprise IGA
Secrets management platforms: HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, or equivalent
IGA platforms with cloud connectors: Saviynt, SailPoint, or equivalent
NHI discovery, inventory, and governance tooling
Just-in-time access, dynamic secrets, and runtime authentication frameworks
Integration APIs and connectors for agentic platforms (e.g., Microsoft Copilot ecosystem, AWS Bedrock) — for identity inventory and observability, not platform ownership
Service-to-service authentication protocols: OAuth, OIDC, SAML, workload identity federation
Containerization and Kubernetes service account management
CI/CD pipeline integrations for identity and secrets (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, Terraform)
Scripting and automation: PowerShell, Python, Infrastructure as Code
Certificate management and PKI
Audit and compliance reporting for cloud and NHI controls
Strong architectural thinking, cross-functional influence, and executive communication skills

Drive consistent application of technical standards, design principles, lessons learned and engineering playbooks across regions, sites and capital projects.
Define enterprise standards, engineering requirements and technical guardrails for new biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy technologies, including requirements for consistent design, deployment, qualification, operation and scale-up across Strategic Investments.

Provide governance and escalation for technical decisions with material safety, quality, compliance, cost, schedule, operability or lifecycle impact.

Partner with Strategic Investments and project leadership to ensure technical assumptions, deliverables, risks and resource needs are integrated into capital program plans.
Apply Strategic Investment lessons learned and standards to improve project quality, speed, reliability and readiness across the portfolio.

Coordinate technical input from project teams, site SMEs, external engineering partners, vendors and cross-functional stakeholders.

Network needs, site readiness, operability, maintainability, startup, handover and operational performance support.

Compliance expectations, validation strategy, qualification readiness, safety, risk review and inspection readiness interfaces.

Cross-discipline technical integration, standards, design reviews, technical issue resolution and lessons learned.

Experience supporting biologics drug substance, cell therapy, gene therapy, viral vector, mRNA, sterile biologics or similarly regulated biopharmaceutical manufacturing environments preferred.
Demonstrated ability to work across global functions, manufacturing sites, project teams, suppliers, vendors and external engineering partners.
Strong communication, risk management, technical judgment, stakeholder engagement and structured problem-solving skills.

Biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy process design and process package review

Biologics and CGT technology transfer, platform deployment and manufacturing scale-up

Engineering governance and standards

GMP and regulated manufacturing awareness
Operational readiness and handover support

Matrix leadership and influence without direct authority

Identify opportunities to simplify or automate recurring reporting, notifications, workflow activities, and operational follow-up.

Ensure Change Management documentation remains aligned with current ServiceNow workflows, approval models, governance requirements, and operating practices.
Develop communications, guidance, and training materials supporting process changes and recurring change-quality needs.

Hands-on experience with ServiceNow Change Management, including workflows, approvals, Standard Changes, reporting, dashboards, and change lifecycle management.

Position Description:
This Senior Scientist – Solid State Characterization position will be in a technical specialty group - Physical Analytical Chemistry (PAC) withing Analytical R&D.  The PAC group is a global team of experienced and innovative scientists which utilize a diverse set of physical analytical tools to advance CMC development programs by providing insights and driving the understanding of materials, processes, and products.  Additionally, the group contributes to development and justification of control strategies and authors relevant sections of regulatory submissions across all development phases.
We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. Perform quantitative phase analysis: Quantify polymorphic and amorphous content in DS and DP using Rietveld, whole-pattern, and multivariate approaches, addressing low drug load, excipient interference, preferred orientation, and micro absorption.
Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.
Conduct orthogonal solid-state characterization including X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis, moisture sorption, microscopy, spectroscopy as applicable for solid form, impurity and stability studies

Represent PAC on CMC teams, lead form-change investigations, mentor scientists, and implement new diffraction technologies.

Position Summary
AbbVie is seeking a Senior Principal Engineer, Clean Utilities to serve as a global technical authority for the design, delivery and performance of clean utility systems supporting our worldwide manufacturing network. You will lead Clean Utilities engineering for complex brownfield expansions and greenfield facilities, set technical direction, develop global standard designs, and guide projects from feasibility through commissioning, qualification and handover. Working with Global Engineering, Strategic Investments, manufacturing sites, Quality, EHS, Validation/CQV and external engineering partners, you will deliver technically robust, compliant and business-aligned solutions that help improve capacity, reliability and efficiency in a regulated, patient-focused environment.
Global Engineering Context
Global Engineering provides engineering leadership, technical governance, standards development and project execution support across AbbVie’s global manufacturing network and strategic investment portfolio.
The organization supports greenfield manufacturing facilities, new technology platform deployments, brownfield expansions, modernization programs, debottlenecking initiatives, lifecycle asset replacement, infrastructure upgrades and capacity expansion investments.
Global Engineering roles are expected to promote common standards, transfer lessons learned across regions and sites, and enable consistent engineering delivery across strategic capital investments.
Key Responsibilities
Global Technical Execution Support
Lead Clean Utilities workstreams for complex brownfield and greenfield capital projects from feasibility and front-end planning through BOD design stage of the project. Provide technical support during detailed design, construction, commissioning, qualification, startup, and handover.
Develop, maintain and deploy standard designs and philophies associated with generation and distribution of Clean Utilities including water reclaim,  Potable Water, Lab Water, Purified Water, WFI, Pure Steam and Process Gas systems
Partner with Key stakeholders including operators, system owners, quality, and third party design firms.
Provide risk based technical input for system commissioning and qualification in support of URS’s, Risk Assessments, Functional Requirements, Verification protocols, PQ’s.
Provide technical leadership for clean utility operation and maintenance troubleshooting, including system excursion root cause analysis, CAPAs and remediation.
Independently verify design calculations and assumptions including hydraulic calculations, diversifications, and system modeling.
Lead multidisciplinary design reviews, constructability reviews, code evaluations, vendor technical evaluations, and technical bid analyses. Resolve advanced non-compliant or constrained existing conditions using risk-based engineering judgment.
Ensure engineering deliverables comply with AbbVie standards, approved project requirements, applicable GxP expectations, EHS requirements, and relevant codes and industry practices. Document assumptions, rationale, calculations, risks, decisions, and recommended mitigations.
Advise leadership on complex technical decisions, alternatives, risks, cost and schedule impacts, reliability implications, sustainability opportunities, and operational readiness. Escalate issues with clear evidence and actionable recommendations.
Coordinate scope, interfaces, deliverables, technical resources, schedules, and discipline budgets with project managers, site engineering, operations, Quality, Validation/CQV, EHS, MS&T, architects, other engineering disciplines, EPCM firms, vendors, and OEMs.
Analyze existing system performance and lead improvements that increase capacity, reliability, maintainability, energy efficiency, environmental performance, and total lifecycle value. Apply data operating data, commissioning, and maintenance systems to identify and sustain improvements.
Mentor engineers, provide technical review and coaching, develop training, and foster engineering excellence, accountability, collaboration, and proactive risk management.
Represent the Clean Utilities discipline in governance forums, project reviews, investigations, change controls, CAPAs, and regulatory or inspection-readiness activities as required.
Decision-Making and Organizational Impact
Independently establishes technical approaches and priorities for assigned complex projects and programs within approved governance and business objectives.
Provides expert contributions that materially influence project outcomes, facility performance, compliance, capital deployment, production continuity, and lifecycle operating cost.
Exercises judgment where requirements are incomplete, competing priorities exist, or solutions require integration of technical, quality, safety, operational, financial, and schedule considerations.
Influences cross-functional teams and external partners without relying on direct reporting authority; decisions may affect multiple functions, sites, or technology platforms
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Science or a relevant technical discipline required; advanced degree preferred where relevant.

title: Sr Scientist, Quantitative Bioimaging
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. We are seeking a Senior Scientist to advance quantitative bioimaging capabilities in support of immunology discovery research. In this role, you will work within a cross-functional team with access to multiple microscopy modalities, complex in vitro models, multimodal biological datasets, and advanced computational infrastructure.
You will develop and apply quantitative imaging, computer-vision, and machine-learning approaches to characterize cellular and tissue phenotypes, support the development of biological models, including co-cultures, organ-on-chip systems, organoids, and tissue explants, and generate insights that advance immunology discovery programs. This role combines hands-on delivery of robust, reproducible image-analysis workflows with the evaluation and application of advanced AI/ML approaches, including biomedical image segmentation, representation learning, foundation models, and scalable computational workflows. You will partner closely with wet-lab scientists, imaging specialists, computational scientists, and other subject-matter experts to translate biological questions into rigorous and impactful analysis strategies.
The role sits at the intersection of biology, bioengineering, microscopy, and computational science. Candidates with combined expertise in two or more of these areas are especially encouraged to apply.
Key Responsibilities
Develop, optimize, and apply imaging assays and quantitative image-analysis workflows for 2D and 3D cellular and tissue models to characterize cellular and other complex biological phenotypes.
Collaborate with wet-lab assay scientists, imaging specialists, and computational scientists from experimental and assay design through image acquisition, analysis, validation, and data delivery.
Extract biologically meaningful, multiparametric features from high-content imaging datasets and use them to characterize disease-relevant phenotypes, mechanisms, and treatment responses.
Apply statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning methods to identify candidate imaging biomarkers and relate imaging phenotypes to molecular, functional, and other biological readouts.
Contribute to the integration of imaging data with multimodal datasets, including molecular, single-cell, spatial, or perturbational data, where appropriate.
Establish quality-control and evaluation frameworks to assess image and assay quality, distinguish biological signal from technical artifacts, and define data-quality criteria, acceptance thresholds, and analytical limitations.
Maintain clear experimental and analytical records; analyze, visualize, and present results rigorously to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
Communicate methods, assumptions, results, uncertainties, and limitations effectively to cross-functional project teams.
Stay current with advances in quantitative bioimaging, image analysis, computer vision, and AI/ML for biological imaging, and evaluate opportunities to incorporate relevant approaches into team workflows.
Basic Qualifications
BS, MS, or PhD in engineering, biophysics, computational biology, imaging science, bioinformatics, or a related discipline, with typically 10-12+ (BS), 8-10+ (MS), or 0-4+ (PhD) years experience.
Demonstrated experience developing quantitative image-analysis or computational solutions involving one or more of the following: image segmentation, feature extraction, phenotypic profiling, object classification, or analysis of high-content imaging data.
Experience with at least one relevant imaging modality or assay type, such as confocal microscopy, high-content imaging, or cell painting.
Ability to assess image quality, recognize common imaging artifacts, and interpret biologically meaningful phenotypes.
Working knowledge of machine-learning or deep-learning approaches for biological imaging, with the ability to understand model behavior, assess performance, and contribute to appropriate evaluation strategies.
Proficiency with the Python data-science ecosystem, including NumPy, pandas, Polars, scikit-learn, and/or PyTorch.
Strong biological grounding, attention to experimental rigor, and demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with wet-lab and computational colleagues.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to explain methods, results, assumptions, and limitations to diverse audiences.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience working with complex in vitro models, such as organoids, organ-on-chip systems, co-cultures, tissue explants, or other advanced in vitro platforms.
Experience with classical bioimage-analysis tools such as CellProfiler, scikit-image, ImageJ/Fiji, or comparable platforms.
Exposure to deep-learning, self-supervised learning, foundation-model, embedding-based, or multimodal AI approaches for biological imaging.
Peer-reviewed publications, patents, conference presentations, or other demonstrated scientific contributions in quantitative bioimaging, computer vision, computational biology, bioengineering, or a related field.

description:
About the Role
The Global Alliance Director, AWS owns the strategic partnership between Adobe and AWS. You will set and execute the joint go-to-market (GTM) strategy, expand customer relationships and AWS Marketplace adoption, and align executives, field teams, product, and marketing across both companies. As the primary liaison between Adobe and AWS, you are accountable for revenue growth, cloud adoption, seller enablement, and delivery of the joint business plan.
This is a build role. AWS’s partner ecosystem is early, and its programs are still being designed. You will work across AWS, technology partners, and systems integrators (SIs), whose incentives on any given deal don’t always align, and you will help shape how new technology reaches the enterprise through the services ecosystem.
Key Responsibilities
Strategy and Execution
Own the end-to-end GTM strategy and operation of the alliance, prioritizing high-value enterprise opportunities and driving revenue through AWS field engagement and joint co-sell motions.
Decide where to concentrate investment across the partner portfolio, and make the case to stop investing where returns are not there.
Provide market intelligence and competitive insight on the partner ecosystem to inform product and commercial strategy.
Partner with Adobe’s alliances, sales, partner marketing, and regional cloud teams to keep the motion consistent globally while regions execute locally.
Governance and Operating Cadence
Lead the alliance operating rhythm: annual business planning, executive business reviews (EBRs), and quarterly and monthly business reviews (QBRs, MBRs).
Develop and manage annual business plans, growth initiatives, and partnership objectives with Adobe and AWS leaders.
Build scalable processes for partnership operations, including escalation management, business reviews, and reporting.
Maintain executive engagement plans, stakeholder maps, governance frameworks, and action tracking.
Prepare executive-ready materials, including strategic updates, account reviews, business cases, win stories, and operating plans.
Performance and Measurement
Own executive dashboards, scorecards, pipeline reviews, forecasting, and performance reporting for both leadership teams.
Define, track, and report alliance KPIs: revenue influence, AWS consumption, Marketplace performance, co-sell activity, customer adoption, migration outcomes, and executive engagement.
Monitor partnership health, flag risks and opportunities, and recommend actions to accelerate growth, drawing on data from sales, finance, marketing, product, engineering, and customer success.
Drive operational excellence through process improvement, reporting automation, and business insights.
Field Activation and Marketplace Growth
Expand AWS Marketplace adoption and manage incentive programs, sponsorships, funding, and co-sell benefits.
Activate partner field teams around Adobe priorities and strategic accounts to accelerate adoption of Adobe’s priority joint solutions and relevant third-party partner solutions.

Support regional sales leadership meetings, pipeline management, reporting, and field enablement alongside the Adobe AWS Alliance team.
Marketing and Thought Leadership
Work with Adobe and AWS sales and marketing teams to develop assets, events, and customer programs.
Support customer references, success stories, analyst engagements, and executive communications.

Align executives, product teams, the Adobe-AWS partner team, sales leadership, and marketing around year-over-year revenue growth.
Coordinate stakeholders across sales, marketing, product, engineering, finance, and operations to drive accountability on strategic initiatives.
Work with product management and engineering to align Adobe and AWS roadmaps and secure opportunities and funding for integration, innovation, and joint solutions.
Represent customer and AWS requirements in product planning, using adoption metrics and usage telemetry to measure impact and business value.

Influence and collaboration: Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and drive execution across matrix organizations, including sales, product, and marketing.
Communication: Exceptional communication skills and executive presence, with the ability to influence senior internal and external stakeholders.

Turn complex technical tradeoffs into clear decisions for engineering teams and concise narratives for leadership

Join our world-class Global Foundation Recruiting team, renowned for its dedication to excellence and innovation in talent acquisition. We are a dynamic, fun and passionate group, committed to building a diverse and high-performing workforce that propels our mission forward. As we navigate the ever-evolving landscape of our business, we pride ourselves on our collaborative approach, working closely with leaders across AMER to shape their hiring strategies.

Together, we are setting the standard for recruiting excellence at Airbnb.
The Difference You Will Make:
Your main responsibility will be to successfully bring searches to fruition and deliver exceptional experiences for candidates and hiring managers across our CBO function, with additional support for hiring across our corporate functions. Our team takes a consultative approach, working closely with stakeholders to understand their needs and provide tailored solutions. Dedicated to sourcing and hiring top talent in the market, we ensure that every individual interacting with Airbnb's recruitment process feels valued and supported.

Manage and drive a full-cycle recruitment process including sourcing, screening, interview, feedback and offers for all levels of candidates from entry to senior level — across our CBO function (sales, business development, partnerships and other commercial/revenue-generating roles) and our corporate functions (such as Finance, Legal, People, Marketing and Communications).

Influence business leaders and educate hiring managers on process, interview best practices, and decision making.

Accurately track candidate data and use systems correctly to be able to report to the business.
Find the best, and most passionate people for Airbnb using new and creative ways to find and engage them, while operating with speed in a high-velocity requisition environment.

5 - 7+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, with proven success recruiting for both revenue-generating roles (Sales, Business Development, Partnerships) and corporate/G&A functions (Finance, Legal, People, Marketing, Communications). title: Senior AI Development Lead
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join
We're the AI & ML Enablement team in Supply Tech. Teams across Airbnb come to us when they want AI to take over a process, or to ship an AI feature they can trust. We're helping business and field teams use AI to take on high volume-low value tasks, and helping product teams understand whether an AI feature works before it reaches our users. Day to day, we move manual review processes to AI and put people where their judgment matters most. We design new workflows so AI does the work from the start. We also build the labeled datasets that show whether the AI is right, and we keep everything running as models and policies change. Our methods and projects change as the models do, and we expect the scope of this role to grow with them.
The Difference You Will Make
You'd work with whichever team has a problem AI could take on, whether that's a business team with a process that's slow, expensive or inconsistent, or a product team getting an AI feature ready to launch. The job looks much the same either way. You start with how the work really gets done, build an AI version of it, and test it until you trust the results. Then you graduate it and use what worked on the next problem. The mix of projects will keep changing as AI takes on more of the work, so we care more about how you work than about a fixed list of projects. This is a hands-on role. You design and build the workflow, prove it works with data, and ship it with engineering and product.
A Typical Day
Drive the AI workflows and features we support from design to launch, defining the quality bar and measurement plan with engineering, product and business partners.
Prioritize projects by business impact, making trade-offs in partnership with your manager and the business and product leads you support.
Sit with the team that owns a problem, map how the work gets done today, and work out how AI can do it and where people step in for the hard cases.
Design and build AI workflows: write the prompts when needed, set up the pipeline and tooling, and monitor quality and drift once it's live.
Design the evaluation framework: build test sets, define accuracy and agreement metrics, and calibrate LLM judges against human reviewers.
Work with engineers on architecture and tooling decisions, and pressure-test estimates and scope.
Turn unclear guidelines into criteria a reviewer can apply consistently, working with product, Legal and Policy.
Work with subject matter experts to write labeling guidelines and produce human-verified labels on real data.
Run labeling at scale with vendor labeling teams, and check their work against agreement metrics and your own spot checks.
Work with product teams early to agree on what "good enough to launch" means for an AI feature, and bring the evidence and a recommendation for the go/no-go decision.
Build reusable evaluation and workflow components, document what you learn, and get other teams using them so the next team gets to production faster.
Keep our methods current as models, tools and policies change, and recommend what to retire when it stops working.
Your Expertise
8+ years in product or program management, analytics, consulting or applied AI, with a proven record of taking technical programs from idea to production and owning results such as backlog, cycle time or launch speed among others.
You're strong in SQL and in the statistics of quality: accuracy, precision and recall, sampling and reviewer agreement. You pull and analyze the data yourself instead of waiting for a report.
You’ve shipped something built on AI that other people rely on, such as a workflow, an agent or an automation, and you can show the before-and-after numbers. You can tell us where it failed and what you changed.
You're technically fluent enough to pressure-test an engineering estimate, understand how prompts, pipelines and evaluations fit together, and know when a workaround is the right call.
You're curious about how work actually gets done, including the awkward exceptions, and you've taken a messy process and made it measurable. You state the desired result first and measure success in business outcomes, not features shipped.
You have good judgment on quality. You can take messy qualitative feedback, such as reviewer comments or disagreements, and boil it down to what matters and what is worth changing.
You write clearly and can work with sales, operations, PMs and engineers in the same week, getting results through people you don't manage.
You're fine being the first person on a problem, and you try things yourself instead of waiting for someone to build them.
Nice to have
Hands-on Python and API experience, such as scripting data pulls, calling model APIs or building small automations.
Experience with LLM evaluation: building test sets, calibrating LLM judges or fine-tuning models.
Experience with experimentation and measurement, such as A/B tests, metric design and dashboards.
Trust and safety, content moderation, customer support automation, annotation operations or other human-in-the-loop work at scale.
Background in a two-sided marketplace, travel, or another operations-heavy business.

The Community You Will Join:
Every day, Airbnb hosts provide unique Stays and Experiences that connect guests with local communities in authentic and meaningful ways. These offerings are the core of what makes Airbnb special — creating connections and unforgettable memories for travelers worldwide.
The Connectivity team sits at the heart of Airbnb’s Supply strategy, managing the API Partners that power a significant share of our global inventory. Our connectivity partners — property management software providers, channel managers, and distribution platforms — unlock access to millions of listings and directly shape the quality and reliability of the host and guest experience. This team plays a critical role in growing, deepening, and shaping Airbnb’s partner ecosystem.
The Difference You Will Make:
As a Senior Partner Program Manager, you will run program management for Airbnb's Tier 3 connectivity book, including the long tail of unmanaged partners, and build the ecosystem partner program from the ground up. You are not managing a handful of accounts; you are designing and running the program that lets a small team credibly cover a big portfolio, and you are shaping how those partners show up on Airbnb.
You will bring a global view of the partner ecosystem, define success through Airbnb’s outcomes, and act as the connective tissue between partners, product teams, and internal stakeholders. You are someone who earns trust, moves fast, and holds yourself accountable for results.
This role goes beyond traditional account management. You will operate at the intersection of:
Program design
Commercial incentives
Ecosystem partnerships, including third-party tools that Hosts use
AI-assisted coverage
Marketplace dynamics
A Typical Day:
Strategic Thinking
Hold a portfolio view of the Tier 3 book and the long tail: which partners are growing, which are stalling, and which levers move the most nights, and set coverage accordingly rather than by relationship depth.
Define success through Airbnb's outcomes, not activity: partner productivity, feature adoption and program retention across the portfolio.
Commercial Acumen
Design incentive mechanics for long-tail API partners that move portfolio goals at scale
Structure what we ask of ecosystem partners (co-marketing, adoption data).
Partner Influence
Build and run the ecosystem partner program. Understand what each one wants from Airbnb, support them with a light touch, and set up cross-functional partnerships so the program stays aligned with their strategy.
Shape partner behavior through plays and programs rather than one-to-one management.
Build trusted relationships with founders and decision makers at ecosystem partners and represent Airbnb in external meetings and at industry events.
Product & Technical
Educate partners on the product roadmap and significant product changes to accelerate feature adoption, drawing on a working understanding of API and technical integrations.
Use AI tooling as part of the coverage model itself: triage, drafting, trigger handling and readouts that let one person hold a large book.
Execution & Ownership
Drive outcomes with minimal oversight. Own a full book of business end-to-end.
Act with speed and extreme ownership. This role is for someone who sees problems and fixes them and identifies opportunities.
Operate cross-functionally
Partner with Product, Engineering, Finance, Legal, and Regional teams.
Drive alignment across regions to ensure consistency in partner strategy.
Your Expertise:
Core Experience
8+ years in partner programs, platform or marketplace partnerships, or ecosystem management , including several years running a scaled partner program.
Program Design: You have built the tiers, triggers and operating rhythm for a partner program and lived with the consequences: who gets a cadence, who gets an automated touch, what gets handed off. You turn what works into a playbook others can run.
Commercial Fluency: Proven ability to structure, negotiate, and close deals — from term sheets to signed contracts. Comfortable in the room with senior commercial stakeholders.

Influencing Skills: You know how to shape behavior through trust, not just authority. Strong communicator with the ability to advocate internally and externally,
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Experience working across product, analytics, legal, finance, marketing and sales operations teams to deliver outcomes for partners.

Background from a marketplace or platform partner program (app ecosystems, developer or integration partner programs, seller or merchant programs). Hospitality technology (PMS, channel manager, OTA connectivity, pricing or data tools) is a plus, not a requirement.

The Community You Will Join:
Airbnb's Online Data organization runs the stores behind every booking, every message, and every payment. Storage Foundation owns the engines underneath those stores. We build and operate Airbnb's source of truth databases for the company's online OLTP traffic, and we own the control plane that provisions, upgrades, and heals them. This is engine work, not fleet administration. When our engines are slow, unavailable, or wrong, so is the product.
As Senior Engineering Manager you will lead engineers across multiple teams and you will manage managers. You will own the engine strategy, the reliability commitment that every service above you depends on, and the growth of the people who do the work. Your leverage comes from the managers and technical leads on your teams, the bar you hold in design and incident reviews, and the trust you build with the teams who stake their product on us.
The Difference You Will Make:
Set the technical direction for Airbnb's online storage engines
You will set a multi-year technical vision for the engines and the control plane beneath every transactional and key value store at Airbnb, and you will make the calls that follow from it. That includes where we invest in our own engine expertise, where we buy instead of build, how we evaluate alternative engines against real production traffic, and which capabilities have to exist before a workload can safely land on us. You will also make the cost of these systems measurable and attributable, so that investment decisions rest on evidence. You will make these calls alongside senior technical leaders across Online Data and the broader Infrastructure organization.
Make reliability the ground truth of the platform
The services built on your engines commit to availability targets that only hold if the engine underneath them is better than they are. You will own that engine level commitment and the error budgets that feed every product surface above it. You will drive fault isolation so that one tenant cannot degrade everyone else, prove regional failover with scheduled production drills, and treat capacity headroom as a reliability decision. You will own incidents in your area personally, and you will turn each one into a structural fix.
Make routine work disappear
Every ticket is a product team waiting on us and an engineer pulled off platform work. You will push your teams to build API first, so that provisioning, schema changes, grants, and quotas can be driven by an engineer, a tool, or an agent without a human in the loop. You will use AI where it takes real work off your teams.
Build and grow the team
You will coach engineering managers and senior technical leads, and grow the depth of database expertise inside Airbnb. That means taking a forward view of talent needs, building a succession pipeline, hiring senior engineers who can own a complex open source codebase, and creating the conditions where people do the most technically ambitious work of their careers. You will also represent this group to executive leadership and to our customers, and you will make the case for investment in terms the business can act on.

title: Deployment Program Manager, Global Logistics
description:
At Amazon, we are deploying Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) tracking technology across our physical network in a first-of-its-kind effort — at a scale and in a way that has not been done anywhere else in the company. This initiative brings real-time, item-level visibility to inbound shipments, and getting the underlying infrastructure installed and live across many sites is the critical path to making it real.
As a Deployment Program Manager, you own the end-to-end execution of site-based infrastructure deployment — from site survey through installation, testing, and go-live — coordinating internal Amazon stakeholders (IT, Operations, Reliability & Maintenance Engineering, and Site Points of Contact) and external installation partners across multiple concurrent sites. This is a tactical, hands-on execution role focused on driving sites through the deployment pipeline. You will be based in Los Angeles and travel to sites as needed for critical milestones, safety reviews, and partner relationship-building.
Key job responsibilities
• Drive parallel pre-install workstreams — network/IT readiness, safety and compliance documentation, hardware procurement and staging, and operational readiness — to completion before installation windows are committed.
• Serve as the primary field coordination point between installation vendors, site points of contact, and internal Amazon teams during active installs.
• Provide timely, accurate site-level status input (survey, design, network readiness, installation, and go-live milestones) to the program’s reporting process.
• Escalate blockers in real time — access delays, compliance gaps, scheduling conflicts, equipment issues — to protect the program’s delivery timeline.
• Coordinate site readiness planning pre-install, including safety zones, operational vs. non-operational area access, and daily coordination plans with site operations.
• Support post-installation testing and validation coordination with technology and installation partners.
• Maintain and continuously improve deployment playbooks and pre-install checklists based on site-by-site lessons learned.
• Travel to sites as needed for critical milestones, safety reviews, and stakeholder relationship-building (frequency determined by program needs).
A day in the life
Your day balances two kinds of work. For sites approaching installation, you run proactive, scheduled readiness coordination — kickoff calls with the Site POC, site IT, and the vendor; dedicated IT follow-up on network readiness; vendor and safety/compliance prep; and a final go/no-go on the start date. For sites already in active installation, you shift to reactive, real-time troubleshooting — morning check-ins, ad hoc issue calls, same-day escalation of field blockers, and feeding site-level status into the program’s reporting. Periodic site travel and ongoing refinement of the deployment playbook round out the role.
About the team
You are part of Global Logistics which provides transportation offerings from imports and domestic shippers into the Amazon Warehouse and Distribution and Fulfillment Network. We treat our shippers as customers and obsess with giving them a loveable way to inject their inventory into our network. In this team specifically, this is a first-of-its-kind initiative bringing Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) tracking technology to Amazon’s physical network to deliver real-time, item-level visibility into inbound shipments. The deployment team is responsible for bringing this infrastructure online across sites — partnering with Operations, IT, Reliability & Maintenance Engineering, site leadership, and external installation vendors to turn the technology vision into live, working capability on the floor. It is a fast-moving, high-ownership environment where field execution directly determines how quickly the program scales.

- 3+ years of maintenance planner/scheduler in industrial maintenance, manufacturing, or distribution industries experience

- Experience in MS Access and SQL
- Experience in requirement gathering and ability to write clear and detailed requirement document
- Experience using Microsoft Projects software
- Experience with material handling systems (MHS) installation, operation and maintenance
- Experience working in an analytical environment with cross-functional teams
