title: Director, Product Management — Forward Deployed Engineering, AWS Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE)
description:
**The Opportunity**
This is a greenfield role. You'll build a product management practice, shape an entirely new category at AWS, and establish the engagement model that delivers delightful outcomes enabling customers to transform themselves.
**The Role**
As the Director of Product Management — Forward Deployed Engineering will lead product management for FDE, building and leading the PM team that owns the end-to-end product lifecycle from customer engagement through production delivery through optimization and self-sufficiency. Your product managers embed directly inside enterprise customers — defining outcomes, writing specs, working hand-in-hand with engineering to ship production systems — and every engagement feeds back into AWS services and an underlying platform that makes the next one faster.
This is not a traditional AWS Product Management role. FDE product managers are field-facing: they live inside delivery, sit with customers, and turn engagement learnings into compounding platform value. You are the "CEO of the customer problem" — responsible for the *why* and *what*, while engineering owns the *how*.
Key job responsibilities
### Product Leadership
You own the customer outcomes. Your teams operate inside customer environments under real constraints and ambitious timelines — regulated data, brownfield infrastructure, multi-stakeholder governance. You lead the customer engagement strategy from the product side: define what a great pod PM does, allocate PM talent across engagements, ensure pods are solving the right problems, and hold executive customer relationships at the CIO/CTO level built on trust earned through delivered outcomes.
### Product & Platform Influence
You see what breaks  across deployments and turn that into product direction. You influence AWS service roadmap from a position of earned authority because you've lived the deployment pain firsthand, and identify when custom pod work should graduate into platform primitives or native service capabilities.
You shape the FDE engagement model: how we scope, what we deliver, what we price, what we leave behind.
### Industry Practice & Productization
You build the domain expertise that compounds. Your teams develop industry-specific accelerators, reference architectures, and blueprints that generate pipeline for the next customer in your vertical. You define the use cases that feed qualification, pricing, and pod composition. You measure what matters: asset reuse rate, time-to-value, engagement velocity
### Go-to-Market Partnership
You partner with sales, specialists, and marketing to define pricing, packaging, and positioning. You own the commercial model for FDE engagements — how we price outcomes, what the customer buys, and how we demonstrate ROI. You build pipeline through customer stories, reference architectures
About the team
95% of enterprise technology pilots deliver zero measurable P&L impact. The technology works — the gap is in the last mile: getting production systems running inside complex enterprises where legacy infrastructure, regulated data, and organizational complexity collide. AWS is making a billion-dollar investment in Forward Deployed Engineering ("FDE") to close that gap, and we're hiring product leaders who will define what we build and why.
Basic qualifications: - BS/MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or related technical field
- 15+ years in product management, with significant experience in enterprise environments
- Track record building and leading product management teams through complex enterprise applications with direct customer and business impact
- Technical depth — agentic systems, AI/ML, business workflow automation, enterprise integration — ability to engage at the architecture level and roll up sleeves when the hardest problems demand it
- Experience with pricing, packaging, and go-to-market — having partnered with sales, marketing, and GTM teams to define commercial models and build pipeline
- Executive presence with C-suite customers, earned through outcomes — can run a room with a VP/CTO and translate business problems into product requirements in real time
- Demonstrated experience designing and architecting software services or platforms consumed by external developers or technical customers — including hands-on work with service architecture, APIs, scalability, and enterprise systems integration
Preferred qualifications: - Founder mentality: has built a team, product, or practice from scratch and scaled it
- Experience delivering production systems inside large enterprise customer environments: regulated data, legacy infrastructure, organizational complexity, multi-party governance
- Has built industry-specific solutions or vertical practices at scale — creating reusable assets that became a competitive moat
- Builder-leader who ships alongside the team, is energized by customer problems, and operates where the customer sees your results in real-time
- Has owned a feedback loop between field/deployment teams and a product/platform org: knows how to turn deployment pain into roadmap priorities with data and earned credibility

title: Principal Product Manager, Technical - Amazon Freight Support Exp, Amazon Freight
description:
When a shipper moves a truckload with Amazon Freight, they expect the load to be scheduled, tracked, and delivered without having to chase anyone. Today, too much of that experience depends on manual work. Support associates switch between many tools to find information, repetitive tasks stay manual, and some work happens outside our systems where no one can see it, measure it, or automate it. Shippers feel the result as slow answers and repeat contacts. We are hiring a Principal Product Manager - Technical to change that: to make shipper support for Amazon Freight fast, measurable, and increasingly automated.
You will own the multi-year product strategy and roadmap for the Amazon Freight shipper support experience, covering the platform, automation, and AI that associates use to resolve shipper issues. Your mandate has three parts. First, eliminate the reasons shippers contact us, by finding root causes in scheduling, tendering, tracking, disruptions, and billing and driving fixes upstream with the teams that own them. Second, make every piece of operational work visible and owned, by consolidating work done in other systems into a single operator console and ensuring every task has an owner, a queue, and a service level. Third, automate the work that does not need human judgment, using rule-based automation first and AI agents where they add value.
The heart of this role is a continuous automation flywheel. You will define the architecture for a framework that captures task-level data across operational workflows (what work is done, why, and how long it takes), then run a repeatable cycle of discover, document, model, measure, build, and automate. You will use that data and AI to find and rank automation candidates, launch rule-based automation for deterministic tasks in areas like scheduling, disruption recovery, trailer pool management, and proactive shipper communications, and route exceptions to the right operator. Every eliminated task is recorded, so the team can prove impact and reinvest the time saved.
This is a technical role. You will work with engineers on the operator platform architecture, the data model for task capture, integrations with the operational systems that work moves out of, and the design of AI agents that retrieve information, draft responses, and take actions safely. You will make build-versus-reuse decisions, weigh trade-offs between rule-based and AI approaches, and set the guardrails for automation.
You will partner closely with Amazon Freight support operations leaders, who own priorities and targets for their teams, and with engineering, operations, policy, and the product teams that own scheduling, execution, and disruption management. You propose solutions backed by data; operations validates them; engineering builds them. You will work as a peer to the Amazon Shipping support product leader, sharing platforms, patterns, and AI capabilities so that what works in one business scales to the other.
We measure success with the same metrics as our other shipper support products: support contacts per load, first-contact resolution, shipper satisfaction (CSAT), automation rate, average handle time, and annual cost savings. Because measurable work comes first, you will also own input metrics that show the work is visible: share of associate work captured in the operator console, share of contacts with a recorded reason, tasks with an owner and service level, and tasks eliminated through automation. You will set the baselines and targets, and report progress in weekly and monthly business reviews.
Key job responsibilities
• Define the 3-year vision and strategy for the Amazon Freight shipper support experience, and secure alignment from operations, engineering, and senior leadership across Amazon Freight and ASCS.
• Analyze contact drivers by shipper segment (enterprise, mid-market, small business) and mode, identify the root causes behind repeat and avoidable contacts, and drive fixes with the teams that own scheduling, tendering, tracking, and billing.
• Define and deliver the consolidation of support work now done outside the operator console into a single tool, so associates plan, execute, and record their work in one place. Sequence the migration in a published priority order and retire replaced shadow tools and dashboards as each workflow moves.
• Define the data model and architecture that captures 100% of associate task execution by task type, reason, and time spent, so labor is measurable by task and the business can model demand, measure productivity, and size automation.
• Define owners, queues, severity tiers, and service levels for every task type, with a daily view for managers, so no shipper issue sits open without an operator.
• Lead the discover, document, model, measure, build, automate cycle. Rank automation candidates with data and AI, launch rule-based automation for deterministic tasks, and use AI to propose new workflows from what the team learns.
• Define the strategy for AI agents that retrieve information, draft responses, and take actions, including the guardrails, human review points, and quality measures that let associates trust them.
• Partner with operations and policy owners so standard operating procedures (SOPs) are current, structured, and usable by both associates and automation.
• Own PRFAQs, PRDs, and launch plans, drive launches from requirements through adoption and measured impact, and mentor product managers on technical product practice.

description:

To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. These teammates bring the right guidance, practice, and credential right into the tools and tasks they already use. This is a new product space where the right experience is still being invented, and we are looking for a product leader who partners deeply with design to define it.
As a Senior Product Manager - Technical, External Services, you will partner with design and lead the development of AI learning teammates, owning the product vision, requirements, and roadmap from concept through go-to-market. You will champion the needs of learners and the organizations that train and certify them, and translate ambiguous, open-ended problems into clear product definitions and detailed business requirements documents. You will work hand-in-hand with design, engineering, science, learning scientists, and operational stakeholders to prioritize the roadmap and spearhead the definition of new capabilities.
This role sits where product, learning, and design meet. A great learning teammate is built on more than a strong model and solid systems. It depends on trust, on clear interaction patterns, and on how it feels to be coached while you work. You will co-own the end-to-end experience with design. That spans how a teammate joins a team, how it surfaces learning in the flow of work, how it recognizes mastery and guides someone toward certification, and how people stay in control of their own development.
The successful candidate must have exceptional problem solving skills, strong business judgment, and demonstrated experience leading cross-functional teams. We are looking for a proven ability to execute both strategically and tactically, and someone who is excited to take on new, ambiguous projects that will be industry defining. This position requires a solid technical background, and the candidate should be customer-focused with a passion for learning, AI, agents, and the future of how skills are built.
AWS Training and Certification helps people and organizations build the cloud and AI skills they need to be successful, from foundational learning through role-based certifications recognized across the industry. As a member of this team, you'll support the development and management of AI-powered learning experiences that reach learners worldwide, including the agentic learning teammates that will define the next decade of how people grow their skills.

- Partner with design to define and own the end-to-end experience for AI learning teammates, from onboarding and interaction patterns to how learning is delivered in the flow of work.

You might start your morning in a design review, working through the interaction model for how a teammate offers a quick coaching moment the instant someone hits a task they haven't done before. title: Program Manager III, Integrations, Amazon Shipping
description:
Amazon Shipping delivers packages for businesses across the United States and Europe, and most of our parcels arrive through API integrations with shippers and shipping software partners such as multi-carrier platforms, warehouse and order management systems, and e-commerce platforms. Every shipper launch depends on a chain of teams landing their part on time: Solutions Architects who design the integration, the developer platform team that grants API access, Product and Engineering who build the capabilities shippers need, Partnerships who manage the software partners, and Commercial who own the shipper relationship. The External System Integrations team owns that launch experience, from a shipper's first technical conversation to go-live and the first weeks of live shipping.
Do you want to own the program that decides how fast a shipper goes from signed deal to first shipment? Have you found where months of elapsed time actually go, and taken them out? Amazon Shipping is seeking a Senior Program Manager to own the shipper integration launch program across the United States and Europe. Hundreds of shippers launch with us each year, from enterprise retailers with complex multi-system landscapes to mid-market shippers launching through existing software partners. You will define the program, break time to first shipment into stages the team can measure and improve, drive the dependencies that hold launches back, and build the capacity and peak plans leadership commits against. You will also run the mechanisms that keep a growing team out of firefighting: launch standards, post-launch handoff, error reduction, and a working relationship with every team we depend on.
Key job responsibilities
- Own the shipper launch portfolio across the United States and Europe, covering every launch from technical discovery to go-live and post-launch handoff, with a single view of stage, risk, owner and date
- Define the launch program, including its goals, stage definitions, entry and exit criteria, and success metrics, with time to first shipment as the measure that matters
- Break time to first shipment into its stages, such as developer registration, API access approval, sandbox testing, partner build and shipper go-live, measure each one, and set targets against what shippers expect rather than what we do today
- Drive dependencies that sit outside the team, including developer access and identity verification, sandbox capabilities, partner build timelines, and EDI and invoicing work owned by other engineering teams, and escalate early when a launch date is at risk
- Run the standing relationship with the developer platform team that controls API access, with a named point of contact, agreed response times, a shared issue log and one combined voice for the business rather than individual escalations
- Build the team's capacity plan, including how integration work is weighted and assigned across architects, and use it to show leadership what the team can launch next quarter and what it would take to launch more
- Own peak readiness for integrations each year: committed shipper list, volume forecasts, API capacity increases, freeze dates and the dependency map, starting months ahead of the season
- Run the post-launch handoff from launch architects to the support team, with defined criteria, a hypercare period, and sign-off from the shipper and Commercial
- Run error-reduction programs with Commercial, Support and Engineering for live shippers whose API errors cost them volume, with a target and an owner per shipper
- Own the integration launch standards: the launch plan template, the partner engagement standard, and a post-launch review for key launch, and make sure what one launch learns is applied to the next launch on the same platform
- Keep pipeline and launch data accurate at the source in Salesforce, including how integration type, partner and launch dates are captured by Commercial, rather than through weekly clean-up
- Maintain the source of truth for integration and partner capabilities used in tenders, sales conversations and enablement, with verified status and dates, and track adoption of new API capabilities across live shippers

Your work starts with the crawl phase: standing up centralized KYC and the legal-entity foundation, and cleaning existing account data so it meets the new standard.

description:

AWS operates the world's largest fleet of Storage servers powering S3 at cloud scale. Our team takes these platforms from design into high-volume production, owning the manufacturing processes, test strategies, and quality systems that determine whether a new server ships on time and at the right quality. We are seeking a Sr Manufacturing Product Engineer to drive New Product Introduction (NPI) manufacturing and quality for Storage server platforms, from early design engagement through volume production. You will define manufacturing processes, test flows, and quality controls, serve as the primary manufacturing engineering interface between hardware design, supply chain, and ODM partners, and ensure products are optimized for manufacturability and launched at exceptional quality.
What You Will Do
You will own how a new Storage platform is manufactured. You will engage with hardware design early to influence testability and manufacturability, define the manufacturing test strategy and quality plan, and drive the process from prototype through Pilot and volume ramp. You will run NUDD (New, Unique, Difficult, Different) risk assessments before design freeze, lead design reviews, and drive root cause corrective action on manufacturing blockers and quality escapes. When a platform ramps to volume with high first-pass yield and no quality escapes reaching the fleet, that is your impact.
Why You Will Love It
The world's most advanced frontier models train on the hardware you help build. You will see your process and test decisions scale across a large fleet of servers, and you will work at the point where design meets the factory floor. The team is deeply technical and high-trust, and you own manufacturing outcomes end to end from design engagement through volume production.
The Ideal Candidate
You think across the full manufacturing stack, from SMT assembly and test coverage to line balance, yield, and quality systems. You are as comfortable in a DFx review reading gerber files as you are on an ODM floor debugging a failing test station. You drive decisions with data, hold manufacturing partners to a high bar, and bring structured problem-solving and disciplined change management to a fast-moving NPI environment. You mentor junior engineers, contribute to hiring, and raise the manufacturing engineering bar for the team.
Key job responsibilities
Design for Manufacturability & Risk
- Perform NUDD (New, Unique, Difficult, Different) risk assessments and carry-over analysis to identify and mitigate manufacturing risks before design freeze
- Participate in DFx reviews (DFM/DFA/DFT) leveraging mechanical CAD models, gerber files, and mock-up samples, driving design improvements in partnership with hardware engineering
- Lead DFMEA/PFMEA reviews and develop process flow diagrams and quality control plans
NPI Manufacturing & Test Strategy
- Own end-to-end NPI manufacturing execution for Storage server platforms across engineering phases and Pilot builds
- Define the manufacturing test strategy including test flows, coverage, duration, fixture requirements such as in circuit tests (ICT), board functional test (BFT) and system-level tests
- Own Contract Manufacturer enablement including BOM requirements, assembly workflows, testing protocols, and tooling specifications
- Research automation techniques and develop new tests and systems to improve manufacturing efficiency and reduce test dwell time
Quality & Continuous Improvement
- Drive Root Cause Corrective Action (RCCA) for manufacturing blockers and quality escapes
- Execute test rack inspections and quality checklists; issue quality alerts, deviations, and ship-holds as required
- Own manufacturing quality metrics and drive yield improvement, and cost optimization through process and automation engineering
Capacity & Production Ramp
- Create manufacturing capacity plans with simulations across build phases; conduct line balance and cycle time analysis to maximize throughput
- Provide on-site ODM support during critical builds and production ramp
- Collaborate with suppliers and internal teams on Storage module integration, thermal validation, and manufacturing requirements
Cross-Team Collaboration
- Serve as the primary manufacturing engineering interface between hardware design, supply chain, and ODM/CM partners
- Manage manufacturing requirements, scope, schedules, and deliverables across engineering teams, suppliers, and partners
- Perform risk assessment, mitigation, and change management throughout the program lifecycle
- Domestic and international travel (~25%) to ODM/CM and design partner sites
A day in the life
You start the day reviewing first-pass yield data from an overnight Pilot build at your ODM, isolating a test station driving a recurring failure. Mid-morning, you lead a DFx review with hardware design, pushing changes to improve testability before design freeze. In the afternoon, you drive an RCCA on a solder defect with the CM quality team and update the control plan. You end the day refining the capacity plan and line balance for the next build phase.
About the team
The Hardware Engineering S3 Storage platform team is a group of engineers and technical program managers directly responsible for launching Storage servers into the AWS fleet. Located in Denver, Seattle, and Cupertino, we collaborate with global development teams and ODM/CM partners to deliver next-generation Storage server infrastructure deployed in datacenters worldwide. We move fast with small, empowered teams delivering end-to-end, from server conception through volume production and fleet-scale operations.

description:

Seattle, WA, USA
The Mission
AWS customers trust us with their sensitive data. We are building operator access controls and security infrastructure that give customers and regulators verifiable evidence of how AWS protects that data. The program brings together authorization, identity, telemetry, operational tooling, and assurance systems across every AWS region into a unified security posture. You drive this program end-to-end: setting the roadmap, aligning teams, accelerating delivery, and producing the evidence packages that demonstrate our controls to customers.
What You'll Drive
You own the program that enables AWS to demonstrate operator access is controlled, monitored, and auditable. You define how AWS services adopt operator access controls, sequence regional launches across commercial and isolated partitions, and deliver evidence packages that unlock customer adoption in regulated industries. You shape how identity, authorization, telemetry, and operational tooling come together into a coherent security posture. You define the metrics that make the program legible: how services are progressing through control adoption, how operators access customer content and under what authorization, and how evidence packages map to audit requirements. These metrics give leaders the data to prioritize investment, give service teams visibility into their own security posture, and give customers confidence in the controls protecting their data. You drive security engagements: threat models, Red Team exercises, third-party reviews. As the program matures, you extend these controls to support Zero Operator Access capabilities.
The Opportunity
Operator access controls touch every AWS service that stores or processes customer content. You work at the intersection of authorization, identity, telemetry, monitoring, operational tooling, and customer-facing assurance teams. Each service brings its own architecture, regional footprint, and operational model. Isolated regions introduce additional coordination across security boundaries. This breadth gives you influence across AWS that is rare for a program role.
You translate this technical landscape into a coherent program narrative for VP and CISO-level leadership: where the program is heading, what is on track, where to invest next, and what trade-offs to make. You are the person who connects engineering execution to customer outcomes and leadership priorities.
The Impact
Your work supports CISO-level goals and direct customer commitments. Regulated customers in financial services, defense, and healthcare make adoption decisions based on the controls you deliver. Evidence packages feed into audit engagements that accelerate customer onboarding. When you succeed, AWS gives customers verifiable proof that operator access is controlled, monitored, and auditable across their services.
What We're Looking For
You thrive in ambiguity and create clarity for others. You have experience managing programs spanning distributed systems, security infrastructure, or compliance-driven initiatives. You understand authentication, authorization, and cryptographic systems well enough to have informed technical conversations and spot opportunities early. You manage through influence, not authority. You work across organizations with different priorities and build alignment. You communicate crisply to senior leadership, distinguishing signal from noise. You build mechanisms that scale: dashboards, status cadences, escalation paths, and dependency trackers that outlast any individual program review.
Key job responsibilities

title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Shipping Speed, Selection & Charges, Shipping Platform
description:
Every time someone shops on Amazon, our systems influence what they see about delivery: whether an item can ship to them, how fast it will arrive, and what shipping will cost. We own shipping speed, selection and charges for Amazon stores around the world. Our 6 Tier-1 services sit on the critical path of every product page, cart and checkout, handling millions of requests per second before checkout. We're looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to help us modernize how that works and to change how we build software along the way.
You'll lead three programs that matter to customers and to how we build:
Rebuild how Amazon models delivery capabilities. Our ship options were first built just to describe speed. Over time each one also took on other delivery features, so a single identifier now does several jobs across many ordering, delivery and fulfillment systems. You'll drive the multi-year platform change that lets teams launch new delivery experiences, like ultra-fast quick commerce, age-verified delivery or grocery delivery, by combining reusable building blocks. Today each one needs a new ship option.
Build the customer rescue product. When an item can't be delivered to a customer, the purchase shouldn't end there. Our team is building customer rescue, the product that catches these dead ends across the shopping journey and help customers complete their order: healing carts and checkouts with substitutes and alternate offers and filtering undeliverable items out of discovery. You'll drive its delivery and adoption across retail, grocery and quick commerce and other programs, partnering with the teams who own each experience.
Help lead our move to AI-driven software development. We're building toward a model where AI agents do much of the development work and engineers step in where human judgment matters. You'll own the plan to roll this out across our teams, decide how we measure success.
You'll work with principal engineers, product managers and engineering leaders across Amazon, and you'll regularly write for and present to senior leadership.
Key job responsibilities
Rebuild how Amazon models delivery capabilites
Own the roadmap to move Amazon's ordering and delivery systems off ship-option-specific logic and onto reusable capabilities and signals, so new delivery experiences launch without new ship options.
Drive adoption across shipping, checkout, fulfillment and transportation systems. Sequence integrations, align designs with principal and senior engineers, and onboard new businesses such as quick commerce, grocery and age-verified delivery.
Customer rescue product
Drive delivery of the customer rescue product from roadmap to launch: cart and checkout healing with substitutes and alternate offers, clear restriction messages, and filtering undeliverable items out of discovery.
Lead adoption across retail, grocery and quick commerce, partnering with the teams who own each shopping experience.
Coordinate A/B experiments, staged rollouts and launch readiness across marketplaces, and use the results to drive launch decisions.
Run weekly, monthly and business reviews with senior leadership, with written narratives on results, risks, recovery plans and decisions needed.
AI-driven software development
Own the plan to move our teams to a model where AI agents do much of the development work and engineers step in at key decision points. Push for full adoption over isolated pilots.
Define how adoption and impact are measured, such as coverage by service, changes shipped through agents and automated test coverage.
A day in the life
Your morning might start chairing the Ship Option Control Board, where you and principal engineers from several organizations decide whether a new delivery experience should be a reusable capability or a signal. Later you turn the latest customer rescue experiment readout into a clear recommendation for the weekly leadership review, then meet with a partner team to plan bringing the product into their shopping experience. In the afternoon you sit with a team moving its service to AI-driven development, find where the agents still get stuck, and fold those gaps into the adoption plan. You might end the day tuning an agent that drafts your program update from tracker data, so the next one takes minutes instead of hours.

title: Technical Program Manager - Business Risk
description:
At Audible, we believe stories have the power to transform lives. It’s why we work with some of the world’s leading creators to produce and share audio storytelling with our millions of global listeners. We are dreamers and inventors who come from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences to empower and inspire each other. Imagine your future with us.
ABOUT THIS ROLE
As a Senior Technical Program Manager focused on Business Risk, you'll serve as the strategic risk advisor to one of Audible's business organizations, partnering with its senior leaders to understand and manage the risks they face across security, fraud, content piracy, data protection, brand, and operational domains. Audible's businesses depend on a broad network of external partners, vendors, platforms, and technology, and increasingly on AI-enabled operations. Each relationship and each system is a place where unauthorized access, fraud, data exposure, or operational failure can become financial loss or harm to the Audible brand.
You will own Audible's business risk program for the organization you support end to end. You'll assess its business processes, vendor and partner relationships, and technology stack; drive remediation programs to completion with Audible InfoSec, Amazon Security, and business teams; run the recurring risk review and risk acceptance process; and own risk reporting to business and Audible leadership. Rather than building new programs, you'll use Audible's and Amazon's established risk management programs and paved path solutions, including security, fraud defense, piracy prevention, and data protection, and help the business adopt them in a way that fits how it works. Your understanding of the organization's strategy and roadmap will let you position risk management as an enabler, so the business can scale, enter new markets, and launch new initiatives safely.
ABOUT YOU
You thrive at the intersection of risk advisory and business enablement. You see risk not as a blocker but as a lens that helps a business grow safely and move faster. You are comfortable starting where the problem is not yet defined: you can take an open question such as "how exposed are we, and where?", frame the program, set its goals and success metrics, and drive it to delivery with limited guidance. You build trusted relationships with senior business leaders, translate technical risk into business language, and influence teams that do not report to you, including security, engineering, legal, and external partners. You make thoughtful trade-offs between short-term needs and long-term risk reduction, and you know how and when to escalate without damaging relationships. Your security background lets you speak credibly with security teams and understand the technical detail behind a risk. You write clear, concise narratives and are comfortable presenting risk decisions to Directors and VPs. You are a simplifier: you add process only where it earns its place, and you retire it when it no longer does.
As a Senior Technical Program Manager - Business Risk, you will...
- Serve as the primary business risk advisor to the senior leadership of the Audible business organization you support, building trusted relationships and helping leaders understand risks across security, fraud, content piracy, data protection, brand, and operational domains
- Own the business risk program for that organization end to end: define its scope, goals, and success metrics, and drive it from assessment through remediation with limited guidance
- Conduct risk assessments of the organization's business processes, platforms, technology stack, and vendor and partner relationships, and turn findings into prioritized, measurable remediation plans
- Drive governance and hardening programs for the external platforms, accounts, and third-party access the business depends on, in partnership with security and platform owners
- Assess risks in AI-enabled and automated business processes, including AI vendor solutions and the data that flows through them
- Run the recurring risk review and the risk acceptance and policy exception process for the organization, ensuring risk decisions are made at the right level, documented, and revisited
- Embed risk review into the organization's planning and launch processes, so new vendors, platforms, products, and markets are assessed before they go live rather than after an incident
- Partner with Audible InfoSec, Amazon Security, Fraud Defense, Anti-Piracy, Legal, Privacy, and Compliance to bring expert guidance and established paved path solutions to the business, and drive their adoption rather than building new programs
- Own risk reporting for the organization, developing risk metrics, dashboards, and executive narratives that give leadership clear visibility into risk posture and remediation progress
- Present risk information to Directors and VPs, laying out the options, the trade-offs between short-term needs and long-term risk reduction, and the decision required
- Negotiate priorities and resources across business, security, and engineering teams to deliver remediation on schedule, and escalate effectively when a path forward is blocked
- Proactively identify emerging risks from changes in the organization's business model, vendors, technology, and use of AI, and streamline or retire risk processes that no longer add value
- Contribute to Audible's broader business risk program, including the shared risk assessment framework, risk acceptance governance, and leadership reporting across business risk areas
- Mentor and develop others, and contribute to hiring for the business risk team
ABOUT AUDIBLE
Audible is the leading producer and provider of audio storytelling. We spark listeners’ imaginations, offering immersive, cinematic experiences full of inspiration and insight to enrich our customers daily lives. We are a global company with an entrepreneurial spirit. We are dreamers and inventors who are passionate about the positive impact Audible can make for our customers and our neighbors. This spirit courses throughout Audible, supporting a culture of creativity and inclusion built on our People Principles and our mission to build more equitable communities in the cities we call home.

title: Engineering Manager, Private Cloud Compute Inference Routing
description:
At Apple, iCloud Platform Engineering builds the server stack behind Push Notifications, iMessage, FaceTime, iCloud, iCloud Private Relay and Private Cloud Compute (PCC), the backbone of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence. We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead PCC inference routing. These systems send every inference request to the right compute across a global, multi-region fleet, while keeping latency low, availability high and PCC's privacy guarantees intact.
This is a technically grounded leadership role for someone who thrives at scale, can bring clarity to complex and fast-changing environments, and is energized by building both systems and teams. You'll guide architectural direction, scale operational practices and develop the engineers and leaders who will shape how Apple delivers cloud inference.
Routing LLM inference at Apple's scale takes systems that adapt to changing demand, available capacity and failures while keeping latency low and accelerator utilization high. As the fleet grows across regions and cells, routing must account for capacity and health across the whole fleet, not just a single site. PCC adds a basic architectural requirement: request content stays encrypted outside trusted compute nodes. You'll lead the design of routing and scheduling strategies within this privacy model. Together with inference and security teams, you'll evaluate techniques such as cache-aware request placement and prefill/decode disaggregation. Your scope includes the inference AI gateway layer, where requests are authenticated, metered, prioritized and streamed back to clients, all without exposing request content.
This work has broad reach. Every improvement to routing makes Siri AI and Apple Intelligence faster and more reliable, and makes better use of Apple's inference capacity. In your first year, you'll be expected to grow a high-performing organization, set a clear technical roadmap, and measurably improve routing latency, availability and fleet utilization.
Minimum qualifications: Extensive software engineering experience with a demonstrated track record of leading teams that design, build, and operate large-scale distributed systems in production environments—whether through direct management, indirect oversight, or a combination thereof
Proven ability to recruit, develop, and retain high-performing engineers and leaders
Experience delivering API gateways (preferably inference AI gateways), request routing, load balancing, scheduling, or traffic management systems at scale
Expertise of LLM inference serving, including request routing, KV-cache placement and reuse, prefill/decode disaggregation, and the tradeoffs between latency, throughput and accelerator use
A record of shipping highly reliable systems in high-availability environments, including leading incident management, on-call and reliability practices

Preferred qualifications: Proven leadership in developing LLM inference serving or routing platforms (e.g., llm-d, NVIDIA Dynamo, vLLM, SGLang, or managed inference services)

Track record of scaling teams and organizations during rapid growth while maintaining top-tier hiring and engineering standards

title: IR Scanning Electrician
description:
In Places, we don’t sit back and let things happen, we make things happen, and we do this in service to all Apple employees and customers. Our team is a diverse and nimble group that manages Apple’s corporate and retail workplaces and workplace services. We develop and manage Apple’s global real estate portfolio, lead all related capital construction projects, provide outstanding facilities and site services, develop and lead sustainability initiatives to reduce the environmental impact of all Apple facilities, including commute and renewable energy programs, and do everything we can to ensure the health and safety of all Apple personnel, facilities, and customers in our facilities around the world.
The Critical Facilities Electrical team is responsible for the safe and reliable operation of electrical systems and critical infrastructure across Apple's NorCal Places portfolio. Our preventive program emphasizes early detection, root-cause analysis, and condition-based maintenance to keep mission-critical equipment running. We partner closely with engineering, operations, and capital projects to protect the people and work that depend on our electrical systems.
We are seeking a detail-oriented and safety-driven IR Scanning Electrician to join our team as the dedicated thermographer responsible for infrared inspections of electrical equipment across Apple's NorCal campuses. This role is essential to identifying anomalies before they become failures and to advancing our shift from reactive repair to predictive, condition-based maintenance.
The IR Scanning Electrician will perform infrared thermographic surveys on switchgear, panelboards, transformers, motor control centers, and distribution equipment across Apple's NorCal campuses. They will document findings, prioritize remediation in partnership with the electrical operations team, and contribute to the Critical Facilities Electrical team's predictive maintenance program. The role reports to the Electrical Manager.
Minimum qualifications: 5+ years of commercial, industrial, utility, or critical-facilities electrical experience.
Current Level I infrared thermography qualification or certification from a recognized program aligned with an applicable industry standard or employer-approved written practice (e.g., ASNT SNT-TC-1A or equivalent).
Demonstrated experience conducting infrared inspections of energized electrical distribution equipment rated from 120/208 V through 12 kV.
Proficiency in using radiometric thermal-imaging cameras and infrared reporting software.
Ability to accurately interpret thermal patterns while accounting for load, emissivity, reflected temperature, environmental conditions, and equipment construction.
Ability to produce technically accurate, well-organized inspection reports and clearly communicate conditions requiring immediate escalation.
Ability to work independently while following established procedures and coordinating with site operations personnel.
Working knowledge of NFPA 70E electrical safe-work practices.
Ability to read and interpret single-line diagrams, panel schedules, and electrical drawings.
Ability to lift and carry up to 50 lbs and work from ladders or lifts as required.
Preferred qualifications: Infrared Thermography Level II certification (or higher).
Mission-critical background: Proven track record conducting infrared surveys in high-reliability environments such as enterprise data centers or critical utility infrastructure.
Program development: Hands-on experience establishing or scaling a predictive, condition-based infrared inspection program.
Complex electrical apparatus: In-depth experience assessing switchgear, transformers, uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, automatic transfer switches (ATS), busway, and emergency/standby generation systems.
Electrical safety studies: Working familiarity with arc-flash assessments, equipment incident-energy labeling, and compliance documentation under NFPA 70E.

title: ISE, Incubation - Software Development Engineer - Proactive
description:
We are a creativity-oriented engineering team focused on conceiving and prototyping the future of software on Apple’s devices. We take big, fuzzy ideas about what might be possible and turn them into concrete concepts, prototypes and livable software! We are passionate about exploring new ideas using whatever tools help us make something tangible. Most often, we choose to modify or extend Apple’s existing software using Objective-C or Swift. But we’re open to using the best tools that help us learn: design tools, prototyping apps, ML, etc. We are looking for a creative, learning-oriented, collaborative individual to come help us explore what the future could look like.
Our team nurtures early-stage ideas into well-developed, usable experiences. For this big idea to work, is there a piece of experience that must feel great? Is there an enabling technology we need to build? Software is the tool we use most frequently to bring concepts to life on our devices. But we try to use the best tool for the job: anything that helps us see, touch, or feel an idea. We often work directly with other teams to leverage expertise from across the company, and share our work with others to find out what works and what doesn’t. Gradually, those fuzzy notions turn into tangible, brand-new ideas that can lead the future of software on our devices. The products we build are part prototype, part proof of concept and part sales pitch, so communicating clearly and being able to empathize with other people's perspectives are key skills for our team. So is the ability to give and receive feedback.
Minimum qualifications: 5 years of experience designing for and/or writing software for Apple platforms
3 years experience of creative prototyping in software
Expertise in Swift or Objective-C, or equally strong experience in Python + ML stacks
Preferred qualifications: Able to deal with ambiguity, and a gut instinct for making things that will help bring clarity. We often work on projects where we need to create something to help understand the objectives & boundaries.
A learning mentality and a willingness to try things that may fail. You should be able to learn from both success and failures.
A sense for effective design. If you have design training or design experience, even better.
Ability to communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical teams
Background in either machine learning or HCI
PhD in computer science or a related field

title: Image Quality Engineer - Camera and Photos
description:
The iPhone camera is cherished worldwide because it captures life’s most meaningful
moments with unmatched fidelity and artistry. Our team is dedicated to pushing those
boundaries even further.
The Image Quality Qualification team is seeking an exceptional engineer who combines deep
technical acumen in imaging science with an artistic eye for photography and cinematography.
Hands-on capture and testing are central to this role: you will spend meaningful time in the
field, shooting with pre-release devices much as customers do, and applying your technical
expertise to explore and assess specific image quality artifacts. In this role, you will help shape
the future of visual capture across Apple products—driving continuous innovation in photo and
video quality and delivering extraordinary visual experiences to hundreds of millions of users
around the globe.
As an Image Quality Engineer, you will sit at the intersection of art and engineering, working
cross-functionally to evaluate, refine, and champion next-generation camera features and
computational photography pipelines. You will design and execute rigorous experimental
studies—both within state-of-the-art laboratory environments and in the field, across a variety
of real-world scenes, lighting conditions, and environments—to validate cutting-edge
algorithms and imaging architectures.
A notable part of your work will involve taking devices into the field to recreate authentic user
captures, thoughtfully targeting specific image quality artifacts, and sharing your assessments
with the team. You can look forward to regular hands-on capture and testing, with occasional
travel.
Your insights and critical eye will directly influence technologies such as Portrait mode,
advanced video workflows, and emerging capture methodologies. Working within a high-
energy, collaborative, and fast-paced team, you will turn complex subjective perceptions into
actionable engineering feedback, ensuring every feature meets Apple’s exacting standards for
image excellence.
Minimum qualifications: Experience with hands-on field capture and testing of photo and video features, and enthusiasm for spending time shooting on location.
Deep practical knowledge of camera systems and core 3A behaviors (Auto Exposure, Auto Focus, Auto White Balance) in laboratory and real-world environments.
Refined visual sensibility and deep technical fluency in photography, videography, and cinematography, paired with an instinctive understanding of the elements of exceptional visual storytelling.
Solid grounding in the Human Visual System (HVS) and the perceptual psychophysics governing how real-world scenes translate into perceived image fidelity.
Hands-on proficiency operating and calibrating benchtop optical instrumentation, studio lighting, standard test charts, and specialized imaging lab equipment.
B.S. or M.S. in Imaging Science, Color Science, Vision Science, Optical Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience, with 3+ years of industry experience in imaging or camera systems.
Preferred qualifications: Proven proficiency in Python or MATLAB for scientific computing, image processing pipelines, data visualization, and test automation.
Direct experience conducting both subjective psychophysical user studies and objective image quality metrics (e.g., MTF/SFR, color accuracy/ΔE, SNR/noise profiling, dynamic range, and tone reproduction).
Comprehensive understanding of end-to-end camera architectures, spanning sensor physics, lens optics, Image Signal Processors (ISP), and modern computational photography frameworks.
Superb written, visual, and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to foster collaboration across multidisciplinary hardware, software, and creative teams.

description:

title: Software Developement Manager, Apple Services Engineering
description:
The Apple Services Engineering (ASE) team builds the container and virtualization runtime technology that powers Apple's next-generation compute platform. We're a fast-moving, highly skilled team of systems engineers designing and developing the virtualization-based runtimes that run Virtual Machines and Linux Containers across our data center, with privacy, security, and performance as first-class requirements.
We're starting a new team focused on one question: how do we patch the node software across our datacenter fleet faster, and more often, with minimal impact to the workloads running on it? We're looking for a domain expert to decide the approach and then build and lead the team that delivers it.
Today, updating a node's software means choosing between speed and workload impact. This team's job is to remove that tradeoff, so we can patch the fleet faster and more often with minimal impact on users. We have not chosen an approach. Live migration, snapshot and restore, kexec-based host updates, live patching, and in-place upgrade of the runtime and VMM are all options, and a different approach may fit better than any of them. We are looking for an expert to decide and guide: which approach, or combination, gets us there, what it costs in workload impact and operational risk, and how we measure the result.
You will:
* Define the fleet patching strategy: evaluate the candidate approaches (including ones we haven't listed), choose, and make the tradeoffs explicit, grounded in a model of how each one fails.
* Set the metrics that matter, such as guest-visible downtime, total migration time, network amplification, abortability, and time to patch the fleet.
* Design and drive the first implementation, building on Cloud Hypervisor and our Linux microVM runtimes on x86 and arm64.
* Hire and grow the team. Depending on your background and interests this is a technical-lead role or a people-management role, and we will decide that together.
* Work with the SRE, Compute, and security organizations on rollout, safety, and fleet operations.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, or equivalent related experience.
At least 8+ years of software design and development experience in infrastructure engineering (compute, storage and network virtualization).
Deep, demonstrated experience in one of the following, and working fluency in the other:
* Operating live migration, live patching, or kexec-style host updates across a production fleet, including the failures: non-convergence, aborts and rollback, and fleet-wide rollout safety.
* Building live migration, snapshot/restore, or device-state serialization inside a hypervisor or VMM (for example QEMU/KVM, Cloud Hypervisor, Firecracker, Xen, or Hyper-V).

title: Vision Display, Optical Module Engineer
description:
Do something different! Apple is seeking a creative and dedicated Optical Module Engineer to contribute to the definition and delivery of innovative optical technologies for Apple’s next-generation vision display products. A successful candidate will possess exceptional technical skills and strong communication and leadership abilities to collaborate effectively with various Apple internal cross-functional teams and external suppliers.
In this role, you will be instrumental in defining critical optical module performance and integration requirements, developing key display features, and implementing effective testing and calibration strategies. Additionally, you will support the module development process from prototype to mass production.
This position provides you with a unique opportunity to translate key product requirements into hardware and features essential for delivering exceptional optical solutions and experiences across Apple’s next-generation products.
Define optical module and feature requirements, including prototype and validation strategies for future Apple vision display products.
Leverage lab equipment to demonstrate display user experience and tradeoffs to key decision makers
Develop integrated simulations and budgets to allocate key user experience figures of merit across multiple component requirements
Support daily activities related to build execution, module setup, data analysis, module failure analysis, and system integration.
Facilitate technical discussions with vendors and internal cross-functional teams.
Collaborate to establish optical module test and calibration requirements.
Foster innovation and introduce new technologies to enhance Apple’s vision display performance and user experience.
Utilize early hardware prototypes to propose solutions and conduct comprehensive trade-off analysis.
Effectively communicate the advantages, disadvantages, and risks to the broader team.
Minimum qualifications: B.S., M.S. or Ph.D. in Optics, EE, Physics, or a related field
4+ years of experience in the relevant industry
Experience in one or more of the following areas: optical design or architecture definition for augmented reality (AR) or virtual reality (VR); display module requirement definition, design, and integration; display/system architecture; optical characterization; numerical modeling; image/video processing and machine learning; human and visual perception; and psychophysical studies.
Preferred qualifications: Experience in one or more of the following areas: development of optical module architectures from concept phase to MP; display technologies (e.g. µOLED, µLED); vendor management and multi-functional collaboration; optical simulation (ZEMAX, LightTools); software/algorithm development, programming (Python, Matlab); display pipeline optimization.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
Strong communication and leadership abilities.

title: WW Sales Finance - Financial Analyst

This person will manage the sales forecast and story of a full line of business — owning and speaking to demand trends, promotions, key supply considerations, insights by market, earnings considerations, and additional topics pertaining to sales performance. This person will support Apple’s growth, both top and bottom line, by applying the same level of innovation toward financial matters as we do toward our products and services.
Minimum qualifications: 3+ years of professional experience in a quantitative or statistical field required including strategic or sales finance, product related engineering, etc.
Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Finance, or another quantitative field.
Preferred qualifications: Passion for Apple’s products and mission.
Advanced spreadsheet, modeling, and analytical skills.
Ability to think tactically and strategically, while executing to a clear plan.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As part of our Member Experience team, you will own quality assurance and training for our frontline support team. You'll make sure every member who reaches out to Base gets accurate, clear, and empathetic help, no matter who picks up. This role blends program ownership with hands-on coaching. You'll build the scorecards, curriculum, and feedback loops that help new agents ramp quickly and help tenured agents keep getting better. You will use data, member feedback, and direct observation to find what's working and fix what isn't, so quality holds up as our member base grows.

 

What You’ll Do

 - Quality assurance scorecard – Build and maintain rubrics across phone, email, chat, and text that measure accuracy, empathy, and resolution.

 - Interaction reviews – Build and maintain a structured program for you and team leads to review a consistent sample of member interactions for every agent every week, leveraging AI to build systems as needed.

 - Calibration – Run regular calibration sessions with team leads and others, so every reviewer grades to the same standard. Manage the process for agents to ask questions about or dispute their scores.

 - Coaching and feedback – Turn QA results into agent-shareable scores and specific, actionable coaching feedback. Partner with team leads on 1:1s and performance improvement plans, and give agents clear, kind feedback they can act on.

 - New hire onboarding – Design and run training for new agents, from classroom learning to shadowing to nesting to self-sufficiency. Set clear ramp milestones and certify agents before they work independently.

 - Ongoing training – Build continuing education for the whole team: refreshers, product and policy updates, and advanced skills like de-escalation and handling hard conversations. Track completion and measure whether training changes results.

 - Knowledge management – Keep the knowledge base, standard operating procedures (SOPs), call guides, and saved reply templates accurate and current. Make sure agents always know where to find the right answer.

 - Metrics and reporting – Track and report on QA scores, member satisfaction (CSAT), first contact resolution (FCR), and new hire ramp time. Connect QA findings to member outcomes and share trends with leadership.

 - Root cause analysis – Find patterns in QA results and member feedback. Separate training gaps from process, tooling, and product issues, and drive the fix at the source.

 - Compliance and risk – Make sure agents follow policies on contracts, billing, and disclosures. Flag risks early and escalate them to Legal and Finance.

 - Voice of the member – Share what you see in member interactions to help shape better experiences, services, and policies across the company.

 - Launch readiness – Partner with other teams so agents are trained and ready before new policies, features, and launches reach members.

 

What You'll Bring

 - 2-8+ years of experience in quality assurance, training, or enablement for a customer support, contact center, or customer success team.

 - Hands-on experience building QA scorecards, running calibration sessions, and turning review results into coaching plans.

 - Experience designing and delivering training, including new hire onboarding and ongoing skill development.

 - Coaching skills that change behavior: direct, kind, and specific feedback that agents trust.

 - Comfort with data. You can analyze QA scores, CSAT, FCR, and NPS, then turn what you find into clear recommendations.

 - Comfort owning outcomes end-to-end, as motivated to fix the root cause as to improve the individual interaction.

 - Strong writing skills with excellent grammar, tone, and clarity for training materials, SOPs, and feedback.

 - Confidence facilitating, from 1:1 coaching sessions to full-team trainings.

 - Tech savvy, with experience in help desk platforms, QA tools, learning management systems, and knowledge bases, and a knack for quickly mastering new ones.

 - Not afraid to get on the front line. You'll listen to calls, read tickets, and take contacts yourself to understand what agents face.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and a fast-paced environment to quickly adapt to changes.

 - Team player motivated by the mission who always puts the company's best interests first.

You’ll help build the warehouse operation that powers Base’s expansion into Connecticut — setting the standard for how materials move, how inventory is managed, and how the floor operates as we scale. Founded in 2017 with dual headquarters in Chicago and Tokyo, CADDi serves manufacturing leaders across more than 20 countries. We are expanding our North American operations rapidly and building next-generation products like CADDi Explorer and CADDi Agent. If you are eager to solve hard data and engineering problems while scaling a fast-growing unicorn, we’d love to talk.

As a Deployment Partner, you own a customer from first discovery through a live, adopted workflow, and then through expansion across the enterprise. You work directly with the people who run the plant floor, procurement, quality, and engineering from operational management up to the C-suite deciding where AI fits in their business.
You work with the CADDi AI Data Platform and suite of workflow-specific products a configurable tool you capitalize on for each customer. You are accountable for their success end-to-end: time-to-value, the deployment of the solutions we promised, the measurable value they see enterprise-wide, and the renewal that follows.

Understand the customer

Meet with cross-functional teams across engineering, procurement, quality, and operations onsite as needed to learn how they work and where time and money are lost.
Advise customer leaders, from operational management to the C-suite, on where AI and a shared data foundation create the most value, and agree on what success means for their business.

Bring what you see in the field back to Product and Engineering so it shapes the roadmap, and return reusable configurations and learnings to the shared library so the next deployment is faster.

Job Description
The AVP, Architecture (Retail Solutions) provides executive-level leadership over the architecture function for the Retail portfolio within Cox Automotive. This role is accountable for defining and executing the Retail portfolio technology strategy, driving solution and technical architecture across retail-facing value streams, and ensuring alignment with enterprise technology standards and governance. The AVP leads a team of Solution Architects and Technical Architects who design and evolve the platforms, capabilities, and integrations that power Cox Automotive's retail dealer and consumer experiences.
This leader partners closely with Retail portfolio product and engineering leadership, Enterprise Architecture, and cross-functional stakeholders to connect retail solutions to the broader Vehicle Lifecycle vision, lower cost to build through platform reuse, and embed AI capabilities into retail products.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership
Define and own the Retail Portfolio Technology Strategy, including platform capabilities, adoption goals per product, and value stream architecture roadmaps.
Oversee the entirety of architectural design, investment planning, development, and implementation for the Retail portfolio.
Establish long-range strategic direction and roadmaps for the current state and evolution of retail technology infrastructure, including dealer-facing and consumer-facing platforms.
Drive the rationalization of duplicate platforms within the Retail portfolio, setting adoption targets and retirement timelines aligned with enterprise goals.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture to ensure Retail strategies operate within enterprise guardrails while optimizing for portfolio-specific outcomes.
Architecture and Design
Lead the architecture of key Retail portfolio capabilities, including: Dealer & Partner Organization Management, Common Dealer Experience (Command Center), Retail Dealer Reporting Platform, Consumer Management (Connected Customer), Retail 3rd Party Data Curation, Dealer Communications, R360 Workflow Strategy/Governance, Retail Agentic Platform (Journey State, Context, Ontology, Tools Catalog, UX, Policies/Governance), and Retail Deal (DealXG, Payment Services).
Direct the design and development of technology products, services, standards, and best practices for retail solutions.
Ensure designs are consistent with enterprise implementation standards and in conformance with network, capacity, security, and data governance plans.
Evaluate and consult with leaders on technical operations, strategic planning of architecture, system operations, and product development, configuration, and deployment.
Governance and Standards
Define and enforce Portfolio-level policies and standards that operate within Enterprise Architecture guardrails.
Participate in the Architecture Council to support strategy cascade, standards alignment, exception management, and scorecard reporting.
Escalate enterprise-level exceptions through proper governance channels.
Oversee adoption tracking and compliance within the Retail portfolio against both enterprise and portfolio standards.
Team Leadership and Talent Development
Lead and develop a team of Value Stream Architects, Solution Architects, and Technical Architects aligned to Retail release trains.
Raise architecture capability through the engineering skills framework; mentor and coach architecture talent.
Ensure every value stream has a named architecture lead; manage quarterly capacity rebalancing.
Maintain program-level and executive sponsorship responsibility for all Retail Architecture initiatives.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Partner with Enterprise Architecture on large, multi-stream initiatives and cross-portfolio integration design.
Collaborate with the CISO on security architecture and the CDO on data strategy for retail platforms.
Work with business leaders, legal, and other stakeholders to define data, infrastructure, and related governance standards.
Drive AI adoption within retail products in alignment with the enterprise AI risk framework and shared AI capabilities.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field with 14+ years of relevant experience, including at least 7 years in a leadership role. Or, an equivalent combination of education and work-related experience.
Master’s degree with 12+ years of relevant experience, including leadership experience, may be substituted.
Preferred
Experience in automotive retail technology, dealer management systems, or consumer digital platforms.
Deep expertise in enterprise and solution architecture, including cloud-native design, API-first strategies, and platform modernization.
Proven track record of leading large-scale platform rationalization and technology consolidation efforts.
Experience with AI/ML integration into product architectures and agentic platform design.
Strong understanding of data governance, integration patterns, and security architecture.

Vacuum interior, scrub, shampoo and spot clean carpet and upholstery. Straighten seatbelts.
Clean glove box making sure that warranty booklet, owner's manual and other manufacturer issued information is returned.
Visibly demonstrate safety commitment by following all safety and health procedures and modeling the behaviors related to such. Actively participate in support of all safety activities aligned with Safety Excellence.

Job Description
*** If you have any questions or to connect with a recruiter while your application is being reviewed, please Text DFS2 to 317-597-8130 ***
Cox Fleet keeps your fleet moving!
As a Cox Automotive business, Cox Fleet delivers integrated uptime solutions designed to reduce downtime, improve fleet performance, and keep drivers safely on the road. Our nationwide operation combines more than 1,500 skilled technicians, 30+ company-operated service centers, and a network of over 65,000 service providers, all supported by 24/7/365 operational coordination. Together, we provide maintenance, repair, and fleet support services for equipment ranging from Class 8 trucks and 53-foot trailers to light-duty vehicles.
Cox Fleet is currently hiring a Lead Mobile Diesel/Trailer Technician. The Lead Mobile Diesel and Trailer Technician serves in a dual-role capacity, balancing master-level technical responsibilities in the field with operational support duties and technical leadership skills development. This role is designed for high-performing technicians who aspire to grow into future leadership or operational positions while continuing to serve as a critical technical resource for the team. In addition to performing advanced diagnostics, complex repairs, DOT inspections, and preventive maintenance, the Lead Mobile and Trailer Diesel Technician partners closely with the Mobile Technician Manager (MTM) to support quality control inspections, technician technical coaching and development, Cox Fleet PM and telematics compliance, inventory and parts reconciliation, estimate workflows, customer engagement, and other operational initiatives that drive market performance, efficiency, safety, and operational excellence. The Lead Mobile Diesel and Trailer Technician also participates in a structured leadership development program, gaining hands-on training in people leadership, business operations, and performance management while serving as a key pipeline for future operational and leadership opportunities.
OPERATIONAL DUTIES:
Partner with the Mobile Technician Manager (MTM) to support market-level operational initiatives designed and directed by the MTM to improve team performance, productivity, efficiency, safety, and customer satisfaction
Support technician onboarding and development efforts by demonstrating and training on company processes, workflows, safety standards, and operational best practices.
Participate in customer meetings, operational reviews, and account support activities, serving as a technical and operational representative of Cox Fleet when appropriate.
Support the Mobile Technician Manager (MTM) in conducting Quality Control Inspections (QCIs) and share technical observation on repair quality, workmanship, and compliance on work completed by Mobile Diesel Technicians I/II/Sr. Provide coaching and training to technicians, at the MTMs direction.
Provide guidance and support to Mobile Diesel Technicians I/II/Sr with inventory management best practices, inventory reconciliation activities, and proper tracking of parts, tools, and service truck inventories to ensure accuracy and operational efficiency
Support PM and telematics compliance initiatives within the team by working closely with the Mobile Technician Manager (MTM) to maintain fleet readiness and ensure compliance with company standards.
Provide technical mentorship, knowledge sharing, and skill support to Mobile Diesel Technicians I/II/Sr. and also Entry-Level Apprentices, in coordination with the MTM to help drive technical skill progression.
Model established workflows and best practices expected of the Mobile Diesel Technicians I/II/Sr. and also Entry-Level Apprentices, along with bringing opportunities to the MTM around process improvement opportunities that enhance service quality, technician effectiveness, and overall market performance.
Provide the MTM and support teams with technical and field information that assists with scheduling, workflow coordination, and service execution.
Participate in a structured leadership-readiness program covering leadership principles, business operations, performance-coaching concepts, and process improvement in preparation for potential future leadership opportunities.
MECHANICAL DUTIES:
Diagnose, adjust and repair various types of truck equipment, including but not limited to: electrical/brake/cooling systems, starters/alternators, AC systems, fan clutches, engine electronics, diesel steering systems, gas and diesel engines, manual and automatic transmissions, clutches, differentials, etc.
Perform scheduled preventative maintenance inspections (“PMIs”), DOT Inspections and follow up repairs on light, medium and heavy-duty vehicles in a mobile/field environment.
Use hand tools, precision instruments, lift and jacks, welding equipment, diagnostic tools, technology and testing equipment, such as handheld computers and pressure gauges, to inspect, test and troubleshoot vehicle systems.
Road test vehicles to identify issues, verify repairs and ensure they are operating safely and properly.
Document completed work (including required DOT forms and service documentation), parts used and repair order findings accurately and on time using company-issued hand-held device.
Follow an assigned daily schedule with a degree of independence, effectively managing multiple concurrent tasks while exercising sound judgment to prioritize work activities and allocate time efficiently in accordance with established procedures and guidelines

description:
About the Team
Symbiosys , a company DoorDash acquired in 2025, helps retailers grow their advertising businesses by enabling brands to reach shoppers across digital channels like Google, Meta, TikTok, Criteo, and DoorDash Storefront. As part of DoorDash’s advertising business, Symbiosys extends advertising capabilities beyond the DoorDash app, helping retailers and brands connect with consumers across more of their shopping journey.
We combine the pace and ownership of a startup with the resources of DoorDash. It’s a fast-moving environment where priorities evolve and everyone has the opportunity to make an impact. People who thrive here are proactive, resourceful, and comfortable with ambiguity - taking initiative, bringing solutions, and following through as we grow.
Our Retailer Success team works closely with Retail Partners, Advertisers, Operations, and Engineering to support campaign execution, deliver actionable insights, and build strong partner relationships.
About the Role
As an Account Manager, Retailer Success, you will manage day-to-day retailer relationships and help partners grow adoption of our platform and scale their advertising businesses. You’ll support campaigns from planning and launch through reporting and optimization, while also coordinating go-to-market activities, gathering and tracking product roadmap requests, and triaging escalations. You’ll work closely with Ad Ops, Product, and Engineering to address retailer needs, resolve issues, and keep key initiatives moving forward.
This role is a great fit for someone with 2–5 years of relevant experience who enjoys working with clients, digging into data, and coordinating multiple projects across teams. You will report directly to the Senior Manager of Retailer Success.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Serve as a day-to-day point of contact for retailer partners, helping address their needs and keeping requests, questions, and priorities moving forward.
Support retailer onboarding and platform adoption through training, resources, and ongoing guidance on features and workflows.
Coordinate go-to-market activities, including launch plans, partner materials, and advertiser enablement, to help retailers grow participation in their advertising programs.
Support campaign planning, setup, launch, reporting, and optimization in partnership with retailers.
Monitor campaign pacing, performance, and platform adoption to identify issues and recommend opportunities for improvement or growth.
Gather retailer feedback and product requests, document business needs, and work with Engineering to communicate priorities and track roadmap updates.
Triage retailer escalations, gather relevant details, and coordinate with Engineering to support resolution and keep partners informed.
Prepare performance reports and business updates that clearly communicate results, open items, and next steps.
Maintain accurate account plans, request trackers, and documentation to keep internal and client teams aligned and ensure follow-through.
We’re excited about you because…
You bring 2–5 years of experience in account management, client success, campaign management, or a related role in digital advertising, retail media, or adtech.
You have experience supporting digital advertising campaigns and are familiar with platforms such as Google, Meta, DSPs, or retailer advertising platforms.
You understand core advertising metrics, budget pacing, and campaign performance, and can turn data into clear observations and recommendations.
You’re comfortable using Excel or Google Sheets to organize information, analyze performance, and maintain accurate trackers.
You communicate clearly and professionally with clients and internal teams, including when explaining results or coordinating next steps.
You’re organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple accounts, deadlines, and shifting priorities.
You take ownership of your work, follow through on commitments, and know when to ask for help or escalate an issue.
You’re curious about retail media and eager to build your platform knowledge and account management skills.
