In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for sales commission. Talk to your recruiter for more information.

title: Kitchen Manager, DashMart
description:
About the Team
We're looking for someone to help scale DoorDash's next billion dollar business, DashMart, by growing our in-house food program, DashMart Kitchens. The DashMart Kitchens team is focused on building a new type of restaurant platform within DashMart, offering a broad selection of prepared foods and well-known restaurant staples to our customers' doorsteps.
About the Role
As the Kitchen Manager for DashMart Kitchens (DMK), you’ll lead the daily operations of a DoorDash-owned kitchen located within a DashMart fulfillment center. You’ll oversee a team of operations associates and shift leads to ensure every meal is prepared safely, efficiently, and to the highest quality standards.
You’ll combine hands-on culinary leadership with operational excellence — managing staffing, scheduling, and kitchen performance while ensuring food safety, order accuracy, and team success. You’ll work closely with your Site Manager to lead multiple food concepts, improve processes, and create a great place to work. This role requires strict adherence to food safety, inventory controls, and safety protocols due to routine access to food, supplies, equipment, and operational systems.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you...
Thrive on iteration and have experience leading teams through changes
Are excited about coaching, managing, and leading teams in fast-paced environments
Enjoy building systems and processes and seeing ideas come to life
Are eager to learn how different parts of a complex operation connect
Are obsessed with preparing consistent, high-quality food for customers
Want to grow in delivery-only kitchen operations
You’ll Make an Impact By...
Leading: You’ll demonstrate compassion and commitment to inclusivity as you lead a team of hourly Kitchen Operations Associates and Shift Leads. You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. Because this position supervises staff and is responsible for maintaining a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace, strong adherence to professional conduct, clear communication, and employee safety standards is required. You’ll serve as a leading change agent for your DMK, helping your team to navigate new food concepts and growth projects. You’ll tackle onsite escalations, including coordination with cross-functional partners.
Operating and Building Systems: With your thumb on the pulse of all outcomes for your team, you will be directly responsible for driving results for your kitchen. To achieve your performance targets, you’ll drive success by building, implementing, and improving systems for effective scheduling, ensuring par levels are met, executing recipes accurately, and deploying best practices.Because this role oversees high-risk kitchen equipment and fast-paced food production, maintaining sound judgment and unimpaired performance is essential to ensure a safe work environment. You’ll engage cross-functional partners within DoorDash as needed for support.
Strategizing: You will analyze performance metrics, identify root causes of issues like prep gaps or order quality, and implement solutions that drive efficiency and adoption. You will refine processes, and partner with your Site Manager and cross-functional teams to execute new initiatives and continuously improve how the kitchen operates.
Delighting: You care deeply about delivering great food and a great customer experience. You will coach your team to maintain recipe accuracy, food safety, and storefront availability, knowing that consistency is key in a multi-concept kitchen. You will collaborate with central teams so your site has the tools, training, and support needed to achieve excellent quality outcomes.
We’re excited about you because…
You have 3+ years of experience in a medium/high-volume fast-casual or full-service restaurant environment.
You have 2+ years of experience leading teams, including hiring, scheduling, coaching, and performance management.
You hold (or are willing to get) a ServeSafe Manager certification and set high standards for food safety and cleanliness.
You’re a hands-on leader who motivates teams of 5+ employees to perform and grow.
You take ownership and thrive in fast-changing, startup-style environments where no task is too big or small.

location: San Francisco, CA; Sunnyvale, CA; Seattle, WA
description:
About the Team
The Market Optimization team builds decision systems that help DoorDash invest in Dasher supply where it creates the greatest marketplace value. Market Optimizer brings together supply forecasts, causal response models, and constrained optimization to inform spending across acquisition, pay, and incentives. We work with the teams that own these levers to improve delivery speed and reliability while managing cost and supporting a healthy Dasher marketplace.
About the Role
We are looking for a hands-on technical leader to advance the causal models and production systems behind Mobilization. You will help answer where and when to offer incentives, how much to offer, and how long they should run. You will estimate the additional supply these decisions create and translate those estimates into dependable policies with Engineering, Product, Analytics, and Operations.
You are excited about this opportunity because you will
Build and calibrate response curves that estimate how incentive amount, timing, duration, and location affect incremental Dasher hours and marketplace outcomes.
Connect causal estimates and supply forecasts to constrained optimization, balancing delivery outcomes, incentive cost, and uncertainty across markets and time periods.
Design learning experiments and evaluation plans with Analytics. Account for marketplace spillovers, supply shifting between nearby areas or time periods, and interactions with other incentives.
Develop policies that direct spending toward periods when additional supply creates the most marketplace value, accounting for diminishing returns and non-linear delivery outcomes.
Own models through production deployment, calibration, monitoring, and incident diagnosis. Build diagnostics that explain policy changes and surface model or data regressions.
We are excited about you because you have
5+ years of experience developing causal inference or causal ML systems, with a record of using the results to change production decisions.
A record of leading ambiguous projects across team boundaries, making technical tradeoffs explicit, and developing other engineers.
Strong statistical judgment about randomized experiments and observational estimation, including confounding, treatment overlap, uncertainty, and the limits of causal claims.
Experience with treatment effect estimation or dose-response modeling and relevant methods such as doubly robust estimation, double machine learning, or off-policy evaluation. You choose methods based on the decision and available evidence.
Strong software and ML engineering skills. You can build reliable data and training pipelines, write maintainable production code, and diagnose failures across models and services.
Experience connecting models to constrained optimization, pricing, or resource allocation, and assessing how estimation errors affect production decisions.
The ability to explain modeling assumptions and incentive recommendations to partners who need to act on them.

Within Strategy & Operations, Dasher & Logistics is made up of teams that each own part of this system, such as Network Strategy, US Markets, Regulated Markets, Canada, Supply, Pay & Efficiency, and Live Ops. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Analytics, Finance, Marketing, and Operations to run and improve one of the largest last-mile logistics networks in the world.

We’re hiring a Senior Manager, Strategy & Operations to own a meaningful part of the Dasher & Logistics network end-to-end. Depending on the team, that could be how we invest in Dasher supply, the health of every US market, our most complex regulated markets, or the delivery network for an entire country. You will find where the network underperforms, design and test the fix, and work with Product and Engineering to build it into how the network runs. You will make tradeoff decisions across Dasher earnings, consumer experience, merchant reliability, and unit economics, and bring clear recommendations to senior leadership. title: Senior Full Stack & Platform Engineer
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
About Compass
Compass is a new venture incubated within MISUMI Americas. We’re building it with the deep manufacturing expertise of Fictiv, MISUMI’s digital manufacturing platform.
Every physical product starts as a CAD model, and most of what it will cost is decided right there. Yet cost and manufacturability are still checked after the drawings are released, by hand and in spreadsheets, when every change is slow and expensive. The result is redesigns, missed schedules, and money left on the factory floor. Compass fixes that at the source. An engineer uploads an assembly, and Compass reads every part the way an expert manufacturing engineer would. It checks each feature against the processes that could make it, prices the part at the volume that matters, reads tolerances and GD&T straight off the drawing, and ranks exactly what to change. It does this across the entire bill of materials, reruns on every revision, and learns from every correction engineers make.
The problems underneath are genuinely hard: making sense of real-world geometry, modeling cost across machining, casting, molding, sheet metal, and additive, interpreting engineering drawings, and building AI that gets measurably better from expert feedback. The stakes are real, too. Our customers are enterprise engineering teams, including aerospace and defense programs, where the platform has to be as secure and trustworthy as it is smart. Compass is a small team that moves fast and gives engineers real ownership. You won’t inherit a finished system. You’ll help define the architecture, the security foundation, and the product that the most demanding customers in manufacturing will rely on.
About the Role
We’re looking for a cross-functional software engineer who thrives at the intersection of application development and cloud infrastructure. description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form Energy is seeking a Cell Teardown Technician to support critical lab activities that enhance the robustness and reliability of our iron-air battery products. As part of the Core Technology Hardware Team, you will contribute to failure analysis efforts through battery cell teardowns, failure data collection, and post-teardown sample preparation and processing. This role requires hands-on work in the lab and close collaboration with a cross-functional team to ensure high-quality failure data documentation. This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission!




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Perform hands-on lab work to disassemble cycled battery cells and support failure analysis using various handheld power tools.

 - Document teardown observations of electrode components and record failure modes to inform battery design and build improvements.

 - Prepare post-teardown electrode samples using machine tools and perform sample processing in a wet lab environment for material characterization essential to failure analysis.

 - Maintain lab tools and equipment, and ensure an organized, efficient workspace.

 - Champion lab safety by following and promoting best practices.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - 2+ years experience as a lab technician or in a hands-on technician role with chemicals, mechanics or battery products.

 - Strong teamwork skills and collaborative mindset.

 - Demonstrate attention to detail in documentation and execution of tasks.

 - Experience in using and maintaining handheld power tools and lab instruments.

 - Ability to lift up to 30 lbs.

 - Comfortable working with chemicals and wearing personal protective equipment (PPE).

 - A positive, solution-oriented mindset with a drive to get things done!

title: Head of Sales
description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the role
As Head of Sales, you'll own Formic's sales strategy, execution, team performance, and revenue generation results. Your responsibility is to grow and manage a high-performing sales organization that consistently wins new business while concurrently growing and expanding within existing customers.
We're looking for a commercially astute builder who knows how to turn complex customer needs into successful sales. You'll develop a sharp understanding of manufacturers, their operational challenges, and the economics of automation, then use customer insights and performance data to strengthen targeting, sales execution, and growth. You'll be responsible for helping to identify what is working, change what isn’t, and implement effective practices to drive sales success.
You'll lead and develop our Sales team, identifying what makes our best customer engagements and salespeople successful and turning those insights into better coaching, stronger qualification, higher conversion, and more consistent performance. You’ll leverage data and insights derived from Formic’s range of GTM tools and tech stack, customer feedback, and feedback from other Formic teams (i.e Customer Success, Solutions, Service, etc.) to continuously improve the sales process and methodologies to better align with unmet customer need and desired outcomes.  You'll stay close to important deals and help the team navigate operational, financial, and technical stakeholders with confidence.
This is a hands-on leadership role requiring a combination of strategic judgment, direct & active team management, and tactical execution. You'll challenge assumptions, make decisions grounded in data and customer insights, prototype, test, iterate, and ultimately implement changes, and measure their impact quantitatively and qualitatively. Working across the business, you'll build a more effective, predictable, and scalable sales organization.
What You'll Do
Sales strategy and execution
Own sales targets, territory strategy, account prioritization, and revenue performance. Establish clear standards for opportunity ownership, workload distribution, response times, pipeline progression, and follow-through; proactively resolve stalled opportunities, capacity constraints, and performance gaps.
Study target producers and manufacturers, applications, buying processes, and competitive alternatives to focus effort on the best opportunities.
Improve discovery, qualification, business cases, proposals, negotiations, and closing; participate directly in high-stakes deals.
Personally own and drive select sales opportunities each quarter to maintain firsthand knowledge of our customers, product, and sales process.
Establish rapid iteration and testing of new or modified sales approaches and tactics, accounting for differences in regions, markets, and application verticals
Balance customer value, pricing, profitability, technical feasibility, and deployment requirements when evaluating opportunities.
Sales leadership and coaching
Build and lead a disciplined sales management organization. Recruit, develop, and hold accountable sellers and managers; equip regional leads with clear expectations, performance metrics, coaching practices, and the skills to develop their teams while maintaining their own commercial effectiveness.
Use call observation, deal reviews, customer feedback, and performance data to understand why individuals and deals succeed or stall.
Translate top-performer practices into repeatable training, targeted coaching, and stronger team-wide performance.
Validate impacts and results of training, coaching, and enablement to ensure the team’s performance is quantitatively improving as a result.
Sales operations and collaboration
Build reliable forecasting, CRM discipline, meaningful metrics, and operating routines that surface opportunities and risks early.
Improve sales processes, tools, reporting, and resource allocation; test changes and measure their impact.
Establish a disciplined operating partnership with Marketing and Sales Development, jointly refining the ideal customer profile, account priorities, qualification standards, opportunity handoffs, sales follow-through, and feedback from won and lost deals to improve pipeline quality and conversion.
Coordinate with Solutions, Engineering, Operations, and Customer Success on feasibility, customer commitments, and handoffs. Own commercial execution for expansion within existing accounts, partnering with Customer Success to surface whitespace, prioritize opportunities, and ensure accountable follow-through.
What makes you a great fit
Curiosity and a demonstrated desire to learn and serve customers
Demonstrated success building sales capabilities, operating rhythms, and team performance in a growing B2B business, including driving process change and improvements while ensuring existing momentum is maintained
Exceptional coach who diagnoses performance gaps and helps people improve through direct feedback and practical training.
Experience leading consultative sales of complex technical or operational solutions, navigating plant-level stakeholders, financial decision-makers, implementation considerations, and extended sales cycles.
Strong analytical and commercial judgment, including pipeline analysis, forecasting, deal economics, and Salesforce or similar CRM tools.
Hands-on, resourceful leader who can build processes, recruit talent, make difficult decisions, and close important deals.
Experience selling hardware or equipment into manufacturing operations is a plus.
What we look for:
We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!
Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.
Create the Magic: You absorb complexity so customers don’t have to. Whether your customer is external or internal, you focus on delivering experiences that are clear, fast, value-added, and outcome-driven. You don’t say “not my job.” You make things work.
Today, Not Tomorrow: You have a bias to action. You close the loop. You take extreme ownership. You understand that speed compounds, and you don’t confuse activity with results.
Seek Truth: You think from first principles. You value data over ego and strong opinions loosely held. You’re willing to challenge assumptions, including your own, in pursuit of the best answer.
Made of Rubber: You are resolute and adaptable. When things break or priorities shift, you rebound stronger. You treat setbacks as learning moments and move forward with grit.
One Formic: You operate without silos. You practice radical helpfulness, document clearly, and make clean handoffs. You assume positive intent and prioritize team success over individual credit.
Equal Opportunity Employment:
Formic is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion or religious creed, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, marital status, family or parental status, disability, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. All employment decisions are based on a person’s merit, business needs, and role requirements. If you require further accommodations or have questions regarding accessibility of our roles, please reach out to accessibility@formic.co .
AI Use:
At Formic, fairness and transparency are at the heart of our hiring process. We use AI-powered tools in some interviews to help our teams evaluate candidate responses, but all final hiring decisions are made by humans. You can learn more about how AI is used in our recruitment process by reviewing our AI Hiring Disclosure linked  here .

title: Associate Creative Director- Moen & House of Rohl
description:
Fortune Brands Innovations (NYSE: FBIN) is an industry-leading home, security and digital products company with a portfolio of trusted brands, including Moen, House of Rohl, Therma-Tru, Larson, Master Lock, Yale residential, and Sentry Safe.
We are building a company that is determined to win, and we are clear about how: strong brands, great people, and disciplined execution.
You'll join a team that puts customers first, keeps its commitments, and cuts through complexity to deliver meaningful results.
If you're looking for an opportunity to make an impact and help shape what's next for our iconic brands, we'd love to meet you. Apply now.
Explore life at Fortune Brands here .
We're looking for TWO Associate Creative Directors to join Creative X, the internal creative agency for Moen and House of Rohl at Fortune Brands Innovations, with one position dedicated to each brand. These creative leaders will help define how our brands show up in the world, bringing bold ideas, compelling storytelling, and exceptional creative execution to life. The roles blend creative leadership, conceptual thinking, brand stewardship, and hands-on creative expertise to deliver work that inspires consumers, empowers professional customers, strengthens brand equity, and drives business results across our mass-premium and luxury portfolios.
We're looking for individuals who bring strong creative vision with expertise rooted in art direction, visual storytelling, copywriting, or brand messaging. While each leader may bring different creative strengths, both will be responsible for guiding the overall creative direction across disciplines, ensuring cohesive, impactful work that reflects their brand's distinct identity and positioning.
As an Associate Creative Director, you'll partner closely with Brand, Marketing, and other cross-functional teams to translate business objectives into breakthrough creative ideas. You'll lead creative development from concept through execution, inspire and mentor creative talent, and ensure every customer touchpoint delivers a consistent and compelling brand experience.
PORTFOLIO REQUIRED: Candidates must include a link to their creative portfolio with their application to be considered for this opportunity.
POSITION LOCATION/TRAVEL : This position is based in Deerfield, IL, and follows a hybrid work schedule, with the flexibility to work remotely on Mondays and Fridays.
Travel is approximately 10% and may include attending industry events, creative productions, team meetings, and other business-related activities as needed.
What You'll Do:
Creative Vision & Brand Leadership
Own the art direction vision for Moen and House of Rohl across omnichannel campaigns, setting the visual standard and ensuring all work is cohesive, insight-driven, and aligned with brand strategy.
Lead the development of big-idea creative platforms that translate business goals, consumer insights, and brand positioning into campaigns with lasting impact.
Guide integrated creative teams (art directors, designers, and copywriters) to develop ideas that drive engagement, preference, and conversion.
Champion the premium and luxury positioning of our brands through refined visual systems, photography direction, and uncompromising design excellence.
Serve as the final creative quality gate for art direction before work goes to senior stakeholders.
Strategic & Stakeholder Leadership
Partner with Marketing, Product, and cross-functional leaders to shape briefs and define creative strategy from the outset, not only at execution.
Present and defend creative concepts and visual direction to senior and executive stakeholders with clarity, confidence, and strategic rationale.
Act as a trusted creative advisor to brand leadership, helping teams frame challenges, uncover opportunities, and make confident creative decisions.
Represent Creative X's point of view in planning conversations, balancing creative ambition with business priorities, timelines, and budgets.
Team Leadership & Craft
Directly manage, mentor, and develop creative talent, providing clear direction, constructive critique, and career growth support.
Build a culture of curiosity, craft excellence, collaboration, and accountability across the team.
Guide hiring, resourcing, goal setting, and performance reviews for direct reports to build a high-performing creative team.
Oversee the development of creative assets across disciplines, including design, copywriting, photography, video, and digital content, ensuring consistent quality and execution.
Provide creative direction for major productions, including photo and video shoots, CGI rendering, campaign messaging, and content development, partnering with production teams and external creative vendors.
Drive the evolution of brand guidelines, visual systems, messaging frameworks, and tone of voice to ensure the brand remains modern, consistent, and culturally relevant.
Innovation & Performance
Bring category, cultural, and design trends into the work to strengthen creative impact and relevance.
Lead the team's adoption of GenAI and emerging creative technologies, setting best practices that accelerate ideation, expand exploration, and improve production efficiency.
Partner with production leadership to streamline workflows, optimize resources, and ensure high-quality delivery across all asset types.
Use performance data and learnings to inform creative decisions and continuously improve results.
Bachelor's degree with 8+ years of experience in art direction or visual design within an agency or in-house creative team; OR a high school diploma with 10+ years of relevant experience.
2+ years of direct people management experience, including leading, coaching, and developing art directors and/or designers.
Background in home, lifestyle, design, luxury, or other aesthetically driven categories.
Strong conceptual thinking, visual and verbal storytelling skills, and the ability to translate brand strategy and business objectives into compelling creative work.
Experience developing and executing integrated creative campaigns across digital, social, print, video, and other marketing channels.
Strong understanding of visual design principles, brand identity, copywriting, messaging, and tone of voice, with demonstrated expertise in at least one creative discipline.
Experience leading creative projects, directing multidisciplinary teams, and providing constructive feedback and mentorship to creative talent.
Familiarity with generative AI (GenAI) tools and their application to creative ideation, content development, design, or workflow efficiency, with an understanding of responsible use and brand integrity .
Ability to present and articulate creative concepts and strategic recommendations to stakeholders at various levels.
Portfolio demonstrating strong conceptual thinking, creative excellence, and impactful brand campaigns or experiences.
Nice to Haves
Experience working within an in-house creative agency or external advertising/creative agency.
Experience developing creative for both consumer and professional audiences.
Advanced expertise in art direction, design, copywriting, or brand storytelling, with the ability to guide creative execution across disciplines.
Experience leveraging emerging creative technologies, including GenAI, to enhance creative processes and execution.
Experience balancing brand-building initiatives with performance-driven marketing objectives
Fortune Brands believes in fair and equitable pay. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is Hiring Pay Range: $90,000 USD - $143,000 USD. Are you a marketing leader who can turn a trusted household name into the most-loved brand in the smart home category? The Connected Products Security team at Fortune Brands Innovations is hiring a Director of Marketing for our Yale and August smart lock brands , sold to consumers and to Pro and B2B customers across the US and Canada. Yale and August are trusted names on the door; this leader will make them the brands people choose first, talk about, and stay loyal to.
The Director of Marketing leads marketing for Yale and August across consumer and Pro/B2B channels, reporting to the General Manager of Connected Security. Every responsibility below spans both. We are looking for a growth-minded, data driven brand builder and operator: someone who pairs creative ambition with rigorous measurement, sets clear OKRs, and is equally strong at planning and optimizing a direct media budget, at finding new and unconventional ways to earn attention and customers, and at building product marketing for B2B and Pro channels, where installers, dealers and property managers buy differently from consumers. The Director leads a small team and a group of agency partners, owns the marketing budget, and is accountable for three outcomes: Pro and B2B activation, winning in ecomm and on shelf, and building brand leadership and growing share for Yale and August. The team operates like a startup inside a large company, so the role combines strategy with hands-on execution and you have to be a player coach. The Director will test new channels, formats and partnerships ahead of the category, and will build an agentic marketing team that lets a small group operate at the scale of a much larger one.
POSITION LOCATION:
This position can be based at our global headquarters in Deerfield, Illinois, in San Francisco, California, or remote within the United States.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Strategy, Brand & Team
Set a bold growth strategy, plan and budget for Yale and August, with clear OKRs for revenue, share, activation and brand health, and a clear point of view on where the next wave of customers and revenue will come from.
Define a clear, differentiated brand position and set the creative standard for every campaign, launch and channel, holding internal teams and agencies to it.
Build and grow an agentic marketing team spanning creative, digital, and product and channel marketing for B2C and Pro/B2B, using AI agents for analytics, reporting, content and campaign operations; manage agency partners across media, creative, PR and web.
Brand Growth & Innovation
Build and scale the Yale and August brands in new and innovative ways, going beyond category-standard marketing to earn attention, advocacy and loyalty, and making home security feel personal rather than transactional.
Launch and grow creator, influencer, community and customer-advocacy programs and turn them into a repeatable engine for acquisition and word of mouth.
Build brand partnerships and ecosystem co-marketing with smart home platforms, builders, property managers, insurers and lifestyle brands that open new customer segments and routes to market.
Identify and pilot emerging growth channels and formats (such as social commerce, short-form video, in-store experiences and AI-driven discovery) against clear hypotheses; scale what wins and stop what does not.
Customer Insight & Product Marketing
Own quantitative customer and market insight (behavioral data, surveys, market share and channel data) that focuses Design's qualitative research, and use the combined findings with Product Management to drive product and marketing decisions and measure their results.
Partner with Product Management on the roadmap, portfolio, pricing and category view, representing customer needs, whitespace and competitive differentiation.
Lead launch marketing from concept through post-launch, designing launches that create buzz and drive trial, with value propositions for each audience, from homeowners to installers, dealers, integrators and property managers, and success metrics set before launch.
Measurement & Commercial Performance
Own the marketing OKRs and an integrated scorecard connecting investment to revenue, share, sell-through, ROAS, CAC, conversion and brand metrics; report results to business leadership and hold the team and agencies accountable to them.
Own working media across search, social, retail media, programmatic and CTV, allocating spend based on measured return.
Run a test-and-learn discipline across channels, reserving budget for bold experiments, spotting underperformance early and shifting strategy and spend to what works.
Omnichannel, Ecomm & Retail
Own the omnichannel experience so Yale and August show up consistently across D2C, Amazon, retailer sites, stores and Pro channels.
Drive discovery and conversion through search (SEO, AEO, GEO), ratings and reviews, enhanced content and accurate product data.
Partner with retail, ecomm and Pro sales teams on channel plans, co-op, sales enablement, point-of-purchase and partner activation programs.
Lifecycle & Content
Turn Design's customer journey plans into lifecycle programs that drive measurable device activation and engagement, and turn customers into loyal advocates through onboarding, referral and loyalty programs.
Set content priorities and an AI-first production model so every channel gets the right content on time.
10+ years of marketing experience, including 3+ years leading teams, within consumer electronics, IoT, smart home, connected products or building products.
Bachelor’s Degree in Marketing, Business, a related field, or equivalent experience required.
Proven ownership of a marketing budget, including planning, agency buying oversight and optimization of paid media.
Strong product marketing background, with launches in both consumer and B2B or Pro channels.
Track record of building or scaling a consumer brand, growing awareness, consideration and share through creative, original and sometimes unconventional programs, not only performance media.
Experience launching creator, influencer, community or partnership programs that measurably grew a brand; experience at a consumer startup or high-growth consumer brand is a plus.
Experience turning quantitative customer, market and competitive data into positioning, portfolio and launch decisions.
Experience marketing through retail, ecomm and D2C channels, including Amazon, search, ratings and reviews, and enhanced content.
Hands-on experience using AI and agentic tools for marketing analytics, reporting, content and campaign operations, and the drive to scale them across a team.
Track record of managing agency partners to clear scopes and measurable results.
Measurement-driven, with a bias for experimentation: has built marketing KPI frameworks and scorecards, and uses attribution, testing and ROI analysis to make spend and strategy decisions, while leaving room for bold bets that data alone cannot yet justify.
Builder and growth mindset: comfortable in a startup-style team, setting strategy and doing hands-on work, with the curiosity, creativity and bias to test new ideas fast.
Strong communication skills with the ability to tell a compelling story at all levels of the organization.
Able to build trust and rapport across functions and lead through influence.
Ability to travel approximately 20%, to Deerfield, trade shows, retail partners and customer sites.

Strong organization, attention to detail, confidentiality, follow-through, and employee service skills.

title: Product Commercialization Engineer
description:
Job Description:
SUMMARY:
The Product Commercialization Engineer will get to work in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, leading the scale-up and commercialization of adhesive, coating, and polymer technologies from laboratory development to full-scale manufacturing. This hands-on role partners with R&D, Operations, Engineering, Quality, EHS, Procurement, and Supply Chain to solve scale-up challenges and ensure products are manufactured safely, reliably, and cost-effectively across epoxy, acrylic/methacrylate, polyurethane, and hybrid polymer systems. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of driving innovation and growth for a division within a market-leading, Fortune 200 organization!
ITW BUSINESS MODEL & CULTURE
We have an environment shaped by our decentralized, entrepreneurial culture that brings our exciting ideas to life.  Our people thrive in our “flexibility within the framework” approach.
We are committed to providing you with growth and development opportunities that maximize your unique potential.
Our culture empowers you to think and act like a business owner – we want your entrepreneurial spirit to thrive!
Be a part of One ITW/One Team, where everyone’s contribution matters in our quest to achieve our full potential.
We live by our Core Values: simplicity, sharing risk, integrity, respect, and trust.
YOU MIGHT LIKE THIS JOB IF YOU ARE...
Are an entrepreneurial self-starter. You take initiative and ownership of your surroundings and constantly seek to find ways to improve.
Thrive in a fast-paced environment that keeps you on your toes – you love a good challenge, meeting aggressive deadlines, and can stay calm under pressure.
Have a passion for innovation and creating new technologies to solve customer pain points and market applicability.
Are resilient. You enjoy finding solutions to complex challenges and do so with poise and resolve.
Can work well with cross functional teams and lead by example. You have strong communication skills and the ability to influence without authority.
PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:
Product Commercialization & Scale-Up
Lead commercialization and scale-up of new adhesive, coating, and polymer products from lab to full-scale manufacturing.
Develop robust, reproducible, and scalable manufacturing processes using chemical engineering principles and process science.
Identify and mitigate scale-up risks related to mixing, reaction control, heat transfer, equipment capability, and process variability.
Define operating windows and critical process parameters to ensure quality, consistency, and manufacturability.
Manufacturing & Process Improvement
Serve as a technical expert in polymer chemistry, process control, mixing, manufacturability, and raw material interactions.
Drive process improvements that enhance safety, quality, throughput, cost efficiency, and waste reduction while maintaining product performance.
Lead manufacturing troubleshooting, root-cause investigations, and resolution of batch variability and scale-dependent performance issues.
Apply DOE, statistical analysis, and structured problem-solving tools to optimize processes and resolve manufacturing challenges.
Change Management & Process Technology
Lead evaluation, validation, and implementation of raw material, process, equipment, and manufacturing site changes, including alternative and second-source materials.
Identify, evaluate, and implement new manufacturing technologies, process controls, equipment, and analytical tools that support commercialization and operational excellence.
Support equipment qualification, process commissioning, manufacturing start-ups, and production readiness activities.
Safety, Quality & Leadership
Provide technical leadership across R&D, Operations, Quality, EHS, Supply Chain, suppliers, and external partners to deliver safe, compliant, cost-effective, and successful product commercialization.
Promote, support, and adhere to all safety, environmental and quality related policies and procedures .
QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, & COMPETENCIES:
B.S. in Chemical Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline.
Minimum 5 years of experience in product/process scale-up and commercialization within a chemical manufacturing environment, including transfer from laboratory through pilot to commercial production.
Demonstrated experience bridging R&D/product development and manufacturing operations, including technology transfer and support of production scale-up between sites. Demonstrated track record of successfully commercializing new products at industrial production scale.
Strong knowledge of chemical engineering fundamentals, including mixing, heat transfer, mass transfer, reaction engineering, process control, and industrial manufacturing equipment/processes.
Proven ability to troubleshoot manufacturing and product-quality issues using structured problem-solving methods, including DOE, statistical analysis, process data analysis, and root-cause investigation; proficiency with tools such as JMP or Minitab preferred.
Demonstrated experience qualifying raw materials and alternate sources in incumbent commercial products.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across technical, operational, and manufacturing teams.
Experience preferred in the adhesives, coatings, sealants, specialty polymers, or formulated chemical products industries, primarily with epoxy, polyurethane, acrylic/methacrylate, and/or hybrid polymer chemistries.
Travel:  Ability to travel periodically to manufacturing facilities, suppliers, and partner locations within the United States. Occasional international travel may be required.

The salary for this role is $100,000.00 - $125,000.00. This is the range that we in good faith anticipate relying on when setting wages for this position. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and this range. This salary range may also be modified in the future.

title: Sr Buyer - Precision Welding Solutions Divison
description:
Job Description:
The Senior Buyer is a key supply chain leader responsible for driving procurement, supplier performance, inventory management, and continuous improvement initiatives within the Precision Welding Solutions Division. In this role you will partner closely with the Materials Manager, suppliers, engineering and cross-functional teams to ensure excellence in cost, quality and delivery.
You will provide leadership, develop talent and drive results across the Precision Welding Solutions Division.  The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced environment, demonstrates strong negotiation and relationship building skills and can drive change through collaboration and influence.
How You Will Make an Impact:
Supply Chain & Procurement
Manage procurement activities, including sourcing, purchasing, inventory planning, and material flow.
Lead supplier negotiations involving pricing, contracts, delivery performance, and service levels.
Evaluate, select, and develop suppliers in partnership with the Materials Manager and engineering team.
Build collaborative supplier relationships while identifying opportunities for supplier consolidation and risk reduction.
Conduct supplier visits, audits, and performance reviews.
Manage supplier corrective action processes and ensure timely resolution of quality or delivery issues.
Monitor and communicate Market Rate of Demand (MRD) changes to suppliers
Cost & Inventory Management
Drive cost reduction, productivity, quality, delivery, and simplification initiatives.
Manage material price variance, inventory turns, and inventory optimization programs.
Track and document cost savings and cost avoidance projects.
Maintain inventory accuracy through cycle count oversight and inventory management practices.
Support inventory transition activities related to product launches, engineering changes, and product obsolescence.
Manage MOH and inactive inventory performance metrics.
Strategic Initiatives
Lead or support divisional materials and supply chain improvement projects.
Develop and implement materials strategies aligned with business objectives.
Actively participate in New Product Development (NPD) initiatives.
Partner daily with manufacturing, engineering, and other cross-functional teams to ensure material availability and operational continuity.
Champion and implement ITW business principles, including 80/20, Product Line Simplification, Market Rate of Demand (MRD), Empowerment, Trust, and Continuous Improvement.
Leadership & Talent Development
Provide leadership, coaching, and support to materials personnel and cross-functional teams.
Depending on organizational needs and candidate experience, the role may include direct supervision of materials personnel.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, improve efficiency, and develop organizational capabilities
How You Show Up:
Collaborative Leader – Builds strong relationships through effective leadership, communication and interpersonal skills.
Supplier Partnership – Builds and maintains supplier relationships while driving negotiation, quality, delivery and cost performance.
Ownership Mindset – Takes initiative to lead cost reduction, inventory management and new product development projects.
Results-Driven – Prioritizes effectively, approaches challenges analytically and follows through to achieve results.
Growth Mindset – Demonstrates a commitment to continuous learning, professional development and personal growth.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s Degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Business Management or related field.
3 years of experience in purchasing, sourcing, supply chain or materials management.
Experience coaching, developing or leading teams either through direct supervision or cross-functional leadership
Proficiency with Microsoft office applications
Company Description
Comprised of a market-leading portfolio of best-in-class brands, the businesses of ITW Welding work together to provide premium performance delivered through a breadth of solutions encompassing welding, cutting, consumables, and accessories.  ITW Welding North America represents Miller Electric Welding Equipment, Safety & Accessories, Hobart Filler Metals, and Bernard / Tregaskiss MIG Guns.
Miller Electric Mfg. LLC, is headquartered in Appleton, Wisconsin, and wholly owned by  Illinois Tool Works  (NYSE: ITW). The company maintains its industry leadership by setting the standard for reliability, quality and responsiveness. Our tagline, “The Power of Blue®,” is inspired by the blue color of Miller equipment.
The company began with an innovation that responded to customer needs, growing from a one-man operation in 1929, to the world’s largest manufacturer of arc welding products. Miller keeps the tradition alive by focusing on its top priority: people.
Why ITW Welding?
Here’s what we offer to help you build the future you want:
Generous Retirement Benefits – 401(k) match PLUS an additional retirement contribution to help you plan for the future.
Paid Time Off – 11 paid holidays, 5 sick days, and vacation time to take time for what matters.

The Analyst, EFT Trade Compliance and Operations is responsible for overseeing and
coordinating all international movements originating from the United States to destinations
worldwide, including but not limited to Mexico, Germany, Bulgaria, and Malaysia. The scope
includes equipment, service parts, repairs, upgrades, returns, loaners, demonstrations,
manufacturing-related tools, components, and materials. This role serves as the primary
coordinator for the end-to-end Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) process and as the
operational interface among engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, logistics,
customs brokers, suppliers, and trade compliance. The position owns shipment visibility,
status management, escalation handling, regulatory readiness, classification
governance, permit management, and export/import compliance from submission through
U.S. export and destination-country import. It ensures products are properly classified,
registered, documented, and compliance-ready before shipment approval.
Essential Job Duties
 Manage end-to-end international movements of capital equipment, repairs, returns,
demonstration units, components, service parts, manufacturing-related tools, and
materials from the United States to countries worldwide

United States and related returns, and lead cross-functional escalation calls for critical
shipments.

milestones and readiness, and serve as the primary owner of the SAF Helpline Zoom
Channel.
 Provide shipment status updates to engineers and project teams, track open issues,
and ensure timely resolution.
 Coordinate with customs brokers, freight forwarders, and logistics providers to
support timely U.S. export and destination-country import clearance and resolve holds,
delays, documentation issues, and classification discrepancies.
 Manage U.S. export and destination-country tariff classification activities.
 Partner with engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, suppliers, and
trade compliance to obtain and evaluate technical information required for classification
and country of origin determinations.
 Review engineering drawings, Bills of Materials, product specifications,
materials, component information, and product functionality to support HTS, Schedule
B, ECCN, and country of origin determinations.
 Verify completion of classification, country of origin documentation, FTA eligibility, metal
certificates, permit or license approvals, and customs documentation readiness.
 Evaluate destination-country import requirements, including permits, product
registrations, labeling or conformity requirements, special regulations, and customs
restrictions.
 Coordinate product data required for applicable customs, inventory control, and trade
compliance systems.
 Ensure products are compliance-ready before shipment authorization and support
inventory registration requirements and customs record maintenance.
 Ensure accurate tracking of exported, imported, transformed, returned, scrapped, and
transferred goods.
 Prepare, review, and validate commercial invoices, export filings, permits, licenses,
certificates, temporary import/export documents, and country-specific customs
declarations.
 Ensure compliance with U.S. export requirements, destination-country import
regulations, applicable trade laws, sanctions and restricted-party requirements, and
company policies.
 Maintain complete, audit-ready trade records and ensure proper export documentation,
recordkeeping, and regulatory compliance.
 Support engineering, manufacturing, service, and supply chain teams with global trade
compliance requirements.
 Support tariff and export classification, country of origin determinations, and trade
program utilization.
 Participate in internal audits and government compliance reviews, perform trade
compliance due diligence and transaction reviews, and support audits and
investigations.
 Identify compliance risks, implement corrective actions, and define requirements for
new shipment types and destination countries.
 Develop and maintain SOPs, procedures, work instructions, playbooks, knowledge
repositories, and classification databases.
 Identify process improvement and automation opportunities and support
implementation of global trade technology solutions.
 Maintain SAF tracking dashboards and monitor SLA performance; report shipment
aging, cycle times, backlog, and escalation metrics.
 Perform other duties, tasks, and special projects as assigned.
Required Skills and Experience
 Minimum 5 years of experience in:
• U.S.-Mexico cross-border operations
• Customs compliance
• Import/export operations
• IMMEX program administration
 Fluent in English and Spanish (written and verbal).
 Experience preparing customs documentation and supporting customs audits.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Advanced Excel and ERP system experience.
Preferred Skills and Experience
 Experience in the medical device, healthcare, pharmaceutical, or highly regulated
manufacturing industry.
 Experience with FDA-regulated products.
 Knowledge of USMCA and other free trade agreement requirements.
 Experience with SAP, GTS, Annex 24 software, or other customs compliance systems.
 Customs certifications or trade compliance credentials are a plus.
 Knowledge of:
• IMMEX Program
• Annex 24
• Annex 30
• U.S. Import Compliance
• U.S. Export Compliance
• Customs broker management
• Temporary import/export programs
Education & Training
 Bachelor's degree in engineering, international trade, customs administration, supply
chain, business, logistics, or a related field.

Normal office conditions.
Travel required (<10%) – both domestic and international.

If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineers (Systems Analysts) at Intuitive Surgical play a critical role in developing the safest, highest-quality robotic platforms for minimally invasive surgery through rigorous engineering analysis, innovative problem-solving, and robust technical execution.
Systems Analysts are central to the design, development, integration, and lifecycle support of next-generation products across the da Vinci Surgical System portfolio. They are responsible for developing, optimizing, and validating algorithms that govern robotic manipulator motion, force control, and system safety across surgical robots, instruments, accessories, and endoscopes.
The role requires broad systems-level expertise and close collaboration across multiple engineering disciplines, including mechanical, software, controls, user interface, electrical, and safety engineering. Systems Analysts provide early technical input into product architecture and design decisions, rapidly evaluate and validate new concepts, and proactively address complex challenges in system integration, functional safety, motion and force control, and manufacturing.
Their ownership extends throughout the product development lifecycle, from early feasibility and architecture through design verification, system integration, manufacturing readiness, and commercial release. The ultimate objective is to deliver innovative robotic technologies that meet the highest standards of safety, quality, performance, and reliability for surgeons and patients.
The Manager of a Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineering (Systems Analysis) team establishes responsibilities within their team. They are responsible for defining and meeting project milestones. They advise senior management on the technical strategy for product and platform projects. They work closely with other algorithms & controls, software, hardware, manufacturing, and clinical engineering teams to enable cohesion of design inputs, design architecture, specifications, and verification. They are expected to hire, coach, and retain Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineering talent within their group
Essential Job Duties:
Manage and support a team of Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineers towards successful accomplishment of product implementation with best-in-class solutions and architectures
Hire, retain key talent required for the team to be successful.
Provide in-depth analysis and characterization of electromechanical architectures during the entire design life cycle.
Facilitate mechanical, electrical, and software integration of new prototypes and new products including complete robotic systems, manipulators, instruments, accessories, and endoscopes
Analyze complex electro-mechanical devices for dynamic safety and clinical risk
Implement safety monitoring algorithms based on sound physics and risk analysis
Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic

Support the definition of manufacturing specifications and the ability to confirm devices meet those specifications
Document and pursue intellectual property
Communicate system architectural choices to the cross functional engineering team
Improve cross functional workflow and interaction through tool building and teaching others

Working closely with the clinical development team to understand performance requirements;
Working closely with the mechanical design team to optimize the mechanism for motion fidelity;
Using analysis and experimentation to develop a deep understanding of the behavior and limitations of the instrument mechanism;
Modifying and tuning the algorithms to optimize motion fidelity and ensure consistent performance in the clinical environment.
Implement features and algorithms to support new instrument development, including collaboration with the design team to iterate through prototypes, analyze performance, and assess feasibility.
Perform risk analysis and implement safety algorithms. This includes documentation of risks, requirements, and test protocols to support requests for approval by regulatory agencies such as the FDA.
Analyze field data to continuously improve the performance and stability of the surgical instrument.
Collaborate with the manufacturing team to develop automated fixtures for calibrating, testing, and aiding assembly of the instrument. Additionally, determine manufacturing test specifications that will ensure instrument performance.

Intuitive understanding of mechanical phenomena with ability to do rigorous analysis.
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
Ability to work independently and the determination to solve challenging problems

Minimum Masters in robotics related engineering field, with 6 years of experience in control of mechatronic systems, or Ph.D. with 3 years of experience in control of mechatronic systems.

Experience launching real-world, commercially successful products

description:

Position Overview
The Upstream Reimbursement Strategist is the architect of the organization’s long-range reimbursement and market access strategy across the U.S. product portfolio. This person is responsible for generating all strategies for all upstream programs and dovetailing those strategies with global market access for ex-U.S. projects. This role is the closest link to the clinical development team and serves as the primary strategic interface with HEOR, regulatory affairs, and health policy stakeholders.
Responsible for evidence generation strategy, CPT/HCPCS code pathway design, CMS payment policy analysis, and the global coordination of evidence that feeds both upstream regulatory submissions and downstream field execution tools. This person shapes the narrative for why a product deserves reimbursement and builds the data package to support it.
Core Responsibilities
CPT/HCPCS Code Strategy: Lead the strategy for new code applications, Category III code conversions, and descriptor modifications. Manage engagement with AMA CPT Editorial Panel, RUC, and HCPCS workgroups.
CMS Payment Policy Analysis: Conduct ongoing analysis of OPPS, PFS, and ASC payment policy. Prepare and submit CMS comment letters during rulemaking cycles. Monitor NT-APC, pass-through, and device payment category developments.
Global Evidence Coordination: Serve as the connective tissue between U.S. evidence needs and global HEOR and OUS markets. Dovetail U.S. upstream strategies with global market access to ensure alignment on ex-U.S. projects. Ensure evidence generation is sequenced to serve both U.S. regulatory/payer needs and ex-U.S. HTA submissions, coordinating timing and deliverables across jurisdictions.
Coverage & Reimbursement Strategy: Generate and own the reimbursement strategy for all upstream programs across the full product portfolio. Develop and maintain the strategic reimbursement roadmap from early pipeline through commercialization, including target product profiles (TPPs) and core value dossiers (CVDs) for pipeline assets. Identify coverage gaps, analyze competitive reimbursement positioning, recommend pathway strategies, and ensure strategic continuity as products progress through development milestones.
U.S. Value Plan Implementation Support: Play a supporting role to HEOR in ensuring the U.S. Market Access team has secured the database resources required to execute strategy and implement the recommendations set out in the U.S. Value Plan.
Competitive Intelligence: Monitor competitor reimbursement strategies, code applications, pass-through approvals, and coverage determinations. Translate competitive intelligence into actionable strategic recommendations.
Product Positioning & Message Alignment: Serve as the primary owner of product positioning in coordination with select downstream stakeholders, ensuring messaging is consistent across other stakeholders in the organization — particularly when producing publications such as burden of illness, cost-utility, and budget impact analyses.
Market Access Research: Lead market access research to support value messaging, including claims analyses and — where needed — coordination of payer interviews, provider interviews, and other primary research.
Shared Midstream Responsibility: Contribute to code acquisition execution, pre-launch payer engagement planning, and payment policy implementation activities in partnership with the Mid/Downstream Tactician.
Required
Health policy degree or similar
3-8+ years of progressive experience in medical device market access, health economics, reimbursement strategy, or related field (for manager level, 3+)
Deep working knowledge of CMS OPPS/PFS/ASC payment systems, APC mechanics, and facility payment methodology
Experience with CPT, , AMA Editorial Panel processes, and HCPCS coding pathways
Strong analytical skills with experience interpreting claims data, cost reports, and CMS rulemaking documents
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to translate complex policy into strategic recommendations
Ability to work cross-functionally with clinical, regulatory, HEOR, and commercial teams
Preferred
Advanced degree (MPH, MBA, or equivalent; PhD or PharmD also welcome)
Familiarity with healthcare data platforms
Familiarity with HEOR models

If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of the Position
The Physician, Corporate Strategy is an MD physician innovator embedded within Intuitive’s Future Forward Incubator. This role translates clinical insight and early-market understanding into new growth opportunities, helping identify unmet clinical needs, evaluate strategic fit, and shape technology concepts from initial hypothesis through early de-risking. We are open to candidates who bring one of two complementary profiles: (1) strong clinical practice experience with exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) deep venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience with an MD background and enough medical/clinical fluency to credibly assess patient care, procedure workflows, and clinician needs. The successful candidate will work closely with engineering, clinical, product, regulatory, reimbursement, and strategy partners to determine which opportunities should advance and how they should be clinically and commercially framed.
Essential Job Duties
Identify, frame, and prioritize unmet clinical needs using clinical immersion, literature review, market sensing, and voice-of-customer input.
Translate physician and patient insights into concise need statements, opportunity hypotheses, clinical workflows, requirements, and early de-risking plans.
Evaluate early-stage opportunities for clinical importance, feasibility, strategic fit, adoption barriers, competitive landscape, and potential business impact.
Partner with engineering and design teams to define clinical use cases, procedural workflows, performance goals, and prototype feedback loops for new platforms.
Lead or support early clinical de-risking activities, including preclinical studies, simulated use, workflow validation, and early feasibility planning where appropriate.
Develop point-of-view assessments on emerging technologies, startups, venture-backed innovation, adjacent markets, and external partnership opportunities.
Collaborate with regulatory, reimbursement, health economics, product, and commercial strategy partners to shape indication strategy and development pathways.
Engage KOLs, clinicians, entrepreneurs, academic innovators, and external partners to validate concepts and inform investment decisions.
Communicate findings to senior stakeholders through clear written recommendations, executive presentations, and data-driven opportunity narratives.
Experience and Qualifications
MD or DO required; active clinical practice is valued but not required for candidates with substantial innovation, venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience.
Must demonstrate at least one of the following experience profiles: (1) meaningful hands-on clinical practice or procedural care experience plus exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) strong venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, corporate strategy, or product strategy experience plus sufficient clinical fluency to evaluate medical needs and care pathways.
Ability to identify unmet clinical needs and convert observations into structured hypotheses, need statements, development plans, or investment theses.
Experience conducting clinician, patient, or stakeholder interviews and synthesizing voice-of-customer input into actionable product or strategy recommendations.
Comfort operating in ambiguous, early-stage environments where the path forward is uncertain and evidence must be built iteratively.
Strong cross-functional influence skills and ability to collaborate with engineering, clinical, regulatory, reimbursement, product, and business stakeholders.
Ability to evaluate clinical workflows, procedure economics, adoption barriers, competitive dynamics, and strategic implications for new technology platforms.
Clear executive communication skills, including crisp written synthesis, structured presentations, and the ability to explain complex clinical concepts to non-clinical audiences.
Curiosity, ownership mindset, and enthusiasm for building new technologies that can transform care delivery and improve patient outcomes.
Biodesign or equivalent needs-based innovation training preferred; experience in venture, startups, business development, product strategy, or corporate strategy strongly preferred.
Working Conditions:
Must be available to work full-time onsite in Sunnyvale, CA
Ability to travel to clinical sites, customer locations, or conferences (up to 25%)

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The Senior Epidemiologist, Real-World Evidence Generation will design and execute data-driven analyses
using claims databases and real-world evidence to demonstrate the clinical and economic value of
emerging robotic platforms. This role focuses on rigorous statistical analysis of U.S. commercial and
Medicare claims data, real-world outcomes research, and translating findings into evidence that supports
regulatory submissions, payer discussions, and clinical adoption. The successful candidate will combine
epidemiologic expertise with advanced statistical methods to generate peer-reviewed publications and
evidence dossiers that demonstrate procedure value and patient benefit.
Essential Job Duties
• Real-World Evidence Generation & Claims Data Analysis
• Design and execute comprehensive analyses using U.S. commercial claims databases (e.g.,
MarketScan, Optum), Medicare data, and other population-level observational datasets to
evaluate procedure outcomes, safety, and resource utilization.
• Develop and apply rigorous epidemiologic and statistical methods (descriptive, analytic, causal
inference techniques) to real-world data to characterize patient populations, identify responder
phenotypes, and quantify procedure value.
• Build and document complex research datasets by integrating multi-source claims data (medical,
pharmaceutical, facility claims) with appropriate data governance and quality assurance
protocols.
• Conduct comparative effectiveness research, cost analysis, and health outcomes assessment
using claims-based methodologies.
• Ensure compliance with data use agreements, privacy regulations, and analytical standards in all
database projects.
Statistical Analysis & Methodology
• Perform advanced statistical analyses including logistic regression, survival analysis, propensity
score matching, instrumental variable analysis, and other causal inference methods appropriate
for observational data.
Develop and document standardized analytical code libraries
(SAS, R, SQL) that enable reproducible, transparent research and
support collaboration across teams.
• Apply epidemiologic principles to address confounding, selection
bias, and other threats to validity in observational research.
• Interpret complex statistical findings and communicate results clearly to both technical and non-
technical audiences.
Health Economics Integration
• Support health economic analyses by providing clinical outcome data, cost drivers, and utilization
patterns derived from claims databases.
• Partner with HEOR colleagues to integrate real-world evidence with economic models, ensuring
clinical parameters reflect actual patient populations and healthcare system utilization.
• Quantify resource utilization, cost burden, and clinical benefits for target patient populations
using claims-based metrics.
• Contribute epidemiologic and statistical expertise to develop value propositions grounded in
evidence.
Evidence Translation, Publication Strategy & External Scientific Engagement
• Lead peer-reviewed publication development for real-world evidence studies, ensuring
methodologic rigor and clinical relevance.
• Translate research findings into clear, evidence-based value dossiers and briefing documents for
regulatory, payer, and clinical stakeholders.
• Communicate complex methodologic approaches and findings to diverse audiences through
publications, regulatory submissions, and scientific presentations.
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align evidence generation with regulatory pathways
and market access objectives.
• Identify and establish relationships with key opinion leaders and clinical experts relevant to
procedural outcomes and value demonstration.
• Develop publication roadmaps in collaboration with identified KOLs to ensure real-world
evidence reaches target clinical audiences and informs procedural adoption.
• Partner with KOLs on evidence interpretation and manuscript development to strengthen
methodologic rigor, clinical relevance, and impact of findings.
• Lead strategic positioning of real-world evidence findings at key conferences, in high-impact
peer-reviewed journals, and through clinical society engagement to build procedural credibility.
• Support advisory activities and collaborative research initiatives with clinical thought leaders that
align with evidence generation priorities and external validation.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Work with Clinical Affairs, Regulatory, and Market Access teams to identify key evidence gaps
and prioritize analyses that support product value demonstration.
• Partner with R&D and Product Management to inform design considerations and clinical
endpoints based on real-world data insights.
• Mentor and support junior analysts and team members in epidemiologic and statistical methods.
• Engage with external stakeholders (KOLs, clinicians, researchers) to validate findings and ensure
clinical relevance.
Required Skills and Experience
4+ years of experience in epidemiologic research, real-world
evidence generation, or outcomes research, with demonstrated
expertise in claims database analysis
• Advanced proficiency in statistical programming languages (R,
SAS, SQL) and experience building and managing large, complex datasets from multiple sources
• Direct experience accessing, analyzing, and interpreting U.S. commercial and Medicare claims
databases (e.g., MarketScan, Optum, Komodo, CMS data)
• Strong knowledge of epidemiologic study designs, causal inference methods, and statistical
approaches for observational data
• Track record of peer-reviewed publications demonstrating methodologic rigor and clinical impact
• Proven ability to work independently on complex analyses while collaborating effectively with
cross-functional teams
• Strong communication skills with ability to translate statistical findings for diverse stakeholder
groups
• Experience working in fast-paced, innovation-driven environments within medical device,
biotech, or health technology sectors

Advanced degree in Epidemiology, Public Health, Biostatistics, Statistics, or related quantitative field (PhD,
MSc strongly preferred); MD/DO with substantial epidemiologic or clinical research background may be
considered

Sense of curiosity and a willingness to always dig deeper.
Ability to read electronic and mechanical schematics, assembly, and fabrication drawings.  Execute testing and data collection using Linux, Matlab, and other software toolsets.
Strong skills in problem solving and using Minitab/JMP, Python, SQL, Tableau and/or other SW tools for data analysis to identify root cause and drive corrective actions.

BS degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering/Science, or Mechanical Engineering.
MS degree in Engineering preferred.

Ability to sit and stand for long periods of time
Ability to lift, and carry parts weighing up to 40 lbs
Ability to maneuver into spaces around robotic system

“Self-starter” attitude and comfort in a hands-on environment, where he/she can demonstrate an ability to work with other engineers to influence product and manufacturing design to improve reliability.
Experience in an ISO 13485, ISO 9001, or medical device manufacturing environment
Experience and proficiency in ERP, CRM, PLM software including SAP and Agile.
Experience with use of EE lab equipment including Oscilloscopes, Spectrum Analyzers, Power supplies, and Multimeters

description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
