If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
The Advanced Product Development (APD) team leverages and advances the cutting-edge of technology to design and develop the surgical robotic systems of the future. Robotics Algorithms and Controls engineers (Systems Analysts) perform a central role in the design, development, and support of new products in the da Vinci product line. They are responsible for developing the surgical teleoperation, motion control, and safety algorithms. This responsibility crosses into electrical, mechanical, software, control, user interface, and safety engineering. Systems Analysts strive to provide early design input, prove out new designs, and seek out solutions to challenging problems.
As a Senior Systems Analyst you will work with a small, multidisciplinary team of talented and dedicated engineers. This position is the software-oriented track within Systems Analysis, bridging the team’s algorithms and the software infrastructure they run on. You will own the software layer between the application and the real-time control loop, the bring-up of the embedded compute platform, the software side of the FPGA interface, and you will bring enough fluency in control algorithms to connect their signals to the right system modes and safety responses. Systems Analysts maintain awareness and interest in developing research and technologies related to medical devices and safety-critical systems and actively apply this knowledge to system design.
Essential Job Duties
•       Design, implement, and own the software layer between the application software and the real-time control loop.
•       Bring up the embedded compute platform and real-time execution environment for new prototype systems.
•       Own the software interface to the FPGA, including drivers and data paths between processors and FPGA logic.
•       Integrate prototype hardware with existing systems and lead embedded bring-up of new manipulators, instruments, and controller boards.
•       Implement control and safety algorithms developed with Systems Analysts as deterministic, production-quality embedded software.
•       Design and implement servo control systems with Systems Analysts, applying control theory to mechatronic and tele-robotic platforms.
•       Connect algorithm signals to the appropriate system modes and safety responses in partnership with the Systems Analysts who own the supervisory logic.
•       Root-cause problems that cross the hardware, software, and control boundary.
•       Develop test, continuous integration, simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop infrastructure for Systems Analysis software; provide tool building for other engineering issues.
•       Document software design, risks, requirements, and test protocols; document and communicate intellectual property.
•       Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic.
•       Communicate system performance to the organization and support it as products evolve from design engineering to manufacturing.
•       Act as an interface between Systems Analysis and Software Engineering; take ownership of issues that cross disciplinary boundaries.
Required Skills and Experience
•       Strong embedded development skills, including intimate knowledge of C and modern C++, and experience with unit testing, continuous integration, and modern build systems.
•       Experience developing software under real-time constraints, with a solid understanding of determinism, latency, and execution-time analysis.
•       Experience with embedded architectures on multi-processor SoC/FPGA platforms, including bare-metal or RTOS development, device drivers, and inter-processor communication.
•       Hands-on experience bringing up embedded platforms and integrating prototype hardware with software.
•       Working knowledge of control systems and robotics sufficient to read, modify, and reason about control code and its timing.
•       MATLAB and Python programming capabilities for analysis, simulation, and tool building.
•       Comfort with the concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis.
•       Detail-oriented, with the ability to develop and drive a single solution to completion.
•       Hands-on engineering experience with a proven ability to work well in a team environment.
•       Self-motivated and proactive in engaging with interdisciplinary teams to address and solve complex problems.
•       A desire to deliver a quality and innovative product that will improve millions of people’s lives.
Required Education and Training
•       Minimum MS degree in CS, EE, ME, or a similar field with 4–5+ years of industrial experience, or a PhD with 1–3+ years of experience, or a BS with 7+ years of relevant industrial experience.
Working Conditions
•       Position is primarily office/lab-based (Sunnyvale, CA). Requires regular access to prototype and lab environments with standard safety precautions. Up to 10% travel for clinical site visits, partner meetings, or conference participation.
Preferred Skills and Experience
•       Experience designing and implementing servo control systems, or a deeper robotics and controls background.
•       Medical device or safety-critical system product experience (FDA design controls, ISO 13485, ISO 14971).
•       Experience with surgical robotics, haptics, or tele-presence system design.
•       Familiarity with FPGA-based motor control or other embedded real-time architectures.
•       Experience developing products in a highly regulated environment, including through FDA clearance.

Reporting to the Director, Workday Solutions, this role serves as the senior technical authority for compensation in Workday. The architect translates Total Rewards strategy and complex business requirements into scalable, compliant, and auditable solutions, covering pay structures, plan design, eligibility, and annual review cycles for merit, bonus, and stock.
This role works in close partnership with Total Rewards, HR Executives, Centers of Excellence (COEs), Finance, HR Business Leaders, and IT leadership to deliver accurate, reliable, and user-friendly compensation experiences for employees, managers, and compensation teams.

Compensation Solution Architecture & Strategy
·      Own the end-to-end architecture for Workday Core and Advanced Compensation, ensuring designs align with Total Rewards strategy, enterprise standards, and business goals.
·      Lead requirements gathering, fit-gap analysis, and design workshops with Total Rewards, HR, Finance, and IT stakeholders.
·      Provide input to the Workday and HR technology roadmap, including compensation priorities, release adoption, and technical debt reduction.

Core Compensation
·      Design and maintain compensation structures, including grades, grade profiles, steps, salary ranges, and pay differentials by geography and job.

·      Proven experience leading at least 2 full-lifecycle Workday implementations or major deployments that included Core and Advanced Compensation, including at least one annual compensation review cycle.

As a Vision Software Staff Engineer, you will act as the technical lead for the software and embedded architecture definition of the real-time, high-definition video processing, imaging, and intra-body illumination systems at the heart of a new generation surgical robotic platform.
You will drive the deep integration of cameras, image sensors, and vision processing pipelines into complex, multi-processor embedded architectures, bringing sound engineering judgment to the trade-offs between hardware, software, and algorithms, and procedure-specific product requirements.
Critical to the success of this role is experience diagnosing and debugging complex vision systems end-to-end – from sensor and optics through the video pipeline to software – driving root cause investigations and collaborating with hardware and algorithms teams to resolve difficult, multi-disciplinary issues. Familiarity with working in a regulated industry and with design controls for medical devices is a plus.
The successful candidate must excel at evaluating design trade-offs through detailed technical deep dives, proof-of-concept development, and rapid iteration, translating rough requirements into robust, well-reasoned embedded software architectures.
A strong sense of shared responsibility and shared reward is required, as is the ability to make the work fun and interesting. Supporting you will be a development and management team that knows and cares about what you are doing and wants you to succeed.
Essential Job Duties
Lead the definition of hardware, software, and algorithms architecture for the real-time video processing engine, image sensors, and intra-body illumination systems of a new generation surgical robotic platform, from concept through implementation.
Drive the integration of cameras, image sensors, and vision processing pipelines into complex, multi-processor embedded architectures, ensuring robust interfaces between hardware, FPGA/ISP, and software components.
Evaluate multiple design trade-offs for the embedded vision software architecture through detailed technical deep dives, proof-of-concept development, and rapid iteration.
Lead bring-up and integration of new, high-performance cameras and image sensors, and the integration and evaluation of advanced camera pipeline video processing algorithms.
Diagnose and debug vision system issues end-to-end – sensor, optics, video pipeline, and software – leading root cause investigations in close collaboration with hardware, algorithms, and systems engineering teams.
Drive development and enhancement of the color and power control functions for intra-operative illumination.
Lead formal risk analyses for vision and illumination subsystems; identify additional hardware requirements and develop software mitigations to minimize potential failures.
Design and develop offline simulation environments and hardware/software diagnostic tools that accelerate development, debug, and test.
Perform and guide detailed design, development, documentation, and verification of embedded vision software and supervisory state machines, in compliance with regulatory requirements and Intuitive's internal guidelines.
Contribute broadly across the video and vision software stack, including extension of current processing frameworks to new hardware platforms.
Apply high-level and specialized imaging/vision expertise to deliver innovations and problem-solving approaches that can be leveraged across multiple products.
Mentor and guide engineers across the vision team.

Bachelor's degree or above in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a similar technical field.
A minimum of 12 years of experience developing and supporting embedded systems, with significant focus on video, imaging, or vision systems (or 8 years with a Master's degree, or 5 years with a PhD).

Fluent in designing and developing mission-critical, cross-platform code in C/C++ for embedded, real-time, Linux-based systems, including application-level and driver-level development for multi-core and multi-processor architectures.
Deep familiarity with integrating cameras, image sensors, and vision processing pipelines into complex embedded architectures, including hardware, software, and algorithm interfaces.
Demonstrated ability to debug and diagnose complex vision system issues through root cause investigation and close cross-functional collaboration with hardware and algorithms teams.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate design trade-offs for embedded software architectures through detailed technical deep dives, proof-of-concept development, and rapid iteration.
Direct experience with imaging devices – e.g., cameras, light sensors, video/graphics hardware – including sensor and camera bring-up, configuration, and integration.
Fluent with image-processing concepts, camera pipeline video processing algorithms, and video processing frameworks.
Working knowledge of Python or other scripting languages for diagnostics, automation, and test.
Demonstrated experience and comfort with all phases of the product development lifecycle, including design, documentation, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing.

Knowledge of image-processing, CUDA, ML, and/or FPGA integration (e.g., Vivado and other FPGA development tools).

description:

Primary Function of Position:
The System Software Lab Integration Engineer is a member of the System Test Release Operations team, reporting directly to the Lab Operations Manager. This role sits at the intersection of lab operations and system test — making it a unique blend of hands-on lab ownership and rigorous software validation. The core mission of this role is to keep the lab running and ensure the system functions as a cohesive, integrated hardware / software unit. Day-to-day, responsibilities include setting up systems and test environments, running diagnostics, and triaging failures that span hardware, firmware, and software boundaries. Beyond reactive troubleshooting, this role takes a proactive approach on maintaining healthy lab systems and improving system reliability by reviewing software changes and hardware failures, flagging pull requests that could potentially brick system hardware, identify non-conformance trends, and drive issues through to resolution.

Own day-to-day lab operations — including system hardware setup, test environment configuration, inventory, and ongoing environment maintenance to maximize lab readiness and system availability
Triage and debug integration failures across hardware, firmware, and software boundaries using methodical debugging techniques; recover bricked boards and restore systems to operational state efficiently; remove, replace and test failed hardware components

Isolate and document defects — reproduce failures, work closely with cross-functional teams to identify root causes across HW/FW/SW boundaries, and file clear, actionable bug reports that accelerate resolution
Analyze test data and non-conformance trends — generate dashboards and executive-level summaries that translate raw data into meaningful insights, and recommend improvements to drive system reliability
Reviewing incoming software changes and pull requests - proactively assess risk, flag PRs that could potentially brick system hardware, and partner with development teams to implement safeguards before changes are merged

Troubleshooting mindset with an ability to break down a system or process systematically and effectively into subparts to identify failure mechanisms
Proven ability to proactively engage with the unknown/unfamiliar, curiosity to learn how things work and apply that learning to new challenges
Understanding of hardware architecture and system-level interactions between software and hardware
Strong hands-on experience with Linux operating systems and command-line tools
Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills
Strong organization skills including attention to detail and task follow-through
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills and eagerness to collaborate cross-functionally
Proficiency in developing and maintaining standard operating procedures
Ability to effectively work independently and as part of a team
Required Education and Training
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical field; or equivalent practical experience
Preferred Skills and Experience
3+ years of hands-on experience in system integration, software debugging, validation engineering, lab operations, or related fields
Experience troubleshooting complex software and integrated system-level issues
Experience developing internal engineering or automation tools
Experience with Python
Ability to analyze logs, trace failures, and perform root cause analysis
Experience with embedded systems, firmware, or hardware validation environments
Knowledge of networking protocols, lab infrastructure, and large-scale test environments
Experience supporting robotics, medical device, embedded, or complex hardware/software integrated systems

title: Systems Analyst - Robotic Control Algorithms
description:

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
Were a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
The Future Forward organization is Intuitive’s advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery.
If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position:
A Systems Analyst is responsible for the detailed design and implementation of robotic control algorithms and safety systems for new surgical robots and instruments. This includes integrating and evaluating fully functional prototypes and conducting formal product testing.
Systems Analysts also provide analytical support to other engineering groups in designing mechanisms, software architecture, and selecting key components, utilizing both physical and algorithmic insights to ensure safe, reliable, and precise motion control performance and high-level behaviors in response to user inputs.
Quick learning and a keen understanding of both user and engineering perspectives are essential,
As part of the Future Forward engineering team, you will design, implement, and integrate complex functionalities into complete surgical robot solutions, overseeing them through human use and product release. You will be part of a high-energy, focused team, with a strong sense of shared responsibility and reward.
Essential Job Duties:
Contribute to the design of new robot manipulators and new robotic instruments through analysis and characterization of prototypes.
Refine and evolve system performance as it matures to a full product stage.
Facilitate mechanical, hardware, and software integration of new prototypes and new products including complete systems, manipulators, and vision.
Provide critical analysis of robot servo control and design fault-detection algorithms.
Provide analytical assistance for other engineering issues.
Document and communicate intellectual property.
Improve group workflow through tool building and robust cross-functional interactions.
Required Education and Training:
Master’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering, or similar technical field, with 3 years of experience in control systems, servo control, or robotics.
Alternatively, a Ph.D. degree in one of the technical fields above, with no experience.
Required Skills and Experience:
Experience implementing, tuning, and debugging modern servo control systems.
Expert knowledge of robot modeling and system identification techniques.
Experience in designing and developing real-time control algorithms in C or C++, with the ability to assess numerical accuracy and computational complexity.
Working knowledge of Python or MATLAB/Simulink for control system simulation, analysis, and testing.
Excellent verbal and written communications skills, with the ability to communicate effectively across all levels of an organization.
Excitement to learn, solve tough technical problems, and to help improve patients' lives.
Preferred Skills and Experience:
Expert in one or more advanced robotic control concepts such as impedance control or the control of flexible manipulators.
Experience designing software products in a regulated industry or for safety-critical applications; comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, risk analysis, and mitigations.
Fluent working with software version control systems such as Git.
Working knowledge of embedded Linux or QNX at multiple levels including application, board bring-up, device drivers and distribution configuration.
Experience in all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing.

description:
Job Description
Role Description
The Lead, R&D Packaging Development serves as the packaging platform leader for Canada, with accountability for leading and developing the Packaging Development team, providing technical leadership across the portfolio, and shaping packaging strategy in partnership with cross-functional and R&D stakeholders.
This role leads a team of packaging developers, including people managers and contractors, and is accountable for delivering business results through the organization. The successful candidate will have a demonstrated ability to coach and develop technical talent, set clear priorities, and build team capability while maintaining a high standard of technical excellence and execution.
The role requires strong packaging expertise and sound technical judgment to guide complex commercialization decisions, troubleshoot technical challenges, and identify emerging technologies that address business needs. Equally important is strong business acumen and the ability to partner with senior leaders and cross-functional teams to translate business priorities into an actionable packaging strategy.
The successful candidate will be an effective communicator and influencer, capable of simplifying complex technical topics and clearly articulating recommendations, risks, and strategic choices to audiences ranging from technical teams to senior leadership.
Key Responsibilities
People & Capability Leadership
Lead and develop Packaging Development team members, including a span-breaker manager, individual contributors, and contractors.
Build technical and leadership capability through goal setting, ongoing coaching and feedback, development planning, targeted project assignments, and training.
Establish clear expectations and priorities while empowering the team to make sound technical decisions and deliver results with increasing autonomy.
Build a strong pipeline of packaging talent and support succession and capability planning across the function.
Technical & Commercialization Leadership
Serve as the technical authority and packaging gatekeeper for the Canada portfolio, ensuring projects are appropriately assessed for technical feasibility, risk, business value, and resource requirements.
Provide technical coaching and direction to help teams resolve complex packaging and commercialization challenges.
Guide teams through technical decision-making, qualification, scale-up, and commercialization while ensuring appropriate technical rigor.
Identify and escalate significant commercialization risks early, ensuring clear communication, effective mitigation plans, and appropriate contingency strategies.
Champion disciplined technical problem-solving, experimentation, data analysis, and evidence-based decision-making.
Strategy & Business Partnership
Develop and communicate a clear packaging strategy aligned with Canada business priorities, growth opportunities, productivity, sustainability, and portfolio needs.
Provide a strategic packaging point of view and influence key stakeholders on priorities, investment decisions, technical trade-offs, and resource allocation.
Partner closely with Operations, Marketing, Quality, Procurement, and other R&D leaders to translate business priorities into actionable packaging programs.
Partner with internal R&D packaging leaders and centers of expertise to leverage global capabilities, technical knowledge, and best practices.
Identify and evaluate emerging packaging technologies and capabilities that can unlock innovation, improve performance, reduce cost, or address future business needs.
External Partnerships & Technology
Build strategic partnerships with material suppliers, equipment vendors, and other external technical partners.
Leverage Kraft Heinz and supplier capabilities, resources, and technical tools to accelerate innovation and solve business challenges.
Maintain awareness of developments in packaging materials, equipment, sustainability, and manufacturing technologies relevant to the Canada portfolio.
Qualifications
BS, MS, or PhD in Packaging, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Minimum 11 years of packaging development experience in the food, beverage, or consumer products industry.
Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, develop, and motivate technical teams, including experience developing other people leaders.
Proven ability to provide technical leadership across complex packaging development and commercialization programs.
Broad technical experience across packaging materials and formats, including flexible films, rigid packaging, corrugated, and secondary/tertiary packaging systems.
Strong understanding of packaging commercialization, manufacturing processes, distribution requirements, and technical risk management.
Knowledge of sustainability principles and their application to packaging strategy and development.
Excellent communication, influencing, stakeholder-management, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to communicate complex technical topics to senior leadership.
Strong business acumen with the ability to connect technical decisions to consumer, customer, operational, and financial outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and allocate resources effectively across a portfolio of projects.
Working knowledge of Design of Experiments (DOE) and structured technical problem-solving methodologies.
Experience with TOPS, SAP, Agile, or comparable packaging, specification, or data-management systems.
Willingness to travel up to 30%, including regular travel within Canada.

What’s on the menu?
We are looking for a Staff Architect – ERP Capabilities to join the Kraft Heinz TECH Architecture Team and support the evolution of Kraft Heinz's global ERP landscape.
In this role, you will provide SAP platform and architecture expertise across ERP capabilities, partnering with business teams, functional IT leaders, architects, and technology teams to guide solution decisions and support business transformation.
The role combines architecture leadership with hands-on solution design guidance. You will contribute to major ERP initiatives such as SAP S/4HANA, provide architectural input for business demands and solution designs, participate in architecture governance activities, and help advance ERP architecture practices across the organization.
The ideal candidate is a strong SAP professional with an architecture mindset, capable of understanding the broader SAP ecosystem, evaluating solution options, and translating architecture principles into practical solutions that deliver business value.
Key Ingredients:
ERP Architecture & SAP Platform
Provide architecture leadership for assigned ERP domains, covering SAP S/4HANA, ECC and the broader SAP ecosystem (BTP, SAP AI/Joule, SAP Fiori, MDG, SAP Integration Suite, OpenText, SAP DRC and others), translating business requirements into scalable and maintainable solutions.
Collaborate with ERP functional teams, solution architects and IT leaders to implement architecture principles, standards and patterns, promoting simplification and reducing unnecessary complexity.
S/4HANA Transformation
Support architecture activities within SAP S/4HANA transformation programs and strategic ERP initiatives, contributing to target-state designs and architecture decisions across functional and technical teams.
Advocate for SAP standard processes, Fit-to-Standard, Clean Core and extensibility principles, helping teams evaluate alternatives and minimize customizations where appropriate
Integration & Technical Architecture
Drive architecture decisions for SAP and non-SAP integration, including APIs, events, middleware and SAP Integration Suite, working with development and integration teams to deliver scalable and maintainable solutions.
Lead the review of technical options and solution designs, challenging assumptions, identifying dependencies, risks and trade-offs, and driving teams toward pragmatic technology decisions.
Architecture & Solution Guidance
Lead ERP architecture assessment within the Architecture Review Board (ARB), challenging new demands, projects and solution designs and driving clear architecture recommendations and decisions.
Guide and challenge functional and solution teams throughout the solution lifecycle, ensuring designs align with ERP architecture principles, standards, patterns and business outcomes.
Stakeholder & Architecture Capability
Build strong partnerships with ERP functional leaders, solution architects, Enterprise Architecture and technology teams, and represent ERP Architecture in relevant technology evaluations, RFPs and solution selections.
Drive selected architecture chapter initiatives and ways of working, developing reusable patterns and standards, sharing knowledge and mentoring architects and functional teams to strengthen architecture capability across Kraft Heinz TECH.
Recipe for Success: Apply if this sounds like you!
Essential Qualifications
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field.
5-8 years of experience in enterprise architecture, solution architecture, or senior technical design roles supporting complex enterprise platforms.
Strong hands-on experience with SAP ecosystems, including one or more of the following: SAP S/4HANA, SAP ECC, SAP BTP, SAP Integration Suite, SAP PI/PO, SAP Fiori, SAP MDG, SAP BW/4HANA, or related SAP backend technologies.
Strong understanding of backend enterprise capabilities, including integrations, APIs, middleware, event-driven architecture, master data, batch and real-time processing, and enterprise security considerations.
Experience guiding architecture across complex ERP landscapes that include SAP and non-SAP platforms.
Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and drive architecture decisions without direct authority.
Strong understanding of system scalability, resilience, security, supportability, and lifecycle management in enterprise backend environments.
Experience contributing to architecture standards, review processes, roadmaps, and reusable design patterns.
Strong communication skills, including the ability to present technical recommendations to both technical teams and senior non-technical stakeholders.
Nice to have
Exposure to SAP RISE/Cloud ERP architectures, FIORI and modern SAP development approaches.
SAP, TOGAF or other relevant architecture certifications.

Job Description:
Mars Snacking - Controls Technician - TNN
Area: 3
Hiring Manager: Scott Walther
Shift Schedule: Rotating night shift 2-2-3
Hours: 6:45 AM - 7:15 PM (Must be flexible pending business needs).
The Controls Technician will maintain, adjust, troubleshoot and repair electrical equipment such as motors, motor control circuits, power distribution systems up to 480 VAC, Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC's focusing on Rockwell and Siemens) and AC/DC drives. The incumbent must be capable of using electrical test equipment, meters, o-scopes, etc., and possess the skills required to troubleshoot to a component level.  Additional requirements include knowledge of robotics, automated processes, and photoelectric and ultrasonic sensors.  The incumbent must also be able to read wiring diagrams and schematics and understand the software associated with PLC's in order to troubleshoot issues.  In addition, the incumbent assists the Maintenance Mechanics when troubleshooting issues.
What are we looking for?
Minimum Qualifications :
Obtain line manager approval.
Meet the required time-in-role criteria
Maintain good standing status (See definition below).
High school diploma and minimum of three to five years' experience in a TPM/technical, manufacturing environment.
Preferred Qualifications :
A technical degree in Industrial Maintenance, Electrical/Controls or related engineering/technical fields.
Physical Requirements :
Perform the essential functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodation.
Frequent lifting/carrying (10–50 lbs) and pushing/pulling (50–300 lbs).
Frequent bending, stooping, twisting, handling, and gripping.
What will be your key responsibilities?
Responsible for the maintenance and troubleshooting of electrical and control systems equipment down to the component level, including 480V electrical power distribution, instrumentation, motor controls, VFD’s, Servo’s, I/O devices/modules, PLC’s, HMI’s, and control networks.
Troubleshoot machine breakdowns and malfunctions utilizing a working knowledge of control system programs and tools required to troubleshoot PLC’s, HMI’s, and VFD/servo systems including electrical schematics, programming software, meters, and other electrical test equipment.
Repair, replace and calibrate all electrical sensing devices, instrumentation including photoelectric, inductive, capacitive, pressure, temperature, weight, position sensors, flow, and analytical instruments.
Coordinate the electrical preventative maintenance program by identifying items that need regular inspection and replacement, scheduling the tasks and task frequencies required, and following up to ensure the completion and effectiveness of each task.
Manage all PLC, Servo and HMI programs and changes as well as electrical documentation.  Ensure that they are all accurate, updated, and available to the technicians and archived at regular intervals.
Other job duties as assigned by your Line Manager.

The opportunity to learn and develop, taking charge of your own career across Mars.
An industry-competitive salary and great benefits package.
The chance to work cross-functionally and add value and impact to the business.
If you are passionate, a great problem solver, resilient, and have a high drive for results, then we want to hear from you!

Job Description:
At MARS, we are committed to developing our people and celebrating success. Reporting to a Retail Sales Director, you will join a high-performing, collaborative team where leadership, teamwork, and strategic execution drive results.
As a Retail Sales Leader, your primary role will be to develop and lead a team of Retail Sales Associates and part-time merchandisers (where applicable) by establishing priorities and evaluating performance.   The expectation of the Retail Sales Leader is to provide continual coaching to direct, engage and motivate the Associate(s) to achieve their individual and team key performance indicators (KPI’s) while actively developing them for their next best role within Mars.
The Retail Sales Leader must have proven People leadership, analytical capabilities, and coaching skills to build and develop an effective and highly motivated field sales team. The role is responsible for translating company strategies into actionable plans for the region and directing the team in the use of data insights to achieve these plans while ensuring alignment with account strategy, business objectives, and selling priorities across your area of responsibility.
Key Responsibilities
Build and maintain long-term, trusted relationships with customers by demonstrating strong consultative selling skills to drive sales, retailer profit, ROI, and market share.
Create value by delivering customized sales presentation(s) based on retailer opportunities and priorities to sell incremental orders and mutually beneficial in-store solutions.
Monitor and analyze performance metrics to identify and execute solutions to achieve territory and region KPIs, retailer category growth, and account/company business targets.
Leverage data and demonstrate a strong priority setting to deliver channel/retailer specific seasonal and limited time offer to sell through targets.
Serve as a primary point of contact for customers, ensuring clear communication of sales priorities, orders, and promotional plans.
Position yourself to be a trusted expert, asking open-ended questions and tailoring solutions to specific needs.
Influence merchandising and operational resources to ensure instore excellence, compliance with execution standards, and timely implementation of sales initiatives.  These include assortment priorities (core and innovation), shelving objectives and planogram integrity, as well as incremental semi-permanent and temporary displays.
Responsible and trusted use of technology is essential, including accurate data entry, analysis of sales data to build a selling story, and effective utilization of company systems to support decision-making and performance tracking.
May have Compression call responsibilities. Comfortable preparing and selling to Market Managers, District Mangers depending on customer base of your territory.
Direct 3rd party providers (where applicable) for in-store execution (including seasonal surge).
Where applicable, sell throughout the year by providing business updates to the store's decision maker and contracts which will support delivery of the distribution, shelving, and display objectives.  Enforce compliance.
Maintain high on shelf availability by working with KDM to address inventory discrepancies and order fulfillment.
Participate in team conference calls, training, and attend all sales meetings.
Responsible for storage facility and managing product rotation, inventory allocation, supplies, etc., in an efficient and effective way.
Job Specifications/Qualifications
This role is an individual contributor.
This role interfaces with customers at store level
This role has a reasonable impact on sales organizations and a reasonable impact on the company.
Education & Professional Qualification:
Bachelor’s Degree
Knowledge/Experience
Minimum Qualifications:
A bachelor’s degree, or HS Diploma and equivalent work experience
Demonstrated proficiency with intermediate technology tools, including mobile devices and basic business applications.
Strong analytical, problem solving, and negotiation skills.
Excellent interpersonal, communication, and relationship building capabilities.
Ability to lift and carry up to 40lbs
Able to sit, stand and/or drive for long periods of time, as well as frequently bend, kneel and stoop
Ability to walk for a minimum of 6 ½ hours per day
Demonstrate ability to work remotely
Subject to outside weather conditions and changing climates
Must live within territory boundaries
Ability to travel overnight if required
Work scheduled may include early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays based on business needs.
Role requires daily travel to multiple customer locations and a valid driver’s license with a clean driving record.
Preferred Qualifications:
A bachelor’s degree and significant experience in field sales and territory management
2+ years with at least one year of selling experience
Proven ability to influence customers through professional selling skills and data driven insights.
Experience using technology to analyze performance, manage accounts, and support sales execution.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Work, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Power Bi.
Prior Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) and/or retail sales experience
Prior selling experience in convenience, grocery or Walmart channels.
What can you expect from Mars?
Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by the Five Principles.
Join a purpose driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.
A strong focus on learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house Mars University.
An industry competitive salary and benefits package, including company bonus.

Our mission is to help every organization own its intelligence: Artificial Intelligence (AI) that knows, reasons, and works the way the organization does. We capture how an enterprise works, including its knowledge, sensemaking, workflows, tools, and expert judgment, in reinforcement learning environments (RLEs). Tasks are long-horizon and open-ended, quality is judged against expert rubrics rather than a single correct answer, knowledge is spread across documents, conversations, slides, and drawings, and every organization works differently. We have shown that reinforcement fine-tuning in well-constructed enterprise environments lets smaller tuned models outperform the latest frontier models on such tasks, at lower cost. We work side by side with customers, product teams, and partners so that new methods reach real users quickly, and the gaps we find in the field shape our next research questions.

Overview
Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment.
We are seeking Research Interns to make long-horizon Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents both  more capable  and  more secure . Agents increasingly act autonomously over long horizons and have access to tools, files, networks, and credentials. Two problems limit how far they can be trusted: they fail in ways that aggregate benchmark scores hide, and they can be manipulated by adversarial inputs. This Research Internship offers two research directions, with Research Interns focusing on one based on their expertise and interests:
Failure-driven self-improvement:  improve long-horizon agents by diagnosing failure modes in their trajectories and synthesizing targeted post-training data that closes specific capability gaps.
Agent security:  develop technologies that make existing agentic systems more secure, including sandboxing, agent permissions, and defenses against novel agent attacks.
Research Interns will contribute to one thrust, depending on their background. Expected outcomes include research prototypes, evaluation of pipelines, and publications at top-tier venues.
Responsibilities
Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer.
Additional Responsibilities
Project 1 — Self-Improving AI Agents
Develop and evaluate a research agent that uses post-training experiments to iteratively improve a target model through synthetic data.
Task decomposition and capability diagnosis.  Develop methods for the agent to infer the capabilities required by a target task and use evaluation results to identify which capability gaps limit the model’s performance.
Capability-targeted data synthesis.  Build methods that translate hypotheses about capability gaps into training data, with control over skill coverage, example difficulty, and data quality.
Closed loop optimization.  Build a self-improvement loop that measures the effects of each round of synthetic data. Use these results to let the agent revise its capability hypotheses and adapt its data generation strategy across rounds.
Project 2 — Secure AI Agents
Develop and evaluate security mechanisms for existing AI agent systems.
Sandboxing.  Isolate agent execution and control access to files, networks, and credentials.
Agent permissions.  Develop least-privilege authorization, task-scoped permissions, and approval mechanisms for sensitive actions.
Agent attacks and defenses.  Study prompt injection, malicious tool outputs, memory poisoning, and cross-agent attacks in controlled environments. Prototype defenses in an existing agent framework and evaluate their security effectiveness, impact on task performance, and usability.
Across both projects, Research Interns will collaborate with researchers to communicate findings to technical audiences and pursue publication at top-tier venues
Qualifications
Required Qualifications
Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in computer science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, or a related field.
Other Requirements
Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship.
In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter.
Preferred Qualifications
Demonstrated Python programming skills and hands-on experience with PyTorch or a similar machine learning (ML) framework.
Publications at top-tier ML conferences such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, or related venues.
Highly self-driven, with the ability to work independently and collaborate effectively in a fast-moving research environment.
Background in one or more systems of security, sandboxing, access control, or Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents.
Demonstrated mathematical foundations and modeling ability.
Demonstrated hands-on software engineering skills, demonstrated by independently building tools, small systems, or software projects from scratch. Open-source contributions are a plus.
High-level awards or equivalent achievements in competitive programming, mathematics, or algorithmic competitions such as ICPC.
Interest in security research and ability to design experiments, analyze results, and communicate findings.

Robotics, quantum computing, and adjacent emerging technologies are markets still taking shape. You will lead the team's strategy efforts and strategic analysis: shaping our point of view on robotics and quantum markets, which partnerships Microsoft pursues and why, and which promising themes become concrete initiatives that can be tested, scaled, or stopped. You will work side by side with BD deal leads, providing strategic support and analysis on live partnerships, while deal leads remain accountable for negotiation and execution.
This role sits adjacent to a classic BD profile. The center of gravity shifts to strategy formulation, analytical rigor, problem solving, and finding clarity in complexity. Coordinates with external stakeholders including third-party warehouses, Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) vendors, and suppliers as necessary to facilitate inbound and outbound deliveries. Conducts follow-ups on items logged within Intelligence Communication Manager (iCM), validating issues, and deals with the escalated issues. Supports creating more efficient receiving routes, moving manual communication and information sharing to automated processes, where possible.

Plans, forecasts, and develops strategies for space optimization, including decommissioning and retention, driving identification of opportunities to improve inventory to address space constraints and ensuring deprecated materials are not stagnant. Prioritizes ticketing queues, works to resolve escalations, and clears blocking issues to enable continued delivery of Inventory and Asset Management (IAM) activities.

Seeks out opportunities to contribute to workstreams and toward greater simplification and automation, improving results of Service Level Agreements (SLAs) against Objective Key Results (OKRs). Conducts root cause analysis and identifies training gaps for potential escalations. Facilitates and pilots environmental sustainability and zero waste initiatives. Completes required security and data management training and complies with security and data management procedures/policies. Conducts training for relevant site-specific procedures and tools (e.g., forklift, pallet jacks, technician on-hand processes, inventory maintenance software, RMA portals, Rack Movement).
Procurement Creates execution plans with the goal to improve satisfaction and performance within an area or organization-level group. Identifies and resolves delivery and execution road blocks, serving as point of contact for arising issues and unblocking critical paths to continue business continuity. Learns different elements of different suppliers, including what parts to order and what supplier(s) to engage with. Gathers data related to POs and provides to direct management. Assists senior leadership with escalated procurement issues. Performs quality control for purchase order and escalations with vendors. Audits on-site supplies and deployment consumables.

Manages and coordinates any escalated task risks and reported issues, establishing safety standard operating procedures for new equipment (e.g., server rack tugs, electric pallet jacks, forklifts). Trains employees on safe and effective equipment and inventory moving. Ensures team and 3rd party vendors are in compliance with Microsoft Corporation safety standards Procures, audits, and reviews personal protective equipment (PPE), leading by example of all safety standards. Presents Identity and Access Management (IAM) metrics to senior leaders. Oversees handling and storage of hazardous materials and chemicals, developing plans to address unsafe materials out of containment and ensuring preparedness of others, and acting as a point of escalation.

Working 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.

Follows all Service Level Agreements (SLAs) related to RMA and non-RMA warranty process.

title: Senior Security Operations Engineer
description:
Overview
Team overview
Every cloud depends on a small set of foundational services that almost everything else trusts. Together they form the cloud's Trusted Computing Base (TCB): the services where a small gap can have an outsized blast radius across the cloud and the customers who depend on it.
These are Microsoft's crown jewels, and protecting them is urgent: sophisticated attackers target exactly these kinds of services, and AI is making it faster to find and exploit weaknesses. Securing them is always top of mind for senior leadership, it comes first when we prioritize risk reduction, and the controls we prove here set the paved path for production services across the company.
The TCB Core Security Engineering team in IAM Protect, part of Microsoft's CISO organization, leads this work. We take a data-driven, attack-path view of risk, modeling the trust relationships between services to understand blast radius and focus our effort where it reduces the most risk. We are a technically deep security that operates horizontally across Microsoft. Our strategy is simple to state and hard to do: isolate these services from the rest of the cloud, minimize what has to be trusted, and defend what remains with layered controls.
Role overview
We are looking for a Senior Security Operations Engineer who pairs a deep understanding of how cloud services and platforms are actually constructed with the security instincts to see where they can be broken. You will identify new risks to our crown jewel services, model them with our attack-path and risk data, develop the policies and security controls that close them, and partner with leaders and service owners across Microsoft to drive those controls to adoption until the exposure is measurably gone. Every attack path you shut down is one no attacker can use against Microsoft's cloud or its customers.
Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.
Responsibilities
•    Identify and analyze risk across our most critical cloud services. Look for unintended trust and access paths into them, such as excessive privilege, credential exposure and unnecessary access between services, and turn findings into clear, prioritized risk statements.
•    Model risk with data. Work with service owners and architects to understand how their services are built, represent trust relationships accurately, and use attack-path analysis to quantify blast radius and decide which paths to remove first.
•    Develop security policies and controls that are enforceable by default rather than dependent on reviews, such as isolation boundaries, least privilege and hardening standards, each with a clear scope, safe rollout, exception handling and validation telemetry.
•    Drive risk burn-down to closure. Lead campaigns with service owners and engineering leaders across Microsoft, set targets, track progress with data, unblock teams, manage exceptions with discipline and report measurable risk reduction to senior leadership.
•    Leverage AI to automate workflows, improve efficiency, and streamline your work.
•    Govern and defend the boundary around these services. Define and run the mechanisms that keep the set of critical services small and well isolated, and partner with detection, incident response and eviction teams so we can assume breach and still contain an attacker quickly.
•    Turn incidents and red team findings into durable protection by converting the lessons into risk models, policies and controls, so the same path cannot be used twice.
•    Scale your impact with data and automation: build KQL queries, datasets, dashboards and AI-assisted tooling that make risk discovery, prioritization and campaign tracking faster.
•    Produce crisp technical artifacts, including risk write-ups, control specifications, troubleshooting guides and leadership updates that unblock execution.

Doctorate in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field OR Master's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 3+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large-scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, anomaly detection, Security Operations Center (SOC) detection, threat analytics, security incident and event management (SIEM), information technology (IT), or operations incident response OR Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 4+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large-scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, anomaly detection, Security Operations Center (SOC) detection, threat analytics, security incident and event management (SIEM), information technology (IT), or operations incident response OR equivalent experience. About the Role

We’re looking for a Brand Data Infrastructure Lead to own the data foundations that make brand marketing measurable and scalable. You will define how brand media, campaign, creative, audience, and research data are organized, connected, validated, and made available for decisions. This hands-on role combines brand and media expertise with practical data fluency, turning fragmented platform and partner outputs into dependable datasets and repeatable workflows.

This role sits within Growth Marketing and works closely with Brand Marketing, Media Operations, Growth Platform’s solutions engineering team, Data Engineering, and Data Science. You own Brand’s data roadmap, business definitions, source requirements, data-quality acceptance, and adoption. Engineering partners own production architecture, connector and pipeline implementation, instrumentation, and technical incident resolution. Data Science owns statistical methodology and model development.

Your first priority is to establish consistent campaign and creative taxonomies, dependable media and measurement feeds, clear data-sharing arrangements, and trusted reporting inputs. Build a foundation that supports TV/CTV, online video, social, audio, out-of-home, and other brand channels, with the coverage and history needed for brand tracking, lift studies, incrementally, and marketing mix modeling.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the Brand data infrastructure roadmap. Translate brand strategy, media plans, and measurement needs into prioritized data capabilities, source integrations, quality improvements, and reporting foundations. We do this with transparency for the overall OpenAI credential framework and providing trusted, role-based certifications that verify practical capability.

About the Role

As a Certification Assessment Specialist, you will design, build, test, launch, and maintain the hands-on assessments behind an OpenAI technical role-based certification. Your work will help candidates demonstrate what they can do in realistic scenarios and give reviewers reliable evidence to score their work.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role reporting to the Technical Certification Lead. You will turn competency models, assessment blueprints and scoring rubrics into working tasks, assessment environments and workflows that capture candidate evidence and produce results reviewers can verify. You will use scripting and automation and partner with engineering on software development and delivery integrations.

You will work with the certification, measurement, engineering and operations teams, as well as technical subject matter experts and external delivery providers. The Technical Certification Lead will coordinate alignment with learning content while keeping confidential assessment details separate from learning materials.

You will take assessments from prototype through pilot, launch, and ongoing maintenance across live and virtual delivery. As products and tools change, you will update tasks, environments, and scoring together so candidates are assessed against the intended skills.

Success means candidates have the opportunity to demonstrate the competencies required for the certification, and reviewers can consistently score that work using evidence they can trace back to the submission.

In this role, you will:

 - Translate assessment blueprints into realistic scenarios, candidate instructions, and hands-on tasks. Work with subject matter experts to check that the tasks reflect the job and elicit the appropriate evidence for each rubric.

 - Define assessment environment requirements and build or configure the environments candidates will use. Establish repeatable provisioning and reset workflows for accounts, tools, data, and permissions so candidates start from consistent conditions.

 - Build and maintain pipelines that capture candidate submissions and other scoring evidence, apply scoring rules, and route results for review. Make scores traceable to the underlying evidence and protect sensitive data under approved controls.

 - Build and test model-assisted scoring with qualified human reviewers using established validation criteria. Compare model scores with calibrated expert judgments, investigate disagreements, implement agreed rules for routing cases to human review, and rerun validation tests after material changes to the model, task, or rubric.

 - Test assessments end to end, from environment setup to evidence capture and scoring. Use dry runs and pilots to check instructions, timing, accessibility, and failure recovery; fix defects and verify the fixes before release. Test scoring against multiple valid approaches, partial and incorrect submissions, and failures in the assessment environment, so a platform issue isn’t mistaken for a candidate error.

 - Translate assessment needs into requirements for delivery integrations. Partner with engineering and delivery providers to test candidate access, submission and results handoffs and troubleshoot issues.

 - Prepare assessments for launch with platform and operations partners. Document setup, version dependencies, and troubleshooting so delivery teams can run assessments consistently and respond when something breaks.

 - Maintain versioned tasks, environments, scoring configurations, and test fixtures. Use candidate feedback and delivery and scoring data to identify issues, update or retire tasks, and check that changes preserve the intended skills and difficulty.

 - Investigate technical issues raised during delivery or candidate review. Reproduce defects where possible, document what was affected, and test fixes with the relevant delivery partners.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have personally designed and built performance-based, hands-on assessments, labs or simulations for technical roles, such as software developers or solution architects, and taken them through testing, launch and maintenance. Experience creating question-and-answer tests alone does not meet this requirement.

 - Have used scripting and automation to build and troubleshoot technical assessment environments. You can work with technical subject matter experts to translate realistic solutions into assessments; deep AI-engineering expertise or prior experience with a particular language or delivery platform is not required.

 - Have experience working at a technology company in a fast-paced environment, setting priorities and delivering work amid changing requirements and evolving business needs.

 - Can use a blueprint and rubric to design realistic tasks and specify what evidence distinguishes competent performance from task completion.

 - Have built or maintained workflows that capture submissions, process evidence, and produce traceable scores or reviewer outputs.

 - Have implemented or validated model-assisted scoring or evaluation against expert human judgments, and can explain when a score should go to human review.

 - Have worked directly with external technical experts or delivery providers and can translate requirements into integrations you can test end to end.

 - Have used pilot results, candidate feedback, and scoring or delivery data to improve assessment quality.

 - Understand how to build for accessibility and protect candidate evidence and confidential assessment content.

 - Communicate technical tradeoffs clearly to subject matter experts, measurement specialists, platform engineers, and operations teams.

It’s a plus if you have experience:

title: Data Scientist, Integrity
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Integrity team protects people and businesses using ChatGPT, Codex, and the API from fraud, abuse, and harmful misuse. Our work spans payment and promotional abuse, compromised accounts and API credentials, business and advertiser integrity, and emerging misuse of frontier AI capabilities. We also help product teams measure authentic usage so that abuse doesn’t distort decisions about how our products are growing.

Integrity Data Science helps teams decide where to intervene and whether those interventions work. A payment control can prevent fraud while blocking legitimate purchases. A product launch can make it easier for customers to get started while creating new opportunities for abuse. We measure both sides of those decisions.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Data Scientist on Integrity, you’ll find emerging abuse patterns, size their impact, and lead the analytical work behind decisions about detection, enforcement, and product launches. You’ll work with Product, Engineering, Research, Policy, and Operations to turn findings into improvements and measure what happens after they ship.

 - Investigate anomalous activity across products. Estimate how common a problem is, who is affected, and what it costs users or the business. Use that evidence to recommend where to focus.

 - Define outcome metrics and guardrails, establish baselines, and build monitoring that surfaces changes in abuse, customer friction, and operational performance.

 - Help build and evaluate detection rules, classifiers, and human review workflows. Use labeled samples and review outcomes to understand what the systems miss, where they flag legitimate activity, and how those errors vary across users and products.

title: Geotechnical Engineer, Data Center Development
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Industrial Compute team is developing data center infrastructure to support increasingly demanding AI workloads. The team brings together site development, civil and structural engineering, utilities, construction, commissioning, and operations to move campuses from early evaluation through delivery.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Geotechnical Engineer to help evaluate, plan, and deliver data center campuses. You’ll translate subsurface conditions into practical recommendations for site selection, campus design, construction, and long-term reliability. The work spans early due diligence through design review and field execution, with a focus on identifying ground-related risks early and helping teams make informed decisions.

Key Responsibilities 

 - Develop, update, and maintain geotechnical and geoenvironmental scopes of work, Owner’s Project Requirements (OPRs), technical specifications, and engineering standards for site due diligence and design phases, ensuring consistency across data center and power infrastructure projects while supporting risk mitigation, cost optimization, and accelerated project deliver

 - Plan and review geotechnical investigations, including borings, in-situ testing, laboratory testing, and groundwater monitoring.

 - Evaluate subsurface conditions and develop recommendations for foundations, settlement, seismic design, earthwork, subgrades, pavements, retaining systems, slopes, and groundwater management.

 - Assess geotechnical risks during site selection and due diligence, including variable ground conditions, liquefaction, expansive or compressible soils, karst, settlement, and constructability constraints.

 - Review geotechnical reports, calculations, drawings, specifications, and consultant deliverables for technical quality and consistency with project requirements.

 - Partner with civil, structural, architectural, utilities, and construction teams to integrate geotechnical recommendations into campus plans and building designs.

 - Support permitting and agency coordination by providing clear technical documentation and responding to review comments.

 - Provide construction-phase support, including review of submittals and field conditions, evaluation of differing site conditions, and recommendations for corrective actions.

 - Help establish consistent geotechnical standards, investigation scopes, design criteria, and risk documentation across projects and sites.

 - Communicate ground-related risks, assumptions, and tradeoffs clearly to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

 - Review construction documents for foundation systems, earthwork, and ground improvement solutions for data center buildings, equipment yards, and power generation plants to ensure compliance with owner requirements, applicable codes, and project-specific geotechnical recommendations.

Qualifications

 - A degree in civil engineering, geological engineering, geotechnical engineering, or a related discipline.

 - Professional experience in geotechnical engineering for large, complex infrastructure, industrial, mission-critical, or campus-scale projects.

 - Strong technical judgment across subsurface investigation, foundation recommendations, earthwork, settlement, groundwater, and seismic considerations.

 - Experience reviewing consultant work and translating findings into actionable design and construction recommendations.

 - Familiarity with geotechnical analysis methods and common engineering tools used for foundation, slope, settlement, and earthwork evaluation.

 - The ability to work effectively with consultants, contractors, designers, and project teams while maintaining clear ownership of technical decisions.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain uncertainty and risk.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience supporting data centers, power generation, advanced manufacturing, or other critical infrastructure.

 - Experience with large campus developments, phased construction, and multiple building or utility packages.

 - Familiarity with local permitting, building-code, and geotechnical design requirements across different jurisdictions.

 - Professional Engineer license, or ability to obtain licensure where required.

 - Experience developing repeatable technical standards or reviewing work across a portfolio of sites.

title: Manufacturing Quality Engineer, Data Center Modular Builds
description:
About the Team

OpenAI and its capital and technology partners are building a global network of data centers for demanding AI workloads. The Infrastructure Quality team sets and verifies quality, reliability, and performance requirements for equipment across that network.

We work with manufacturing partners, general contractors, engineers, and operations staff from supplier qualification through commissioning. Together, we verify that equipment arrives ready for installation, startup, and long-term service.

About the Role

As a Manufacturing Quality Engineer for Data Center Modular Builds, you will own supplier manufacturing and integration quality for modular systems, including hot aisle containment (HAC), modular cooling units (MCUs), and electrical skids. Working with mechanical and electrical integrators and their suppliers, you will lead supplier qualification, support product and process development, and translate engineering requirements into manufacturing controls, inspections, and acceptance criteria.

You will partner with cross-functional teams to monitor production and integration quality, conduct audits, and resolve risks to integrated products acceptance and delivery. You will also serve as the primary quality contact for site escalations involving manufacturing or integration defects in modular systems and(OFCI) components. Through structured root-cause investigations, corrective action, and closed-loop learning (CLL), you will drive resolution and feed field lessons back into supplier processes to prevent recurrence and improve future builds.

Key responsibilities

Modular Systems Quality and Supplier Development

 - Lead supplier qualification and support product and process development for mechanical and electrical integrators.

 - Oversee manufacturing and integration quality for modular builds, including HACs, MCUs, and electrical skids.

 - Work with integrators and suppliers to translate engineering requirements and critical-to-quality (CTQ) characteristics into practical manufacturing controls, inspection points, and acceptance criteria.

 - Develop and drive supplier improvement plans (SIPs) using the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) approach to strengthen manufacturing and integration processes.

 - Use production data, audit findings, test results, and supplier scorecards to identify systemic or recurring issues, prioritize improvements, and measure sustained results.

Site Escalations and Corrective Action

 - Serve as the primary quality point of contact for escalated site issues attributable to manufacturing and integration failures, coordinating containment and resolution with site teams and supplier factories.

 - Lead root-cause and corrective-action (RCCA) investigations using structured methods such as 8D and 5 Whys. Verify root causes, track corrective and preventive actions to closure, and confirm their effectiveness.

 - Apply closed-loop learning (CLL) to incorporate field findings and lessons learned into supplier and integrator manufacturing controls and future builds, preventing recurrence.

Manufacturing and Integration Monitoring

 - Partner with Quality Program and Manufacturing Operations teams to monitor production and integration progress, quality controls, inspection results, and factory test readiness. Identify emerging risks and coordinate timely action with suppliers.

 - Conduct product and process audits during and after manufacturing and integration to verify compliance with engineering requirements, approved procedures, and quality standards. Document findings and track corrective actions to closure.

 - Align production checkpoints, inspections, and factory testing requirements with suppliers, engineering, sourcing, supply chain, commissioning, and quality teams. Coordinate deviation resolution and escalate risks to equipment acceptance or delivery.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, or industrial engineering.

 - At least 10 years of data center industry experience spanning quality engineering and manufacturing engineering.

 - Experience working with integrators and suppliers across multiple tiers to manage quality throughout the product lifecycle, from OFCI component manufacturing through integration and site issue resolution, and drive product and process improvements.

 - Ability to define CTQs and acceptance criteria, develop inspection and test checklists, review test results, and maintain auditable quality records.

 - Experience monitoring supplier production, conducting product and process audits, managing controlled documents and deviations, and using supplier scorecards to drive improvement.

 - Demonstrated experience leading root-cause investigations and corrective actions for manufacturing or field issues using structured methods such as 8D and 5 Whys, and driving continuous improvement through PDCA.

 - Ability to coordinate supplier schedules and plan inspections and tests across multiple equipment programs.

 - Ability to communicate quality requirements, resolve issues, and coordinate decisions across suppliers, engineering, commissioning, sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, operations, and construction teams.

 - Willingness and ability to travel approximately 40% of the time to supplier manufacturing facilities and data center project sites.

Preferred Skills

 - Technical knowledge of data center infrastructure, including mechanical, electrical, and controls systems.

 - Experience in supplier performance management for mission-critical facilities.

 - ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, Quality Manager, or Quality Auditor.

 - Experience in industrial or high-volume manufacturing environments.
