title: Protection Scientist Engineer, Integrity
description:
About the Team

The Integrity team is responsible for the scaled systems that help identify and respond to bad actors and harm on OpenAI’s platforms. We protect users and the wider world by developing responses to complex harms and building the harm protections needed for new product and model launches. Integrity’s work spans not only across frontier harms like biological weapons and cybersecurity, but also high severity abuses such as child safety, nation-state misuse, and violence.

About the Role

Protection Scientists within Integrity design, orchestrate, and mature systems of defence against usage harms enabled by OpenAI's products. We are systems thinkers that combine deep harm domain expertise with breadth across investigation, data science, machine learning, policy and operations. Our distinctive strength is understanding how these disciplines fit together and translating between them to design and build effective systems of defence.

In San Francisco, we are hiring for protection work focused on sextortion, trafficking, national security (including nation-state misuse), and jailbreaks. Depending on your domain expertise, your work could include identifying AI-enabled coercion and exploitation, detecting misuse that supports trafficking, uncovering coordinated activity by state-linked actors, or investigating attempts to circumvent model safeguards. You will translate these evolving threats into detection systems and interventions that reduce harm.

Your core hands-on technical responsibility is harm detection. You will design, build, evaluate and maintain production detection systems, drawing on investigative expertise, data and shared engineering platforms. You will develop signals and classifiers that identify abusive behaviour and patterns across accounts and activity, and adapt them as adversaries change tactics.

You will also own the strategy and cross-functional delivery of protection work for a harm area or product launch. Working closely with investigators and other domain experts, you will ground the design in a deep understanding of how the harm occurs and translate that understanding into a system of defence. You will connect detection with policy, review, interventions, enforcement and measurement, continually calibrating the system against real cases and expert judgement as it scales.

You will identify what needs to be built or changed and make it happen. Success requires setting clear priorities, aligning partners, resolving dependencies and communicating evidence, decisions and trade-offs crisply. It also requires a willingness to jump in and work directly on whatever is blocking system effectiveness, using your breadth of skills.

This role is based in our San Francisco office and includes participation in an on-call rotation that may involve resolving urgent escalations outside normal working hours. Some investigations may involve sensitive content, including sexual, violent or otherwise disturbing material.

In this role, you will:

 - Define and drive protection strategy for a harm area or launch. Translate ambiguous risks into goals, priorities and roadmaps, and make trade-offs based on evidence, risk and available capacity.

 - Directly build and maintain harm detection. Develop production signals, classifiers and pipelines using SQL, Python, machine learning and language models, integrating with shared engineering platforms.

 - Lead cross-functional execution. Translate between specialist roles, establish shared understanding and ownership, resolve technical and organisational dependencies, and communicate recommendations and specific asks clearly.

 - Investigate exploitation and national security threats within your area of focus. Work with domain experts to understand actor behaviour, recognise patterns of coercion, exploitation or coordinated misuse, and turn case findings into detection criteria.

 - Connect detection to effective action. Partner with Policy and Operations to develop review and escalation protocols, distinguish abusive activity from legitimate use, and improve interventions as new cases reveal gaps.

 - Evaluate and improve the complete system of defence. Measure remaining harm, detection quality and intervention effectiveness and collaborate with Data Science on more sophisticated metrics. Use expert feedback and operational outcomes to guide improvements.

 - Protect product and model launches. Define data, detection and review requirements; establish monitoring; investigate gaps and critical escalations; and drive improvements informed by post-launch findings.

 - Scale effective approaches with language models, agents and reusable tools. Choose where automation and human judgement are needed, and build documentation and processes that improve reliability and help others extend the work.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Think in systems. You have enough breadth across technical, analytical, investigative and operational disciplines to understand how they fit together, recognise gaps and translate between specialist perspectives.

 - Bring deep expertise in at least one of sextortion, trafficking, national security, jailbreaks or a closely related harm domain. Relevant backgrounds may include trust and safety investigations, counter-exploitation, threat intelligence, investigations of state-linked actors, or adversarial testing of AI safeguards. You do not need expertise across all of these areas.

 - Have experience investigating adversarial behaviour and translating incomplete, evolving evidence into actionable signals. You can connect individual cases to broader patterns while being explicit about uncertainty and the risk of misidentifying legitimate activity.

 - Are proficient in SQL and Python and have experience writing reliable and efficient production code for detection and data processing. Additional ML or SWE experience is a plus.

 - Can apply quantitative analysis and machine-learning methods to measure risks and evaluate system effectiveness. You understand the limitations of your data and can reason about missed harms, false positives and appropriate interventions. Additional DS/measurement background is a plus.

 - Have experience setting strategy and delivering complex, cross-functional technical projects. You can turn an ambiguous problem into a plan, align people with different priorities and drive work through to completion.

 - Communicate clearly and concisely in writing and conversation. You can explain technical findings, make actionable recommendations and surface uncertainty and trade-offs to different audiences.

This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who can connect operating system internals, hardware-backed security, and real-world product constraints. description:
About the Team

Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption.

Within Customer Education, the Certification team helps individuals demonstrate competence for in-demand AI skills and helps customers and partners validate that their workforce has the skills they need to meet their AI-enabled business goals. Our work centers on the belief that learners should understand where to go to build skills and capabilities, how to demonstrate them, and what to pursue next. Similarly, Enterprise leaders should understand what each credential signifies and how it supports workforce readiness. We do this with transparency for the overall OpenAI credential framework and providing trusted, role-based certifications that verify practical capability.

About the Role

As Technical Certification Lead, you will lead the design, development, and ongoing quality of OpenAI’s technical role-based certifications. Your work will make clear what each certification validates and what candidates must demonstrate to earn it.

This is a hands-on people manager role on the Certification team. You will manage the Certification Assessment Specialists building technical assessments across the certification portfolio, setting priorities, coaching team members, and holding the team accountable for quality and delivery. You will personally turn shared certification frameworks into certification-specific competency models, job-task analyses, assessment blueprints, scoring rubrics, and passing criteria.

You will apply program-wide certification standards to individual technical certifications and partner with operations and platform teams to prepare assessments for delivery. You will align learning content to competency models and blueprints while keeping confidential assessment content separate from learning development.

You will take certifications from role analysis through pilot, launch readiness, and ongoing maintenance. As AI tools and technical roles evolve, you will keep the assessments relevant to the work people actually do.

Success means each certification makes a clear claim about what someone can do, the assessment supports that claim, and the curriculum gives candidates a practical way to build the skills they need.

 - Build and maintain competency models and facilitate job-task analyses for technical roles. Work with practitioners and subject matter experts (SMEs) to identify critical tasks, define the skills and proficiency each role requires, and keep the models current.

 - Validate AI-assisted scoring against judgments from calibrated human reviewers. Define when scores require human review, and revalidate scoring after material changes to the model, assessment task, or rubric.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have led the development and maintenance of role-based technical certifications or other high-stakes technical assessments, from role analysis through pilot, launch, and post-launch improvement.

Develop and validate signal processing and machine learning algorithms that enable new core sensing capabilities in future Oura products.
Own exploratory research, design experiments to address key scientific and technical uncertainties, and build proof-of-concept capabilities to establish which sensing concepts are worth advancing.
Design and support internal and external data collection studies to develop, benchmark, and validate new biomarkers and algorithms.

Document and present scientific findings and algorithm performance to technical and nontechnical audiences, with actionable recommendations that guide research priorities and product decisions.

A PhD with 3+ years of relevant work experience, or an MSc with 5+ years, in biomedical engineering, computer science, electrical engineering, neural engineering, or a related field.

Hands-on experience with wearable hardware, including prototypes, in one or more modalities such as electrical, optical, or inertial sensing. Relevant experience may include PPG, motion sensing, or electrophysiology.

Proficiency using AI tools to accelerate research, coding, and data analysis, with sound judgment in evaluating their outputs and validating results.

Knowledge of human physiology and its relationship to wearable sensing signals.

description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary As an Adventure Readiness Specialist, you are a critical part of the Rivian Service team during our peak seasonal periods, helping us provide seamless care that keeps owners focused on their adventure and their Rivians ready for the journey ahead. During our seasonal surges in delivery and service demand, you’ll be on the front lines, helping our team navigate the high-volume peaks and ensure every owner’s journey continues uninterrupted. Cycle Counters are accountable for quality, safety, productivity, and adherence to current standardized work. You may be placed in any of our Normal, IL locations besides the plant. Responsibilities Perform scheduled and unscheduled cycle counts, recounts, urgent verifications, and inventory audits across assigned facilities and production areas. Remain on feet and walk continuously between inventory bins, production lines, warehouse zones, and assigned locations throughout the whole workday. Identify, document, and promptly escalate discrepancies, material-flow issues, damaged or mislabeled inventory, and unsafe conditions to Team Leads and Inventory Control Analysts. Coordinate with Material Handling, Production, Quality, and other partners to verify material movements and resolve inventory issues without bypassing required controls. Support SOX-related count procedures, internal/external audit selections, inventory investigations, obsolescence reviews, and special projects as assigned. Maintain 5S standards and required PPE; participate in daily startup meetings, training, and continuous improvement activities. We believe high-level autonomy won’t just enhance the drive; it’ll give our customers their time back and transform the utility of their vehicles—a paradigm shift that will drive purchase decisions at scale. As a Staff Product Manager on the Autonomy team, you’ll own the vision, strategy, and execution for scaling our L2 and L2++ hands-free driving features beyond their initial launch, shaping experiences that deliver unparalleled freedom and convenience. You’ll also extend this work to robotaxi, in areas such as driving behavior and remote assistance. This high-visibility role requires empathetic leadership and exceptional communication skills to influence and engage diverse teams across engineering, senior leadership, business strategy, and marketing. Shape product requirements for robotaxi remote assistance, partnering with Engineering, Safety, and Operations through driverless launch. MBA is a plus. 7+ years of Product Management experience in automated driving, driver assistance, or robotics, including shipping L2/L2++ features in production vehicles; or a mix of 3-4 years in engineering and 3-4 years in product management in these fields. Experience translating customer needs into user journeys, scenarios, and intuitive experiences for autonomous driving or robotics products, making pragmatic trade-offs within engineering constraints. Track record of scaling automated driving features after launch (1 to 1.x), as well as launching 0-to-1 features in nascent markets. Familiarity with global regulatory frameworks. Strong analytical, communication, and leadership skills. Bonus Qualifications Strong understanding of the automated driving stack. Experience on L4/robotaxi programs, especially remote assistance or teleoperations. Experience working with high-volume telematics data to extract insights into feature use, edge-case frequency, and intervention patterns. title: Staff Service Engineer, Body Structures
description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary The Collision Repair Service Engineer is responsible for defining collision repairability and service strategies for all body sheet metal components from the earliest stages of new vehicle development through launch and 3rd level field support. This role represents the voice of the collision repair technician, customer, insurer, and certified repair facility in vehicle design decisions, helping Rivian deliver vehicles that are safe, insurable, repairable, and economically viable to restore after a collision. The engineer will leverage RCAR principles, collision repair industry practices, organizational feedback, and service engineering expertise to influence design concepts before key architecture and component decisions are finalized. The role will simplify repair strategies for complex vehicle structures, establish repair-versus-replace recommendations, create service part numbers and if necessary drawings for service unique subassemblies, and own the service bill of materials to enable sourcing for our NPI stakeholders. This position partners closely with Vehicle Engineering, Design, Service NPI, Manufacturing, Quality, Purchasing, Supply Chain, Technical Publications, Collision R&D, Service Operations, Insurance, and certified collision repair facilities in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment. Responsibilities Lead collision repairability assessments for exterior systems and components beginning in concept, architecture, and advanced development phases and continuing through production launch. Evaluate repairability and replacement strategies for body sheet metal, including closures, fenders, quarter panels, body sides, bumper reinforcements, underbody exterior panels, and related structural or cosmetic assemblies. Translate collision repair requirements into clear design inputs, serviceability targets, and trade-off recommendations for Engineering and Design teams. Establish repair-versus-replace strategies that consider technician safety, repair quality, vehicle performance, customer experience, cycle time, parts availability and total repair cost. Apply RCAR standards and principles, along with recognized collision repair practices, to drive service-focused design concepts and improve vehicle insurability. Represent the voice of the technician and customer in design reviews, architecture decisions, development milestone reviews, prototype evaluations, and production readiness activities. Identify complex vehicle structure systems that may create repair challenges and develop simplified, repeatable, and clearly documented repair paths. Define permissible repair methods, limitations, sectioning or replacement boundaries, attachment strategies, joining requirements, corrosion protection, sealing, refinishing, and post-repair verification needs. Assess the impact of mixed materials, adhesives, rivets, welds, fasteners, composites, castings, high-strength steels, aluminum, and other joining or material technologies on collision repair. With the support of engineering define required tools, fixtures, equipment, and consumables for certified collision repair facilities. Participate in hands-on and virtual prototype, pilot, and validation repairs to confirm that proposed repair strategies can be executed safely, consistently, and efficiently in the field. Create and maintain service part numbers for collision-related components, subassemblies, kits, hardware, consumables, and repair-specific parts in the appropriate product lifecycle and service systems. Own the collision repair service bill of materials for new product introduction, ensuring accurate structure, applicability, service intent, supersession logic, interchangeability, and release status. Ensure service BOMs remain aligned with the latest production design, engineering changes, supplier changes, and approved repair strategies through disciplined change management. Define service assembly content and replacement packages where a repair is not technically, economically, or operationally appropriate at the individual component level. Partner with Technical Publications to convert engineering decisions into collision repair procedures, illustrations, labor-impact inputs, parts recommendations, training content, and technical communications. Develop repairability and insurability metrics, track progress through development, and escalate risks that could affect repair cost, repair cycle time, parts availability, facility capability, or customer satisfaction. Lead issue resolution for collision repair concerns using structured problem solving, root-cause analysis, and closed-loop corrective actions. Gather and analyze feedback from technicians, certified repair facilities, insurers, estimators, adjusters, and customers to identify opportunities for design, service content, parts, or process improvement. Coordinate field returns, repair observations, and part analysis to validate assumptions and improve future product designs. Support launch readiness, service introduction, repair network readiness, and field actions related to collision repairability and service parts. Build and maintain standards, playbooks, checklists, and design review tools that institutionalize prediction, prevention, and protection across vehicle programs. Drive change management activities by evaluating service impact, repair strategy, part interchangeability, documentation updates, and disposition of affected service content. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Automotive Technology, a related engineering/technical degree, or equivalent hands-on industry experience. Technical collision repair training, I-CAR training, OEM certification, ASE certification, or equivalent industry credentials are valued. Training or demonstrated proficiency in CAD, PLM, BOM management, technical documentation, or engineering change control is preferred. 8+ years of experience in collision repair, automotive service engineering, body repair, vehicle body structures, repair facility operations, estimating, insurance claims, or a closely related field. Demonstrated hands-on knowledge of collision repair processes for exterior body and trim components. Strong understanding of repair-versus-replace decision-making and the factors that influence vehicle insurability, repair cost, cycle time, safety, and customer experience. Experience interpreting engineering drawings, CAD data, service procedures, parts catalogs, or repair manuals. Experience working with part numbering, bills of material, engineering change management, or product lifecycle management systems. Ability to evaluate repair concepts for feasibility in a certified collision repair facility, including technician access, sequence of operations, tooling, equipment, and facility constraints. Knowledge of automotive materials and joining methods, including steel, aluminum, plastics, composites, adhesives, rivets, welds, and mechanical fasteners. Ability to identify risks in complex vehicle structures and communicate clear, actionable recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Strong written, verbal, and visual communication skills, with the ability to influence design decisions across a cross-functional organization. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple programs, deliverables, and priorities across development phases and locations. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, especially when requirements are incomplete, ambiguous, or technically complex. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Collision repair technician, structural repair, or OEM service engineering experience. Experience applying RCAR standards, procedures, research, or repairability principles. Experience with vehicle exterior systems, body structures, closures, plastics, lighting, glazing, or trim. title: Assembler
description:
At S&C Electric Company, a 100% employee-owned company, we help keep the lights on for people and businesses worldwide. Our manufacturing roles build the equipment that protects the critical infrastructure of the power grid, and each of our team members lends their unique skills to this crucial mission. We empower our people by providing pathways to a long-term career and support them in their professional growth by sustaining a culture founded on respect, strengthened by collaboration, and measured by our shared successes. The manufacturing industry is booming with opportunities to learn new things, expand your skills, and build a long-term career.
Join S&C to make an impact on tomorrow’s energy challenges and become an employee-owner!
Hours :
4:30 pm- 1:00 am (Mon-Fri)
Occasional Overtime on Saturdays
Compensation:
At S&C, we are dedicated to providing competitive and equitable compensation for all our team members, with a commitment to transparency in our pay practices. The estimated hourly base pay rate for this position is $20.25 per hou r. This role is also eligible for S&C’s annual short-term incentive bonus, subject to eligibility criteria.
Join Our Team as an Assembler!
Are you passionate about assembly? S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to join our Vista & Vista SD Assembly team. As an Assembler, you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team. In this job, you will assemble VISTA units and corresponding subassemblies. You will work in a production environment, engage in continuous productive activity, and must meet requirements within time constraints. This is an assembly line operation involving as many as six stations. Initially you will be assigned to one station but will need to be flexible and open to working additional stations as business needs require. Tasks require a high degree of eye-hand coordination, manual dexterity, and the use of both hands and arms on a repetitive basis for a full range of motion. You will frequently use hand and power tools; occasionally work while standing on ladders; and occasionally work inside tight compartments.
Key Responsibilities:
Assemble VISTA Switch, both on the assembly line and directly on the shop floor.

title: Contract and Billing Specialist - USA
description:

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

About the role:
Samsara's Customer Success team is on the front lines of business value delivery by helping customers adopt our platform, realize measurable business value, and renew and expand with confidence. Billing errors, concession requests, and cancellation or return exceptions currently land with CSMs, CS managers, and several partner teams, each holding part of the picture. As our customer base and billing complexity have grown, these cases take too long, repeat for the same reasons, and pull CSMs away from adoption and renewal work. As the Contract and Billing Resolution Specialist, you will be the single owner of complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts.
You will take a customer's report that something is wrong with their bill, work out what happened across systems and teams, choose the right path to fix it, and see it through, keeping the customer informed. It is part detective, part project manager, part customer advocate. You will also tell the teams who own the underlying systems and processes what keeps breaking.
Your role will be cross-functional, working alongside and connecting Customer Success Managers, Sales, Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal. This is a new role, and you will help shape the case record, the root-cause tags, and the monthly read-out that define how Customer Success resolves billing and contract cases at Samsara.
This is a remote  position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.
In this role, you will:
Own complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts, from the first report to a confirmed fix, and keep the customer informed in plain terms, including accounts that are delinquent or facing suspension.
Reconstruct the full story behind a billing error across contracts, order forms, segment or ownership changes, reprocessing, and invoicing, including cases with several AE handoffs and no clean record of what was promised.
Separate a correction of a Samsara error from a concession, a return, a reprocess, and a contract amendment, and choose the path that fixes the customer's billing, not only the immediate complaint.
Drive Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal to execute the fix.
Evaluate and prepare concession requests: confirm whether Samsara was at fault, size the request against policy and the approval matrix, write a short case summary (what happened, root cause, options considered and ruled out, recommendation, and risk), route it to the right approver, and confirm the credit is applied and the customer told.
Support cancellation, return, and ETF exceptions: validate eligibility (purchase and renewal dates, trial history, Return ACV, financing partner, documentation), prepare the case for the approving team, act as the Customer Success fallback when the first approver does not respond within the window, and make sure approved outcomes are processed.
Be the front door for billing, concession, and cancellation requests: log every request in a single case record, including those that arrive via Slack, email, or Gainsight; redirect them to the right path; and coach CSMs and AEs on what a complete request looks like.
Fix repeat causes: tag the root cause on every case, separate one-offs from systemic failures, and deliver a monthly read-out to the teams that own the systems and processes involved.
Carry forward the billing improvement work with Support, Finance, and Product, including earlier detection of billing problems that threaten renewals.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's operating principles, including Keep a High Bar, Be Intellectually Honest, and Solve Problems Together, as we scale.
Minimum requirements for the role:
4+ years of experience in billing operations, order to cash, revenue operations, deal desk, contracts, or a similar finance and operations role.
This is a demanding position with high internal visibility that requires strong priority management and high emotional intelligence.
Strong investigative skills: you can rebuild a timeline from incomplete or conflicting information across CRM, billing, and contract systems, including when the people involved have left.
Sound financial judgment about credits, concessions, reprocessing, and refunds, and a clear way of explaining your recommendation.
Customer-facing communication that stays honest and composed in hard conversations, and written summaries a leader can read once and decide on.
A record of driving results across teams without authority over them, including working to deadlines in an approval process.
Familiarity with order forms, amendments, and terms, and how they flow into billing.
Comfort with ambiguity and incomplete precedent, and rigorous case management so nothing drops across weeks and stakeholders.
Diplomacy, tact, and poise under pressure when working through customer issues.
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience handling escalated or high-dollar billing disputes.
Experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, or an equivalent ERP, and CPQ tools. We also use Zendesk, Gainsight, and Sweethawk.
Customer Success, Support, or account management background with customer-facing financial or contract work.
Experience building or improving billing dispute processes.
Exposure to subscription or hardware-plus-subscription billing.
AI First: Experience using AI tooling to drive efficiency and outcomes.
Strong bias for action and insistence on high standards

About the role:
As an Adoption Specialist on our Mid-Market team, you are the technical expert our customers and our Account Managers call when a high-value feature needs to go from "purchased" to "running in the operation." You work on a project-scoped basis: each engagement has a defined goal, a timeline, and clear commitments from both Samsara and the customer. Think of the structure of a solutions architect team, delivered as part of the Samsara relationship rather than as a paid service.
You pair deep product and technical knowledge with project management discipline. You dig into a customer's use case, understand how their industry and operating procedures shape the way they use Samsara, and design a practical path to adoption. You translate highly technical concepts into plain language for non-technical audiences, and you hold customers accountable to the milestones that make a project succeed.
You are also a force multiplier for the broader Customer Success organization. Through research, documentation, and coaching, you help Account Managers learn new products and level up their product knowledge, and you work cross-functionally with Support, Product, and Engineering to solve problems and bring customer insight back to the teams building Samsara. Account Managers continue to own the customer relationship and the renewal; you own the project and the adoption outcome.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world : Your efforts will result in real-world impact, helping to keep the lights on, get food into stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You have an innate curiosity about how businesses work : One day you'll be learning how a waste management company dispatches its routes and the next you may be digging into the inner workings of a food distribution center. You want to understand customer operating procedures well enough to shape our products around them.
You thrive the most when solving technical problems : You enjoy diagnosing why something isn't working, researching workarounds, and building a solution that fits a customer's real-world workflow.
You deliver to a deadline : You run projects with clear plans, owners, and dates, and you are comfortable having direct conversations when a customer or internal partner falls behind.
You are a natural teacher : You can take a complex product concept and make it clear for a fleet manager, a safety lead, or an executive, and you enjoy helping teammates build their own expertise.
You are the architect of your own career : This is a new role on a team that is still shaping its future. You will have plenty of autonomy and opportunity to define how the role works and master your craft in a hyper-growth environment.
You want to be with the best : At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.

Be a deep Subject Matter Expert on the Samsara product, API, integrations and AI capabilities.
Lead project-scoped adoption engagements with Mid-Market customers, from scoping and kickoff through delivery, to increase adoption of Samsara's technical features and drive measurable customer outcomes.
Hold customers accountable to agreed-upon commitments, and escalate early and constructively when a project is at risk.
Complete deep research into customer use cases, current workflows, and workarounds, and recommend practical, well-supported solutions.
Develop a working understanding of the industries we serve and how Samsara's products are tailored to each industry and each company's operating procedures.
Support the broader team in learning new products and upleveling product knowledge through training, documentation, and hands-on enablement.
Work cross-functionally with Support, Product, and Engineering to troubleshoot complex issues, and share customer insights that inform the product roadmap.
Capture what you learn in reusable playbooks, templates, and best practices so the team can scale the impact of each project.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.
Minimum requirements for the role:
3 to 5+ years of experience in a customer-facing technical role such as implementation, solutions engineering, technical customer success, or professional services, ideally in SaaS, IoT, technology, or logistics.
Bachelor's degree from a 4-year institution, or equivalent practical experience.
Strong technical aptitude, with a track record of quickly learning complex products and troubleshooting issues independently.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects and deliver to deadlines, with clear planning and follow-through.
Proven track record of communicating technical concepts clearly and empathetically to non-technical audiences, from day-to-day users to executives.
Solutions-oriented with strong research and problem-solving skills.
Strong communication, presentation, and organizational skills.
Familiarity with Salesforce, Gainsight, Gong or similar GTM tools.
Comfort with a rapidly changing, high-growth environment.
An ideal candidate also has:
Strong bias towards action , has the ability to think big, with insistence on high standards.
AI First : Experience using AI tooling to drive efficiency and outcomes.
API and Integration Experience : Experience building with APIs, and/or working with and building integrations.
Project Management Experience : Experience running scoped, project-based customer engagements.
Technical Proficiency : Experience with building deep knowledge of a suite of technical products (bonus points if familiar with integrating hardware with software solutions).
Industry Knowledge : Experience with routing, navigation, commercial trucking fleets, and logistics.

Drive adoption by coaching sellers and partnering with Sales Enablement and Product Marketing, and measure the business impact of what you ship.
Set clear, measurable goals for adoption, productivity and business impact, instrument the product to track them, and use the results to decide what to build next.
Resolve cross-functional dependencies, such as aligning teams on shared datasets with Data Engineering or getting Product Marketing content into the AI knowledge base, and take on the analytics and operational work needed to make the product succeed.

Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team of product managers.

10+ years of experience in product management, or in strategy and operations roles where you owned a product built with engineering.
5+ years of experience leading, developing and mentoring product managers or product-oriented teams, while staying close to execution.

Hands-on experience with AI, such as building or shipping AI-enabled products, using AI tools in your own work, or prototyping with them.
Strong analytical skills, with examples of using data to identify problems, shape product decisions and measure results.
Technical fluency and ability to establish credibility with engineers.
Strong problem-solving and structured thinking, with a record of driving work to completion across teams and stakeholders.
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience owning internal tools or AI products used by sales, customer success or other go-to-market teams.
Familiarity with the systems and data that run a go-to-market organization, such as CRM, forecasting and sales enablement tools.
Experience defining quality, evaluation and trust standards for AI products.
Experience coaching end users and working with enablement teams to get a new tool used.
Experience leading product teams that use AI throughout their own work, from research and requirements to prototyping and launch.
Comfort with fast-changing priorities and with the cross-functional alignment that a company at Samsara's scale requires.

title: Manufacturing Quality Inspector
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.


About the role

Robots only work if every part is exactly what it claims to be — and you're the one who makes sure of it. You'll be the final word on mechanical quality in our QC lab, using GD&T to catch what others miss and confirming that the parts going into our robots match the drawings they came from. Get it right, and every arm we ship starts on solid ground.


What you'll do

- Inspect mechanical parts and assemblies in the QC lab using GD&T (ASME Y14.5), catching deviations before they turn into downstream problems.

- Program and run CMMs and other advanced measurement equipment to verify parts against spec.

- Lead First Article Inspections for mechanical parts at launch and after any process change.

- Run process audits on production mechanical operations so quality holds steady as we scale.

- Mentor Receiving Inspectors on mechanical inspection techniques and GD&T fundamentals.

- Keep inspection records and traceability tight and audit-ready for all mechanical work.

- Take a seat on the Material Review Board and help resolve mechanical nonconformances.

- Review mechanical drawings for inspectability, and flag GD&T issues to NPI and Engineering before they cause rework.

- Support our 6S and FOD programs to keep the QC lab clean, organized, and safe.


What you'll bring

- 5+ years of mechanical inspection experience in a QC lab environment.

- Strong working knowledge of GD&T per ASME Y14.5.

- Hands-on skill with measurement equipment — CMM preferred, plus height gauges, optical comparators, and surface plates.

- Sharp drawing interpretation skills.

- The patience and precision to work through complex measurements without cutting corners.


Nice to have

- CMM programming experience with PC-DMIS, Calypso, or similar software.

- Experience inspecting industrial robotics or precision mechanical assemblies.


Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $34-40/hour, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

description:
Crafting the world’s finest coffee, one meaningful moment at a time
We believe in creating a warm and welcoming space where every cup of coffee sparks connection.   As a coffeehouse leader, you don’t just run a business—you lead a team that creates moments of connection and joy.    Every day provides an opportunity to lead with craft and heart, making your coffeehouse a place where your community feels welcome.
We are invested in your growth journey, empowered through developmental experiences as well as our industry leading benefits .
We'd love to hear from people with:
3 years retail / customer service management experience or 4+ years of US Military service
Strong organizational, interpersonal and problem solving skills
Entrepreneurial mentality with experience in a sales focused environment
Strong leadership skills and the ability to coach and mentor team partners with professional maturity
Minimum High School or GED
Requirements:
Legal documentation establishing your identity and eligibility to be legally employed in the country in which you apply.
Ability to work full time (the work regularly demands in excess of 40 hours per week) including variable hours including early mornings, evenings, weekends and/ or holidays.
Let us give you the opportunity to grow as an individual, to build lasting relationships and make an impact in a place where people, quality and value mean everything.
Join us and connect with something bigger, apply today!
As a Starbucks partner, you (and your family) will have access to medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, and other voluntary insurance benefits. Partners have access to short-term and long-term disability, paid parental leave, family expansion reimbursement, paid vacation from date of hire*, sick time (accrued at 1 hour for every 25 hours worked), eight paid holidays, and two personal days per year. Starbucks also offers eligible partners participation in a 401(k) retirement plan with employer match, a discounted company stock program (S.I.P.), Starbucks equity program (Bean Stock), incentivized emergency savings, and financial well-being tools.  Additionally, Starbucks offers 100% upfront tuition coverage for a first-time bachelor’s degree through Arizona State University’s online program via the Starbucks College Achievement Plan, student loan management resources, and access to other educational opportunities.  You will also have access to backup care and DACA reimbursement.   Starbucks will comply with any applicable state and local laws regarding employee leave benefits, including, but not limited to providing time off pursuant to the Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act, and in accordance with its plans and policies. This list is subject to change depending on collective bargaining in locations where partners have a certified bargaining representative. For additional information regarding partner perks and more detailed information about benefits, go to starbucksbenefits.com .
*If you are working in CA, CO, IL, LA, ME, MA, NE, ND or RI, you will accrue vacation up to a maximum of 120 hours (190 in CA) for roles below director and 200 hours (316 in CA) for roles at director or above.  For roles in other states, you will be granted vacation time starting at 120 hours annually for roles below director and 200 hours annually for roles director and above.
The actual base pay offered to the successful candidate will be based on multiple factors, including but not limited to job-related knowledge/skills, experience, geographical location, and internal equity.  At Starbucks, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at the high end of the range for their role, and compensation decisions are dependent upon the facts and circumstances of each position and candidate.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. About Stripe

The Stripe Marketing organization is undergoing a fundamental transformation in how it works. We're building a team of Forward Deployed AI Accelerators (FDAs) embedded directly with marketing cohorts to make AI the default mode for all work — not an occasional tool, but the foundation of how every marketer at Stripe executes.
Today, marketers are already achieving remarkable results — building their own data dashboards, creating agents that compress multi-day processes, and authoring tools that accelerate workflows. The FDA team exists to take what's working and systematically scale it across the entire marketing organization.
What you'll do
As a Forward Deployed AI Accelerator, you'll be embedded with a cohort of 25–45 marketers organized by functional team, shared workflow, or location. You'll build alongside them, and you'll help them fundamentally change how they operate. Your measure of success is the number of workflows you've permanently transformed and the extent to which those in your cohort start any task with an AI tool.
Responsibilities
Identify and document the highest-leverage workflow transformations within your cohort's day-to-day work by deeply understanding their processes and outputs
Build custom tools, agents, automations, and skills tailored to each marketer's specific responsibilities
Coach and partner with each marketer through a progressive journey — from awareness, to first win, to regular AI integration, to full workflow transformation, to self-sufficiency
Teach marketers to build and iterate on their own tools over time, creating independence
Recognize patterns across your cohort and systematically scale what works — a tool built for one marketer will be reusable for their peers
Document every tool, playbook, and transformation pattern you build so the entire FDA team uses each other's work
Share wins visibly within your cohort and with leadership to build momentum, inspire, and celebrate success
Track individual and cohort progress rigorously against a defined maturity model, moving every marketer toward self-sustaining, AI-first work
Prepare marketers for an agentic future — not just prompt writing, but designing, building, and overseeing autonomous, multi-agent workflows
Who you are
We're looking for people who have already lived the transformation they'll be driving for others. You've used AI to fundamentally change how work gets done, not as a novelty, but as your default operating mode.
You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You don't just know what AI can do in theory. You've built things that changed how real teams operate, and the people you built for actually use what you shipped. You build in real time alongside the people you support.
You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new programs become viable that weren't worth doing before. Then you build the thing, not just the slide.
You understand marketing work. You either have direct experience in marketing or quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of your assigned cohort. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it.
You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions.
You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences, adapt your style to different people, and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders.
You are high-caliber, persistent, and versatile. Your skills and experience are valuable across the company. You're the kind of person who succeeds in many roles at Stripe.
You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next quarter.
You are comfortable with ambiguity and evolution. This is a new team building a new operating model. The playbook will be rewritten as we learn. You thrive in that environment.

5+ years of professional experience in a role requiring diagnostic thinking, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration
Demonstrated, hands-on experience building and deploying AI-powered agents, tools, automations, or workflows that real people use in their actual work, whether that made existing processes meaningfully more efficient or made previously unviable work possible for the first time
Proficiency with AI development tools and platforms (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, custom agent frameworks, API integrations, workflow automation tools)

Track record of coaching, teaching, or enabling others, with evidence that people you've helped actually changed how they work

Experience in a formal AI transformation role where the job was substantially about identifying opportunities for workflow transformation and executing on them with hands-on builds
Experience helping people become more expert AI users and capable builders
Experience in marketing, marketing operations, growth, or a closely adjacent function, including familiarity with marketing technology stacks (e.g., Marketo, Salesforce, analytics platforms, content management tools)

Own the security architecture. Threat-model the edge compute layer, provider integration surface, credential management system, billing pipeline, and analytics store. Make the architecture decisions — API key lifecycle, secrets rotation, data classification, auth enforcement — and partner with product and infra teams through implementation.
Secure the credential layer. Design and implement controls for API key issuance, rotation, revocation, and abuse detection across user-facing keys and upstream provider credentials spanning multiple secrets engines and cloud boundaries. This is the highest-risk surface on the platform and requires deep expertise in cryptographic credential management, OAuth/OIDC federation, and token-based access control.
Build detection and response. Instrument the platform for security events across edge, async processing, and database tiers. Build alerting, runbooks, and forensic tooling. Lead incident response when it matters. You own time-to-detect and time-to-contain, not just the playbook.
Integrate the platform into Stripe's security programs. Bring the platform into SecRev, vulnerability management, and incident response processes. Adapt controls designed for Stripe's primary infrastructure to fit an edge-first, multi-cloud architecture. You’re an engineer and a people leader who is comfortable representing the security posture to executive leadership . Software & security engineering depth. 10+ years in software engineering with deep expertise in at least two of: API security architecture, credential and secrets management, cloud security (IAM, network segmentation, encryption), or application security for high-throughput distributed systems.

The ability to secure high-throughput proxy, API gateway, or edge compute systems
Experience designing, operating, or security infrastructure on Google Cloud

title: Senior Staff AI Scientist / Engineer – Oncology Foundation Models & Agentic Platforms
location: Chicago; Boston; Redwood City; New York City
description:
Passionate about precision medicine and advancing the healthcare industry?
Recent advancements in underlying technology have finally made it possible for AI to impact clinical care in a meaningful way. Tempus' proprietary platform connects an entire ecosystem of real-world evidence to deliver real-time, actionable insights to physicians, providing critical information about the right treatments for the right patients, at the right time.
We are seeking an exceptional AI Scientist/Engineer to bridge two cutting-edge domains in medical AI: Oncology Foundation Models and Agentic Systems . In this role, you will design and train domain-specific foundation models on complex, multimodal cancer datasets (genomics, histopathology, longitudinal EHRs, and clinical imaging) while simultaneously building agentic workflows that orchestrate these models.
By integrating foundation models with agentic frameworks, you will help create intelligent clinical tools capable of dynamic reasoning, multi-step evidence synthesis, and complex decision support in oncology.
Core Responsibilities
1. Oncology Foundation Model Development
Design, train, and fine-tune large-scale multimodal foundation models specialized in oncology (e.g., integrating spatial transcriptomics, whole-slide images, and clinical histories).
Implement pre-training strategies tailored to bio-medical domains, including self-supervised learning (SSL), contrastive learning, and masked token prediction.
Evaluate model robustness, generalization, and domain shift across diverse patient cohorts, tumor types, and sequencing platforms.
2. Agentic Platform Engineering
Architect scalable agentic frameworks (e.g., tool-use, multi-agent communication, autonomous planning, and retrieval-augmented generation) tailored for clinical workflows.
Design safety guards, reasoning trace verification, and human-in-the-loop interventions for AI agents operating in high-stakes medical settings.
Integrate agentic systems with external biological knowledge bases, literature databases (PubMed, clinical trials), and EHR interfaces.
3. Connecting Models & Agents (The Synergy)
Expose specialized oncology foundation models as core tools/capabilities within the agentic platform, enabling agents to dynamically invoke multi-omic analysis tools.
Develop agent-driven workflows that use foundation models to summarize complex patient trajectories, propose biomarker-driven treatment hypotheses, or query trial eligibility.
Optimize end-to-end latency, reasoning chains, and output interpretability for clinical and scientific research end-users.

Review field redlines and ensure electrical, instrumentation, and automation drawings are accurately updated to as-built condition.

Develop and coordinate commissioning plans, loop checks, point-to-point checks, energization activities, functional tests, FAT/SAT activities, and startup support.
Validate CygNet configuration, communications, point-to-point mapping, alarm setpoints, shutdown setpoints, trends, and required operating displays for changes made to the facility during the project.

Experience with Allen Bradley PLC programming, RSLogix 5000, Studio 5000
